# AURA â€” Adaptive Unified Responsive Assistant

A local, working-prototype personal assistant built on Google's
[Live API web console](https://github.com/google-gemini/live-api-web-console).

- **Assistant**: real-time voice conversations with Gemini Live, plus typed messages in the same session.
  It can search the web (Google Search grounding) for news and other current information and shows its sources.
- **Memory**: AURA learns durable facts from your conversations, stores them in SQLite on your computer,
  and recalls them in later sessions (even after a restart). You can inspect, edit, restore and delete them.
- **Meeting Mode**: records a room through your microphone and produces a timestamped transcript with
  speaker labels. People with a registered voice profile appear by name; everyone else becomes
  Speaker 1, Speaker 2, â€¦ You can rename speakers, move or merge lines, fix text, and export.

Everything except the Gemini API calls runs on your machine.

## Requirements

- **Node.js 22.13 or newer** (Node 24 LTS recommended). AURA uses Node's built-in SQLite module, so
  nothing native has to be compiled.
- A Gemini API key from <https://aistudio.google.com/apikey>.
- Chrome or Edge (microphone access requires `localhost` or HTTPS).
- About 70 MB of disk for the local models, downloaded automatically on first start.

## Setup and start

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env        # Windows: copy .env.example .env
# open .env and paste your key after GEMINI_API_KEY=
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` starts the local server on port 3001 and the web app on <http://localhost:3000>.
The first start downloads three small models from the Hugging Face hub into `data/models`
(memory search, voiceprints, speaker-change detection). The Meeting page shows a notice while that is happening.

Single-port alternative: `npm run build` once, then `npm run serve` and open <http://localhost:3001>.

## Desktop app (Windows)

The same app also runs as a Windows desktop app. Electron starts the local server with its own
built-in Node and shows AURA in a window, so `src/` and `server/` are unchanged.

```bash
npm install
npm run desktop      # builds the web app, then opens AURA in a desktop window
npm run dist:win     # builds an installer: dist-desktop/AURA Setup <version>.exe
```

- **API key**: on first start AURA asks for your Gemini key and stores it encrypted with your Windows
  account (`%APPDATA%\AURA\desktop-settings.json`). Change it from the **AURA** menu. When you run
  `npm run desktop` from the project, a key in `.env` also works. `.env` is never put in the installer.
- **Your data**: the installed app keeps its data in `%APPDATA%\AURA\data`. Running `npm run desktop` from the
  project keeps using the project's `data/` folder. To take your existing memories, conversations and voice
  profiles into the installed app, quit AURA and copy the project's `data` folder over `%APPDATA%\AURA\data`.
  Set `AURA_DATA_DIR` to use another folder.
- **Microphone**: Windows must allow desktop apps to use the microphone
  (Settings â†’ Privacy & security â†’ Microphone â†’ "Let desktop apps access your microphone").
- The server listens on 127.0.0.1 port 3017 (another free port if that one is taken). It stops when you
  close AURA, and also if the app crashes or is ended from Task Manager. Its log is at
  `%APPDATA%\AURA\logs\server.log` (AURA menu â†’ Open server log).
- Closing the window quits AURA; there is no tray icon or background mode yet.

## How it works

```
browser (React, existing CRA stack)               local server (server/, plain Node)
 â”œâ”€ Gemini Live websocket  â—„â”€â”€ ephemeral token â”€â”€  POST /api/live/token   (API key stays here)
 â”œâ”€ conversation + memory UI  â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ REST â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â–º   SQLite: data/aura.db
 â””â”€ Meeting Mode: mic â†’ VAD segments â”€ PCM â”€â”€â”€â”€â–º   speaker embedding (local) â†’ Gemini transcription
```

### Assistant (`src/hooks/use-live-api.ts`, `src/lib/genai-live-client.ts`)

- Reuses the console's Gemini Live client, audio recorder, audio streamer and worklets.
- The browser never sees the API key: the server issues a single-use
  [ephemeral token](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/ephemeral-tokens) for each session.
- Input and output audio transcription are enabled, so spoken turns appear as text and are saved.
  If your English is written down in Hindi script, set Settings â†’ Assistant â†’ "Language you speak" to English
  (or English and Hindi). It only changes the transcript; some Live models may ignore it, and if one rejects it
  AURA reconnects with automatic detection and says so.
- Dropped sessions show a **Reconnect** button that resumes the same context (session resumption);
  server `goAway` notices reconnect automatically. Microphone and API errors are shown in plain words.
- Default Live model: `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` (change it in Settings, e.g. to
  `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest`).
- **Web search**: the session is given Gemini's built-in Google Search tool, so questions about news,
  scores, prices or anything recent are answered from the web. Answers that used search show the
  search terms and numbered source links; the sources are saved with the conversation. Turn it off in
  Settings ("Let AURA search the web"). Search runs inside Gemini; nothing else is called.

### Documents (`server/documents.mjs`, `server/doc-text.mjs`)

Use the paperclip in the message box (or drop files into the chat) to add documents to the current
conversation: PDF, Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), Excel (.xlsx), CSV/text/Markdown/code and images
(PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC). Old .doc/.ppt/.xls files have to be saved in the new format first.

- Files are stored in `data/documents/` and deleted with the conversation (or with "Delete everything").
- PDFs and images are sent to Gemini as they are, so scanned pages and photos of text work (limit 14 MB).
  Word, PowerPoint and Excel text is extracted locally, with no extra dependencies (limit 30 MB; only
  the first ~300,000 characters are used).
- When a document is added, Gemini (the text model) writes a short overview, key points and three
  suggested questions, shown on a card in the chat. In a running voice session AURA also says in a
  sentence or two what it is.
- Questions go through the assistant's `ask_document` tool: the text model answers from the document
  only, says when the answer isn't there, and gives short quotes with page or section.
- Cost: one request when a document is added and one per question, from the text model's daily quota
  (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`: 500/day on the free tier). Every question re-sends the document, so very
  large documents use a lot of tokens.



- **Extraction**: a few seconds after each reply (and when a session ends), new messages are sent to
  Gemini (`GEMINI_TEXT_MODEL`, default `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, chosen for its larger free daily quota) together with the related existing
  memories. The model returns `add` / `update` / `retire` / `forget` operations.
- **Conflicts**: an `update` never overwrites. The old fact is kept with status *superseded* and a
  link to its replacement; `retire` marks a fact *outdated*. Only *active* facts are given to the
  assistant, each with its "last confirmed" date. The model can only change memories it was shown.
- **Retrieval**: sentence embeddings from a local model (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` via transformers.js)
  plus keyword overlap. The 30 most recent active facts are placed in the Live system prompt; the
  assistant can search the rest through a `recall_memories` tool, and typed messages get the closest
  matches attached. If the embedding model can't load, search falls back to keywords.
- **Asking before changes**: new facts are saved automatically, but when AURA wants to change, mark
  outdated or delete a memory you already have, it asks first (a card in the Assistant view and on the
  Memory page, with a badge in the sidebar). You can accept, edit the wording first, or keep the old
  fact; a change you turned down isn't proposed again. Turn this off in Settings.
- **Conversations** are stored and listed in the sidebar (pinned ones first). Open one to read it,
  **continue it** (the assistant gets the earlier messages as context), rename it (click the title),
  pin it, export it as Markdown, text or JSON, or delete it.

### Meeting Mode (`src/lib/segmenter.ts`, `server/meetings.mjs`)

1. The browser records 16 kHz audio and cuts it into pieces at pauses (energy-based voice
   activity detection; â‰¥0.7 s silence, max 10 s per piece).
2. **Speaker changes inside a piece** are found with a local speaker-segmentation model
   (`onnx-community/pyannote-segmentation-3.0`), so two people talking back to back become two lines.
   Very short turns (< 0.6 s) are folded into their neighbour.
3. Each turn gets a **voiceprint** from a local model (`onnx-community/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM`,
   the embedding model behind pyannote 3.x).
4. The voiceprint is compared with the voices already heard in this meeting (default similarity
   â‰¥ 0.55) and with registered voice profiles (â‰¥ 0.58, and clearly ahead of the next profile).
   Otherwise it becomes a new *Speaker N*. Numbers are never reused within a meeting. An unnamed
   speaker who later turns out to match a profile gets that name.
5. Turns are **transcribed by Gemini**, in one of two ways (Settings â†’ Meeting Mode â†’ Transcription):
   - **Live** (default): the browser keeps a Live API session open with `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live`
     and sends each speaker turn as its own utterance. On the free tier this model has no daily request
     cap. If it fails, the rest of the meeting switches to Standard automatically, and turns the
     browser never reported back are transcribed by the server.
   - **Standard**: turns are collected for a few seconds and sent several at a time to
     `GEMINI_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL` (default `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`), together with the last few transcript
     lines as context. An optional language hint (Settings, e.g. "English and Hindi") helps with mixed-language
   meetings. 429/5xx responses are retried; failed or empty pieces keep their audio and can be retried.
6. **After the meeting ends**, every line is checked again against the final voiceprint of each
   speaker: unnamed speakers that are really one person are merged, and lines that clearly belong to
   someone else are moved. Lines you moved by hand and speakers you renamed are never changed.
7. Corrections: click a speaker chip to rename it everywhere, use the merge icon when one person was
   split in two (their future lines follow the merge), change a single line's speaker from its
   dropdown, double-click text to fix it. Export as text, Markdown or JSON.
8. **Memory from meetings** (`server/meeting-notes.mjs`): once the speaker check is done, durable facts
   from the transcript (plans, decisions, people, dates) go into long-term memory, linked to the meeting.
   It follows the same rules as conversations (changes to existing memories wait for your OK). Turn it
   off in Settings; the meeting page has "Add to memory" / "Check again" to run it by hand.
9. **Minutes of meeting**: "Write minutes" on a finished meeting asks Gemini (the text model) for a
   summary, key points, decisions, action items (owner and due date only when clear from the
   transcript) and open questions. They are stored with the meeting, included in exports, and an
   automatic "Meeting <date>" title is replaced by the topic. One request per click.
10. **Asking about meetings**: the assistant knows today's date and has two tools, `find_meetings`
    (date range and/or topic) and `get_meeting` (minutes, memories and transcript of one meeting). So
    "what meetings did I have last Wednesday?" or "what did we decide about the budget on the 13th?"
    work in voice and typed chat. Long transcripts are shortened (start and end kept) before being
    sent to the model.

Voice profiles (Meeting Mode â†’ Voice profiles) require ticking a consent box and reading a short
passage for at least 12 seconds. Record them with the microphone and room you use for meetings.
Only the numeric voiceprint is stored, not the recording. "Test recognition" shows the similarity to
every profile for a fresh sample, which helps tune the thresholds in Settings. Profiles made with an
older speaker model are marked and must be re-recorded (voiceprints from different models can't be
compared).

### Proactive nudges (optional, off by default)

AURA can bring things up on its own. Each type has its own switch in `.env`; with none set, nothing is
created, scheduled or shown and AURA works exactly as before. Restart the server after changing them.

| Switch | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `AURA_PROACTIVE_MEMORY=1` | Once a day at most, asks "Is this still true?" about an older fact that tends to change (work, people, plans, where you live). **Yes** marks it confirmed, **Changed** replaces it (recorded through the normal change-proposal path, then applied because you typed it), **Forget** deletes it. |
| `AURA_PROACTIVE_REMINDERS=1` | Ask by voice or text ("remind meâ€¦", "set a reminderâ€¦", "set an alarmâ€¦"). In voice chat AURA uses a `set_reminder` tool, reads back the exact day and time, and sets it only after you say yes. A **Set reminder** card with the resolved date also appears in the inbox, and dated action items in meeting minutes become suggestions too. When it is due, the reminder shows in the inbox and is read aloud: by AURA in its own voice during a voice session, otherwise by the browser's built-in speech (a voice installed on your computer when there is one). The speaker button in the inbox turns this off. The AURA tab must be open, and the browser only lets a page speak after you have clicked in it once. With this switch off, voice AURA is told it can't set reminders, so it won't promise to. |
| `AURA_PROACTIVE_BRIEFING=1` | **Brief me** in the inbox: up to 5 lines from upcoming reminders, recent memory changes, open memory reviews and the last meeting's action items (one Gemini call; none when there is nothing to say). Add `AURA_BRIEFING_TIME=08:30` to get one automatically once a day. |

Nudges appear in a small inbox at the bottom right with Accept / Later (snooze) / Dismiss. Limits for
all types: `AURA_NUDGE_MAX_PER_DAY` (3), `AURA_NUDGE_COOLDOWN_MIN` after a dismissal (120),
`AURA_QUIET_HOURS` (22:00-08:00, or `off`), `AURA_MEMORY_CHECKS_PER_DAY` (1, max 2),
`AURA_MEMORY_CHECK_AFTER_DAYS` (30; half that for facts learned from meetings), `AURA_TIMEZONE`
(default: the computer's). During a voice conversation only reminder cards appear; nothing appears while a
meeting is recording. Reminders that fall in quiet hours or over the daily limit wait until they are allowed.
Saying no to a reminder doesn't start the cooldown. Outcomes per
type: `GET /api/proactive/stats`. Dates are parsed with chrono-node in your time zone.

## Your data

All data lives in `data/` (git-ignored): `aura.db` (conversations, memories, meetings, voice
profiles) and `models/` (downloaded model files). Delete items individually in the app, or use
Settings â†’ Your data to delete conversations, memories, transcripts or everything.

## Tests

```bash
npm run test:server   # API, memory conflict handling, speaker attribution, corrections, export
npm run test:desktop  # desktop shell: starting, stopping and restarting the local server
npm test -- --watchAll=false   # frontend unit tests (voice-activity segmenter)
```

The server tests replace Gemini and the two local models with fakes, so they check AURA's own logic,
not model quality.

## Known limitations (honest status)

- **Speaker recognition accuracy has not been measured on real meetings.** The models and thresholds
  were checked only on synthetic voices with added room noise and echo: there, the same voice scored
  0.61â€“0.96 and different voices âˆ’0.02â€“0.56, and a 12-line test meeting with two registered and two
  unregistered voices (including two people talking back to back) was attributed correctly. Real
  rooms will do worse. Expect mistakes with similar voices, people far from the microphone,
  short interjections (under 1 s they are attached to the previous speaker and marked *unsure*) and
  overlapping speech (overlaps go to whoever was already talking). Lines near a threshold are marked
  *unsure*; correct them in the transcript.
- One laptop microphone in a room is the hardest case for any speaker recognition. Recording voice
  profiles in the same room and on the same microphone helps the most.
- Transcription quality and speed depend on the Gemini model and your API quota. Standard
  transcription uses the daily request quota of the text model; Live transcription doesn't, but a Live
  session lasts at most 10 minutes and is reopened automatically.
- Web search on the free tier: Google's quota table lists Search grounding for Gemini 3 models at 0
  requests/day on free keys. If answers that need the web fail or come back without sources, switch the
  Live model in Settings to `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` (Gemini 2.5 grounding quota).
- Memory extraction depends on Gemini's judgment; review the Memory page and correct anything wrong.
  Facts learned from meetings rely on speaker names from voice recognition, which can be wrong.
- Minutes, memory-from-meetings and the meeting lookup tools were tested with a fake Gemini only; the
  quality of real minutes and whether the Live model calls the meeting tools reliably are unverified.
- Only one microphone user at a time: starting a meeting ends the current voice session.
- Documents: tested with a fake Gemini; answer quality on real files is unverified. Excel dates may appear
  as serial numbers, charts and embedded images in Office files are not read, and password-protected
  files can't be opened.
- Single local user, no accounts. The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only.

## Project layout

```
server/            local API (node:http + node:sqlite), Gemini calls, local models
  index.mjs        routes          memory.mjs    extraction / conflicts / search
  meetings.mjs     diarization, transcription worker, export
  meeting-notes.mjs  minutes, memory from meetings, date/topic lookup for the assistant
  documents.mjs    documents in conversations   doc-text.mjs  text from Office and text files
  models.mjs       transformers.js embeddings   gemini.mjs   tokens, JSON + transcription calls
desktop/           Windows app (Electron): main.cjs window + menu + key prompt,
                   server-process.cjs starts/stops the server, server-entry.mjs its entry point
src/
  hooks/use-live-api.ts      Live session, transcripts, persistence, recall tool
  lib/genai-live-client.ts   Live websocket client (from the console, token-based)
  lib/segmenter.ts           voice-activity segmentation for Meeting Mode
  views/                     Assistant, Memory, Meeting, Voice profiles
  components/                Sidebar, Settings drawer, Orb, ConfirmButton
```

FILE: desktop/key-preload.cjs
================================================
// Gives the API-key window two calls into the main process, and nothing else.
"use strict";

const { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } = require("electron");

contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("auraKey", {
  save: (key) => ipcRenderer.send("aura-key:save", String(key || "")),
  cancel: () => ipcRenderer.send("aura-key:cancel"),
});

// AURA desktop shell (Electron main process).
// It runs the existing local server (server/index.mjs) with Electron's embedded Node and shows the
// existing React build in a window. No app logic lives here: src/ and server/ are used unchanged.
"use strict";

const { app, BrowserWindow, Menu, dialog, ipcMain, safeStorage, session, shell } = require("electron");
const path = require("node:path");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const { ServerProcess, pickPort, describeExit } = require("./server-process.cjs");

const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");
const ICON = path.join(__dirname, "assets", "icon.png");
const PREFERRED_PORT = 3017; // a fixed port keeps one origin; 3001 stays free for `npm run dev`
const BG = "#15171c"; // matches --bg in src/App.scss, avoids a white flash

app.setAppUserModelId("com.soubhagya.aura");

// ---- paths -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const userDir = () => app.getPath("userData"); // %APPDATA%\AURA
const settingsFile = () => path.join(userDir(), "desktop-settings.json");
const logFile = () => path.join(userDir(), "logs", "server.log");

/** Where conversations, memories, meetings and models live. */
function dataDir() {
  if (process.env.AURA_DATA_DIR) return path.resolve(process.env.AURA_DATA_DIR);
  // Unpackaged (npm run desktop): keep using the project's data/ folder so existing data stays.
  return app.isPackaged ? path.join(userDir(), "data") : path.join(ROOT, "data");
}

// ---- Gemini key, encrypted with Windows DPAPI via safeStorage ------------------------------
function readSettings() {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(settingsFile(), "utf8"));
  } catch {
    return {};
  }
}

function writeSettings(s) {
  fs.mkdirSync(userDir(), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(settingsFile(), JSON.stringify(s, null, 2));
}

function storedKey() {
  const s = readSettings();
  if (s.geminiKeyEnc && safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
    try {
      return safeStorage.decryptString(Buffer.from(s.geminiKeyEnc, "base64"));
    } catch {
      return "";
    }
  }
  return s.geminiKey || "";
}

function saveKey(key) {
  const s = readSettings();
  delete s.geminiKey;
  delete s.geminiKeyEnc;
  if (key) {
    if (safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) s.geminiKeyEnc = safeStorage.encryptString(key).toString("base64");
    else s.geminiKey = key;
  }
  writeSettings(s);
}

function serverEnv() {
  const env = { ...process.env, AURA_DATA_DIR: dataDir() };
  const key = storedKey();
  // A key saved in the app wins. Without one, the server falls back to GEMINI_API_KEY from
  // the environment or the project's .env (unpackaged only; .env is never packaged).
  if (key) env.GEMINI_API_KEY = key;
  return env;
}

// ---- server lifecycle ------------------------------------------------------------------------
let server = null;
let mainWindow = null;
let booted = false;
let quitting = false;
let serverStopped = false;

const appOrigin = () => (server ? server.url : null);
function isAppUrl(u) {
  const origin = appOrigin();
  if (!origin || !u) return false;
  try {
    return new URL(u).origin === origin;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

async function launchServer() {
  let lastError = null;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
    const port = await pickPort(attempt === 0 ? PREFERRED_PORT : 0);
    const proc = new ServerProcess({ execPath: process.execPath, root: ROOT, env: serverEnv(), logFile: logFile() }).start(port);
    try {
      const health = await proc.waitUntilReady(90000);
      server = proc;
      watchForCrash(proc);
      return health;
    } catch (e) {
      lastError = e;
      await proc.stop();
      if (!/EADDRINUSE/.test(e.message)) break; // only a port race is worth a second try
    }
  }
  throw lastError;
}

async function stopServer() {
  const old = server;
  server = null;
  if (old) await old.stop();
}

async function restartServer() {
  await stopServer();
  const health = await launchServer();
  if (mainWindow) mainWindow.loadURL(server.url);
  return health;
}

function watchForCrash(proc) {
  proc.exited.then(async (info) => {
    if (quitting || proc.stopping || server !== proc) return;
    server = null;
    const { response } = await dialog.showMessageBox(mainWindow || undefined, {
      type: "error",
      title: "AURA",
      message: "AURA's local server stopped unexpectedly.",
      detail: `${describeExit(info)}\n\n${proc.tail(15)}`.trim(),
      buttons: ["Restart server", "Open log", "Quit"],
      defaultId: 0,
      cancelId: 2,
    });
    if (response === 0) await restartServer().catch(showFatal);
    else if (response === 1) shell.openPath(logFile());
    else app.quit();
  });
}

function showFatal(e) {
  dialog.showErrorBox("AURA could not start", `${e?.message || e}\n\nLog: ${logFile()}`);
  app.quit();
}

// ---- windows ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function createMainWindow() {
  mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 1280,
    height: 860,
    minWidth: 900,
    minHeight: 600,
    title: "AURA",
    icon: ICON,
    backgroundColor: BG,
    show: false,
    webPreferences: { contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true, nodeIntegration: false, spellcheck: true },
  });
  mainWindow.once("ready-to-show", () => mainWindow.show());
  mainWindow.on("closed", () => {
    mainWindow = null;
  });
  mainWindow.loadURL(server.url);
}

/** Small window asking for the Gemini API key. Resolves with the key, or null when cancelled. */
function promptForKey({ firstRun }) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const win = new BrowserWindow({
      width: 540,
      height: 430,
      resizable: false,
      minimizable: false,
      maximizable: false,
      parent: mainWindow || undefined,
      modal: Boolean(mainWindow),
      title: "Gemini API key",
      icon: ICON,
      backgroundColor: BG,
      autoHideMenuBar: true,
      webPreferences: { preload: path.join(__dirname, "key-preload.cjs"), contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true },
    });
    win.setMenuBarVisibility(false);
    let result = null;
    const onSave = (e, key) => {
      if (e.sender !== win.webContents) return;
      result = String(key || "").trim() || null;
      win.close();
    };
    const onCancel = (e) => {
      if (e.sender === win.webContents) win.close();
    };
    ipcMain.on("aura-key:save", onSave);
    ipcMain.on("aura-key:cancel", onCancel);
    win.on("closed", () => {
      ipcMain.removeListener("aura-key:save", onSave);
      ipcMain.removeListener("aura-key:cancel", onCancel);
      resolve(result);
    });
    win.loadFile(path.join(__dirname, "key.html"), {
      query: { firstRun: firstRun ? "1" : "0", hasKey: storedKey() ? "1" : "0" },
    });
  });
}

async function changeKey() {
  const key = await promptForKey({ firstRun: false });
  if (!key) return;
  saveKey(key);
  await restartServer().catch(showFatal);
}

// ---- security: mic for AURA only, everything else opens in the default browser ----------------
const ALLOWED_PERMISSIONS = new Set(["media", "clipboard-sanitized-write", "fullscreen"]);

function openExternal(url) {
  if (/^https?:\/\//i.test(url)) shell.openExternal(url);
}

function setUpSecurity() {
  const ses = session.defaultSession;
  ses.setPermissionRequestHandler((wc, permission, callback, details) => {
    callback(ALLOWED_PERMISSIONS.has(permission) && isAppUrl(details?.requestingUrl || wc.getURL()));
  });
  ses.setPermissionCheckHandler((wc, permission, origin) => ALLOWED_PERMISSIONS.has(permission) && isAppUrl(origin));
  app.on("web-contents-created", (_e, contents) => {
    contents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url }) => {
      openExternal(url);
      return { action: "deny" };
    });
    contents.on("will-navigate", (e, url) => {
      if (!isAppUrl(url)) {
        e.preventDefault();
        openExternal(url);
      }
    });
  });
}

function buildMenu() {
  const template = [
    {
      label: "AURA",
      submenu: [
        { label: "Set Gemini API keyâ€¦", click: () => changeKey() },
        { label: "Open data folder", click: () => shell.openPath(dataDir()) },
        { label: "Open server log", click: () => shell.openPath(logFile()) },
        { type: "separator" },
        { label: "Restart server", click: () => restartServer().catch(showFatal) },
        { type: "separator" },
        { role: "quit" },
      ],
    },
    { role: "editMenu" },
    {
      label: "View",
      submenu: [
        { role: "reload" },
        { role: "forceReload" },
        { role: "toggleDevTools" },
        { type: "separator" },
        { role: "resetZoom" },
        { role: "zoomIn" },
        { role: "zoomOut" },
        { type: "separator" },
        { role: "togglefullscreen" },
      ],
    },
    { role: "windowMenu" },
  ];
  Menu.setApplicationMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate(template));
}

// ---- app lifecycle ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
async function boot() {
  setUpSecurity();
  buildMenu();
  if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(ROOT, "build", "index.html"))) {
    dialog.showErrorBox(
      "AURA",
      'The web app has not been built yet. Run "npm run desktop" (it builds first) or "npm run build", then start AURA again.'
    );
    app.quit();
    return;
  }
  let health = await launchServer();
  if (!health.hasKey) {
    const key = await promptForKey({ firstRun: true });
    if (key) {
      saveKey(key);
      health = await restartServer();
    }
  }
  createMainWindow();
  booted = true;
}

if (!app.requestSingleInstanceLock()) {
  app.quit();
} else {
  app.on("second-instance", () => {
    if (!mainWindow) return;
    if (mainWindow.isMinimized()) mainWindow.restore();
    mainWindow.focus();
  });
  // During first-run setup the key window may be the only window; don't quit when it closes.
  app.on("window-all-closed", () => {
    if (booted) app.quit();
  });
  app.on("before-quit", () => {
    quitting = true;
  });
  app.on("will-quit", (e) => {
    if (serverStopped || !server) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    stopServer().finally(() => {
      serverStopped = true;
      app.quit();
    });
  });
  app.whenReady().then(boot).catch(showFatal);
}

// Entry point for the AURA server inside the desktop app.
// Same server as `npm run serve`, plus one rule: exit when the desktop app goes away.
// The app keeps this process's stdin open; if the app is closed, crashes or is killed,
// the pipe closes and the server stops instead of lingering with the database open.
import { start } from "../server/index.mjs";

const leave = () => process.exit(0);
process.stdin.on("end", leave);
process.stdin.on("close", leave);
process.stdin.on("error", leave);
process.stdin.resume();

await start();



================================================
FILE: desktop/server-process.cjs
================================================
// Starts and supervises the existing AURA server (server/index.mjs) as a child process.
// In the desktop app, Electron's own embedded Node runs it (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1),
// so no separate Node.js install is needed. Plain Node only: no Electron imports here.
"use strict";

const { spawn } = require("node:child_process");
const net = require("node:net");
const http = require("node:http");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

function portIsFree(port) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const s = net.createServer();
    s.once("error", () => resolve(false));
    s.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => s.close(() => resolve(true)));
  });
}

function anyFreePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const s = net.createServer();
    s.once("error", reject);
    s.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const { port } = s.address();
      s.close(() => resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

/** The preferred port when it is free (keeps the app on one origin), otherwise any free port. */
async function pickPort(preferred) {
  if (preferred && (await portIsFree(preferred))) return preferred;
  return anyFreePort();
}

/** GET /api/health on the local server; null when it isn't answering yet. */
function getHealth(port, timeoutMs = 2000) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const req = http.get({ host: "127.0.0.1", port, path: "/api/health", timeout: timeoutMs }, (res) => {
      const chunks = [];
      res.on("data", (c) => chunks.push(c));
      res.on("end", () => {
        if (res.statusCode !== 200) return resolve(null);
        try {
          resolve(JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
        } catch {
          resolve(null);
        }
      });
    });
    req.on("timeout", () => req.destroy());
    req.on("error", () => resolve(null));
  });
}

class ServerProcess {
  /**
   * @param {object} o
   * @param {string} o.execPath  binary that runs the server (Electron's exe, or node in tests)
   * @param {string} o.root      project root containing server/index.mjs and build/
   * @param {object} o.env       environment for the server (AURA_DATA_DIR, GEMINI_API_KEY, ...)
   * @param {string} [o.logFile] server output is appended here
   * @param {string} [o.script]  entry script (default: desktop/server-entry.mjs)
   */
  constructor({ execPath, root, env, logFile, script }) {
    this.execPath = execPath;
    this.root = root;
    this.script = script || path.join(__dirname, "server-entry.mjs");
    this.env = env;
    this.logFile = logFile;
    this.port = null;
    this.child = null;
    this.exitInfo = null;
    this.exited = null;
    this.lines = [];
  }

  get url() {
    return `http://127.0.0.1:${this.port}`;
  }

  _record(chunk) {
    const text = chunk.toString("utf8");
    if (this.log) this.log.write(text);
    for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) if (line.trim()) this.lines.push(line);
    if (this.lines.length > 200) this.lines.splice(0, this.lines.length - 200);
  }

  /** The last lines the server printed, for error messages. */
  tail(n = 20) {
    return this.lines.slice(-n).join("\n");
  }

  start(port) {
    this.port = port;
    if (this.logFile) {
      fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(this.logFile), { recursive: true });
      this.log = fs.createWriteStream(this.logFile, { flags: "a" });
      this.log.write(`\n--- ${new Date().toISOString()} starting AURA server on port ${port} ---\n`);
    }
    // stdin stays open as a lifeline: server-entry.mjs exits when it closes (app quit, crash or kill)
    this.child = spawn(this.execPath, [this.script], {
      cwd: this.root,
      env: { ...this.env, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: "1", AURA_PORT: String(port) },
      stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
      windowsHide: true,
    });
    this.child.stdin.on("error", () => {});
    this.child.stdout.on("data", (c) => this._record(c));
    this.child.stderr.on("data", (c) => this._record(c));
    this.exited = new Promise((resolve) => {
      const done = (info) => {
        if (this.exitInfo) return;
        this.exitInfo = info;
        if (this.log) this.log.write(`--- server exited (${describeExit(info)}) ---\n`);
        resolve(info);
      };
      this.child.once("exit", (code, signal) => done({ code, signal }));
      this.child.once("error", (error) => done({ code: null, signal: null, error }));
    });
    return this;
  }

  /** Resolves with the health payload once the server answers; rejects if it exits or times out. */
  async waitUntilReady(timeoutMs = 60000) {
    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
      if (this.exitInfo) {
        throw new Error(`The AURA server stopped while starting (${describeExit(this.exitInfo)}).\n\n${this.tail()}`);
      }
      const health = await getHealth(this.port);
      if (health && health.ok) return health;
      await sleep(250);
    }
    throw new Error(`The AURA server did not start within ${Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)} s.\n\n${this.tail()}`);
  }

  get running() {
    return Boolean(this.child) && !this.exitInfo;
  }

  async stop(graceMs = 3000) {
    if (!this.running) return this.closeLog();
    this.stopping = true;
    const exitedWithin = (ms) => Promise.race([this.exited.then(() => true), sleep(ms).then(() => false)]);
    this.child.stdin.end(); // polite: server-entry.mjs exits on its own
    if (!(await exitedWithin(graceMs)) && this.running) {
      this.child.kill();
      if (!(await exitedWithin(2000)) && this.running) this.child.kill("SIGKILL");
      await this.exited;
    }
    this.closeLog();
  }

  closeLog() {
    if (this.log) {
      this.log.end();
      this.log = null;
    }
  }
}

function describeExit(info) {
  if (!info) return "unknown";
  if (info.error) return info.error.message;
  if (info.signal) return `signal ${info.signal}`;
  return `exit code ${info.code}`;
}

module.exports = { ServerProcess, pickPort, portIsFree, getHealth, describeExit };

FILE: desktop/tests/server-process.test.cjs

// Checks the desktop shell's server supervisor against the real server/index.mjs.
// Runs with plain Node (no Electron needed): npm run test:desktop
"use strict";

const test = require("node:test");
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const os = require("node:os");
const path = require("node:path");
const net = require("node:net");
const { ServerProcess, pickPort, portIsFree, getHealth } = require("../server-process.cjs");

const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, "..", "..");

function tempDir() {
  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "aura-desktop-test-"));
}

function serverEnv(dataDir) {
  // AURA_NO_WARMUP: don't download or load the local models during the test
  return { ...process.env, AURA_DATA_DIR: dataDir, AURA_NO_WARMUP: "1", GEMINI_API_KEY: "test-key-not-real" };
}

test("starts the real server, reports health, keeps data in AURA_DATA_DIR, stops cleanly", async () => {
  const dataDir = tempDir();
  const logFile = path.join(dataDir, "logs", "server.log");
  const port = await pickPort(0);
  const proc = new ServerProcess({ execPath: process.execPath, root: ROOT, env: serverEnv(dataDir), logFile }).start(port);
  try {
    const health = await proc.waitUntilReady(30000);
    assert.equal(health.ok, true);
    assert.equal(health.hasKey, true);
    assert.equal(path.resolve(health.dataDir), path.resolve(dataDir));
    assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(dataDir, "aura.db")), "database created in the data folder");
    assert.equal(proc.url, `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`);
  } finally {
    await proc.stop();
  }
  assert.equal(proc.running, false);
  assert.equal(proc.exitInfo.code, 0, "stopped politely (stdin closed), not killed");
  assert.equal(await getHealth(port, 500), null, "nothing answers after stop");
  assert.ok(await portIsFree(port), "port released");
  assert.match(fs.readFileSync(logFile, "utf8"), /server on http:\/\/localhost/);
});

test("pickPort falls back when the preferred port is taken", async () => {
  const blocker = net.createServer();
  await new Promise((r) => blocker.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", r));
  const taken = blocker.address().port;
  try {
    const port = await pickPort(taken);
    assert.notEqual(port, taken);
    assert.ok(await portIsFree(port));
  } finally {
    blocker.close();
  }
});

test("reports an unexpected exit with the server's last output", async () => {
  const dataDir = tempDir();
  const port = await pickPort(0);
  const proc = new ServerProcess({ execPath: process.execPath, root: ROOT, env: serverEnv(dataDir) }).start(port);
  await proc.waitUntilReady(30000);
  proc.child.kill("SIGKILL"); // simulate a crash
  const info = await proc.exited;
  assert.ok(info.code !== 0 || info.signal, "exit recorded");
  assert.equal(proc.running, false);
  assert.match(proc.tail(), /server on/);
});

test("fails fast with a readable error when the server can't start", async () => {
  const fakeRoot = tempDir();
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(fakeRoot, "server"));
  const script = path.join(fakeRoot, "server", "index.mjs");
  fs.writeFileSync(script, 'console.error("boom: listen EADDRINUSE"); process.exit(3);');
  const proc = new ServerProcess({ execPath: process.execPath, root: fakeRoot, env: process.env, script }).start(await pickPort(0));
  await assert.rejects(proc.waitUntilReady(10000), (e) => /exit code 3/.test(e.message) && /EADDRINUSE/.test(e.message));
});

test("the server exits by itself when the app process is killed (no orphan holding the database)", async () => {
  const dataDir = tempDir();
  const port = await pickPort(0);
  // a stand-in for the Electron main process: starts the server, then gets killed without cleanup
  const parentScript = path.join(dataDir, "parent.cjs");
  fs.writeFileSync(
    parentScript,
    `const { ServerProcess } = require(${JSON.stringify(path.join(__dirname, "..", "server-process.cjs"))});
     const p = new ServerProcess({ execPath: process.execPath, root: ${JSON.stringify(ROOT)}, env: ${JSON.stringify(serverEnv(dataDir))} }).start(${port});
     p.waitUntilReady(30000).then(() => console.log("ready"));
     setInterval(() => {}, 1000);`
  );
  const { spawn } = require("node:child_process");
  const parent = spawn(process.execPath, [parentScript], { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "inherit"] });
  await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    parent.stdout.on("data", (c) => String(c).includes("ready") && resolve());
    parent.once("exit", () => reject(new Error("parent exited early")));
  });
  assert.ok(await getHealth(port), "server up");
  parent.kill("SIGKILL");
  const deadline = Date.now() + 10000;
  while (Date.now() < deadline && !(await portIsFree(port))) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));
  assert.ok(await portIsFree(port), "server exited after its parent was killed");
});

# AURA memory evaluation (Direction A)

Reproducible experiments on AURA's long-term memory: how the "ask before changes" review gate,
the extractor's candidate selection and memory search affect what the assistant ends up believing.
Results and what they support: **[RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md)**.

Everything runs against AURA's **real** server code (`server/memory.mjs`, `server/db.mjs`), the real SQLite
schema and the real local embedding model (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), on a **throw-away database in a
temporary folder**. Your own `data/aura.db` is never opened: `lib/env.mjs` refuses to run if the database
path is not inside the new temporary folder.

## Running

```bash
npm run eval:gate          # Exp. 1  review policies vs. extractor error rate      (~1-2 min)
npm run eval:gate:fix      # Exp. 1 again, extractor candidates without the 0.25 minimum score
npm run eval:retrieval     # Exp. 2  does search find the right memory?            (<1 min)
npm run eval:reach         # Exp. 3  can the extractor see the memory it must change? (<1 min)
npm run eval:all           # all of the above
npm run eval:real          # Exp. 4  real Gemini extractor: shows the plan, sends nothing
npm run eval:real -- --yes # ... and runs it (needs internet + GEMINI_API_KEY in .env; ~170 requests)
npm run eval:rescore -- <real-gemini run folder>   # re-score with the current rules + annotation sheet
npm run eval:compare       # paired comparison of baseline / +F1 / +F2 / both (writes ABLATION.md, ABLATION.csv)
npm run eval:results       # writes RESULTS.md from the result folders (never edit its numbers by hand)
python eval/make_figures.py # figures (PDF + PNG) from the result folders; needs matplotlib
```

Exp. 5, LongMemEval (needs `longmemeval_s_cleaned.json` in `eval/data/`, see the header of `run-longmemeval.mjs`):

```bash
npm run eval:lme                    # shows the plan and the number of requests, sends nothing
npm run eval:lme -- --yes           # 30 knowledge-update questions x (append, auto, gate + 2 baselines)
npm run eval:lme -- --questions 78 --yes   # all knowledge-update questions (many more requests)
npm run eval:lme -- --check-with-sim       # plumbing test on a made-up fixture, no Gemini, no dataset
```

Each question is played through AURA's real extractor and store with its evidence sessions plus a few
distractor sessions, then answered from the memories AURA's search returns and graded by a Gemini judge and by
string match. The gate's reviewer is an oracle approximation (LongMemEval has no labels for which changes are
right); read `run-longmemeval.mjs`'s header before quoting results. Resumable like Exp. 4 (`--out`, `--budget`).

After a real-Gemini run: `npm run eval:rescore -- <folder>`, fill in `human_label` in that folder's
`annotation.csv` (labels explained in `annotation-guide.md`; ideally a second person labels a copy),
run `eval:rescore` again to get the agreement (Cohen's kappa, `agreement.md`), then
`npm run eval:results -- --real <folder>`. Real runs also save every review card and decision
(`decisions.jsonl`) and every final memory (`memories.jsonl`).

Each run writes `eval/results/<experiment>/<timestamp>/`: `config.json` (settings), `summary.md`
(tables), `summary.csv`, raw rows (`runs.csv` / `queries.csv` / `changes.csv` and the `.jsonl`
checkpoint), `run-info.json`. Runs are resumable: `--out <folder>` continues an unfinished run, and
`--budget <seconds>` stops starting new work after that many seconds. Useful options:
`--personas`, `--seeds`, `--errors 0,0.1`, `--policies auto,gate`, `--u`, `--sizes`.

Simulation runs are exactly repeatable: they use a simulated clock (`Date.now()` ticks 1 ms per call
from a fixed start), because AURA orders memories by millisecond timestamps and same-millisecond ties
otherwise depend on timing (an earlier version without it varied by about 0.5% between runs). A repeated
slice of Exp. 1 matched the full run field by field. Real-Gemini runs use the real clock.

On Linux, transformers.js cannot load the Windows build of the `sharp` image library; the harness
replaces it with a stub (`lib/sharp-stub.mjs`) because only text is embedded. On Windows nothing
changes.

## What is real and what is simulated

| Part | Exp. 1-3 | Exp. 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Memory store, operations, supersede/retire/forget, review proposals | AURA code | AURA code |
| Candidate selection for the extractor (12 related + 8 most recent) | AURA code | AURA code |
| Sentence embeddings | local MiniLM model | local MiniLM model |
| Extractor (Gemini) | **simulated, known error rate e** | **real Gemini** |
| User who reviews proposals | simulated, slip rate u | simulated, slip rate u |
| Conversations | scripted personas (`lib/scenarios.mjs`) | same personas |

## Design

**Personas** (`lib/scenarios.mjs`). Each persona has 8 of 12 fact types (city, employer, dog, sister,
diet, gym time, language, car, project, coffee, hobby, birthday) and 5 sessions, about 21 user turns:
facts are stated, later updated ("I've just moved to Hyderabad."), retired ("I stopped going to the
gym."), forgotten on request ("Please forget what I told you about my car."), repeated, and mixed with
distractors that must not become memories (hypotheticals, questions, an assistant suggestion, facts
about friends). The true memory state is known after every turn. The memory store starts with 30
unrelated true facts and gains 10 between sessions, as months of earlier use would.

**Simulated extractor** (`lib/harness.mjs`, `makeSimExtractor`). Returns what a correct model would
return for the turn, using only the memories shown in the prompt (a change whose target is not shown
becomes an "add", as a real model would do). Errors are injected at rate e: a correct operation is
dropped (miss), a distractor becomes a false memory (spurious add), and a true memory shown to the model
is retired or overwritten with a false value (wrong change). Random draws are made in a fixed order per
turn, so all policies face the same errors.

**Policies.**
`append` = only new facts are stored, nothing is ever changed;
`auto` = every operation is applied (AURA with "Ask before changing memories" off);
`gate` = changes to existing memories wait for the user (AURA's default);
`gateAll` = new facts must be confirmed too (emulated by the harness; AURA has no such setting).

**Simulated user.** Reviews pending proposals at the end of each session; approves correct ones and turns
down wrong ones, but gets it wrong with probability u.

## Metrics

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| precision / recall / F1 | over the persona's facts: active persona memories that are true / true facts that are active |
| stale facts | active memories holding a value the user stated earlier but that is no longer true |
| false facts | active memories the user never stated about themselves (spurious or corrupted) |
| true facts destroyed | true memories (persona **and** background) that ended up superseded, outdated or deleted by a wrong change. F1 does not see background memories, so this is the safety metric |
| wrong changes applied | injected wrong changes that took effect (applied directly, or accepted by the user) |
| prompts / 100 turns | review cards the user had to answer per 100 user turns (burden) |
| prompt precision | share of review cards that proposed a correct change |
| candidate miss rate | share of change turns whose target memory was not among the candidates shown to the extractor |
| forget residual | forget requests whose value is still stored in a memory row (any status) / in the conversation text |
| ended / hypothetical / third-party (Exp. 4) | model wording: a correct note that a retired fact ended / a hypothetical kept as a memory (error) / a fact about someone else (allowed) |
| hit@k, found / noise (Exp. 2) | right memory among the top k / never-stated questions that still return memories |
| reachable (Exp. 3) | the memory a change refers to is among the extractor's candidates |

## Files

```
eval/
  run-gate-sim.mjs      Exp. 1          run-retrieval.mjs   Exp. 2
  run-reachability.mjs  Exp. 3          run-real.mjs        Exp. 4 (+ --check-with-sim)
  rescore-real.mjs      re-score a real run, annotation sheet, agreement
  build-results.mjs     writes RESULTS.md from the result folders
  make_figures.py       figures         RESULTS.md          findings (generated)
  lib/env.mjs           isolated database, safety check
  lib/harness.mjs       persona runner, simulated extractor and user, exact scoring
  lib/scenarios.mjs     personas, distractors, background facts, ground truth
  lib/loose.mjs         value-based scoring for model-written memories (Exp. 4)
  lib/hooks.mjs, register.mjs, proxy-gemini.mjs, cached-models.mjs, sharp-stub.mjs   module plumbing
  lib/stats.mjs, rng.mjs  statistics, seeded random numbers
  results/              one folder per run; figures/ for the paper
```

## Changes made to AURA for the evaluation

- `server/memory.mjs`: `memoryEvents` (extraction, applied operations, review decisions, whether the
  user edited the wording before accepting); `lexicalScore` exported; `searchMemories(..., { minScore })`
  option; `AURA_EXTRACT_MIN_SCORE` environment variable for the extractor's candidate selection
  (unset = unchanged behaviour).
- `server/gemini.mjs`: `usage` totals (requests, prompt/output tokens, latency) for `generateJSON`.
- `package.json`: the `eval:*` scripts.

None of these change what the app does by default; `npm run test:server` passes (26/26).


## Ablation of the two memory switches (journal paper, Direction 1)

Switches (all default off, read from the environment on every call; see `server/memory.mjs`):

- `AURA_CANDIDATES=default|nomin|sentence|adaptive`: which stored memories the extractor is shown.
- `AURA_REPROPOSE=N`: a rejected change may come back at most N times, only after the user said something new.

Every runner takes `--candidates`, `--repropose` (and the simulated and real runners also `--restate 1`, which adds a
"Like I said, ..." turn after each update). Use one folder per variant:

```
# simulated (about 4 s per variant)
for v in "baseline default 0" "f1 default 2" "f2 adaptive 0" "both adaptive 2"; do set -- $v
  npm run eval:gate -- --errors 0,0.1,0.2 --policies auto,gate --restate 1 --candidates $2 --repropose $3 --out eval/results/ablation/$1
done
npm run eval:compare                      # paired differences, bootstrap intervals, sign tests

# real Gemini: same four variants into eval/results/real-ablation/<name>, then
npm run eval:compare -- --dir eval/results/real-ablation --out eval/ABLATION-REAL.md

# LongMemEval: baseline vs. both
npm run eval:lme -- --candidates default --repropose 0 --out eval/results/lme/baseline
npm run eval:lme -- --candidates adaptive --repropose 2 --out eval/results/lme/both
```

// Writes eval/RESULTS.md from the result folders, so every number in it comes from a file.
//
//   npm run eval:results
//   npm run eval:results -- --real eval/results/real-gemini/<folder> [--real-fix eval/results/real-gemini/<folder>]
//
// Re-run after any new experiment run (and after `npm run eval:rescore -- <folder>` for real-Gemini runs).
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { mean, ci95, parseCSV, mdTable } from "./lib/stats.mjs";

const EVAL = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const R = (p) => path.join(EVAL, "results", p);
const { values: a } = parseArgs({
  options: {
    gate: { type: "string", default: R("gate-sim/v2-20261013") },
    "gate-fix": { type: "string", default: R("gate-sim/v2-20261013-extract-nomin") },
    retrieval: { type: "string", default: R("retrieval/v2-20261013") },
    reach: { type: "string", default: R("reachability/v3-20261014") },
    "scorer-check": { type: "string", default: R("real-scorer-check/v2-20261013") },
    real: { type: "string", default: R("real-gemini/20261013-130739") },
    "real-fix": { type: "string" },
    out: { type: "string", default: path.join(EVAL, "RESULTS.md") },
  },
});
const rel = (p) => path.relative(EVAL, p).split(path.sep).join("/");
const csv = (dir, f) => parseCSV(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), "utf8"));
const jsonl = (dir, f) => (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, f)) ? fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), "utf8").split("\n").filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l)) : []);
const json = (dir, f) => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), "utf8"));
const f = (x, d = 2) => (Number.isFinite(+x) ? (+x).toFixed(d) : "n/a");
const pct = (x) => `${Math.round(100 * x)}%`;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- data
const G = csv(a.gate, "summary.csv");
const GF = csv(a["gate-fix"], "summary.csv");
const gCfg = json(a.gate, "config.json");
const gRuns = jsonl(a.gate, "runs.jsonl");
const cell = (S, sweep, policy, e, u) => S.find((r) => r.sweep === sweep && r.policy === policy && +r.e === e && +r.u === u);
const err = (S, policy, e) => cell(S, "error", policy, e, gCfg.u);
const n = (r, k) => +r[k];
const destroyedAll = (r) => n(r, "destroyed_mean") + n(r, "fillerLost_mean");
const errors = gCfg.errors;
const POL = { append: "append", auto: "auto", gate: "gate (AURA)", gateAll: "gateAll" };

const RS = csv(a.retrieval, "summary.csv");
const TH = csv(a.retrieval, "threshold.csv");
const RQ = jsonl(a.retrieval, "queries.jsonl");
const RA = jsonl(a.retrieval, "absent.jsonl");
const rCfg = json(a.retrieval, "config.json");
const CH = csv(a.reach, "summary.csv");
const CHrows = jsonl(a.reach, "changes.jsonl");
const reachCfg = json(a.reach, "config.json");
const SC = jsonl(a["scorer-check"], "runs.jsonl");

const real = fs.existsSync(path.join(a.real, "rescored.jsonl")) ? { dir: a.real, rows: jsonl(a.real, "rescored.jsonl"), labels: jsonl(a.real, "labels.jsonl"), cfg: json(a.real, "config.json") } : null;
const realFix = a["real-fix"] && fs.existsSync(path.join(a["real-fix"], "rescored.jsonl")) ? { dir: a["real-fix"], rows: jsonl(a["real-fix"], "rescored.jsonl"), cfg: json(a["real-fix"], "config.json") } : null;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- text
const md = [];
const P = (...x) => md.push(...x);
P(`# Results: user-controlled memory in AURA (Direction A)`, ``);
P(`Generated by \`npm run eval:results\` (eval/build-results.mjs) on ${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}; every number below is computed from the run folders named in each section. ` +
  `Do not edit numbers by hand: re-run the experiment, then this script. How the experiments work: [README.md](README.md).`, ``);
P(`**Status of the evidence.** Experiments 1-3 use AURA's real memory code, database and local embedding model (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) with a **simulated** extractor ` +
  `and a simulated user: they measure the system's mechanics, not Gemini's judgement. ` +
  (real
    ? `Experiment 4 uses the **real** Gemini extractor (${real.cfg.extractor}) on ${real.rows.filter((r) => r.policy === real.rows[0].policy).length} personas per policy: enough to see which errors a real model makes, too few for firm rates.`
    : `Experiment 4 (real Gemini) has not been run yet.`), ``);

// Finding 1
const red = errors.filter((e) => e > 0).map((e) => 1 - destroyedAll(err(G, "gate", e)) / destroyedAll(err(G, "auto", e)));
const gatePrompts = errors.map((e) => n(err(G, "gate", e), "promptsPer100Turns_mean"));

P(mdTable(["e", "policy", "F1", "stale", "false", "true facts destroyed", "prompts / 100 turns", "prompt precision"],
  errors.flatMap((e) => Object.keys(POL).map((p) => {
    const r = err(G, p, e);
    return [e, POL[p], `${f(r.f1_mean, 3)} Â± ${f(r.f1_ci95, 3)}`, f(r.stale_mean), f(r.falseMem_mean), f(destroyedAll(r)), f(r.promptsPer100Turns_mean, 1), r.promptPrecision === "NaN" || r.promptPrecision === "" ? "-" : f(r.promptPrecision)];
  }))), ``);
P(`- With auto-apply, true facts destroyed grow with the error rate (${errors.filter((e) => e > 0).map((e) => f(destroyedAll(err(G, "auto", e)))).join(", ")} per persona at e = ${errors.filter((e) => e > 0).join(", ")}). ` +
  `The gate cuts this to ${errors.filter((e) => e > 0).map((e) => f(destroyedAll(err(G, "gate", e)))).join(", ")}: **${Math.round(100 * Math.min(...red))}-${Math.round(100 * Math.max(...red))}% fewer**.`);
P(`- **F1 hides most of this damage.** F1 counts only the user's own facts; at e = ${e2}, auto-apply destroyed ${f(err(G, "auto", e2).destroyed_mean)} of the user's facts and ${f(err(G, "auto", e2).fillerLost_mean)} background facts per persona, ` +
  `because a wrong change hits whatever true memory the extractor was shown, and most shown memories are background ones. Report destroyed facts as the safety metric and F1 next to it.`);

P(`- Append-only never destroys anything but leaves every changed fact stale (${f(err(G, "append", 0).stale_mean)} per persona at e = 0).`, ``);

const us = gCfg.uSweep;
P(`## Finding 2: the gate depends on a careful user, and a mistaken "keep" is never asked again`, ``);

P(mdTable(["u", "gate F1", "gate stale", "gate wrong changes applied", "gateAll F1", "gateAll wrong changes applied"],

P(`AURA does not propose a change again after the user turns it down (\`propose()\` in \`server/memory.mjs\`). That avoids nagging, but one mistaken rejection of a correct update keeps the old fact for good: ` +

  P(`- It also wrote correct memories in forms a strict checker would miss: facts about people in the user's life (${byLabel("third-party").map((c) => `"${c}"`).filter((v, i, x) => x.indexOf(v) === i).join("; ")}) ` +

  const wrong = s(real.rows, "proposalsJudgedWrongDuringRun");
  if (wrong) {
    const logged = jsonl(real.dir, "decisions.jsonl");
    P(logged.length
      ? `- ${wrong} review card(s) were judged wrong during the run (see decisions.jsonl for each card and decision).`
      : `- During the run the simulated user turned down ${wrong} review card(s) it judged wrong with the rules in place at the time. Cards were not logged in this run, so which one is not known; ` +
        `a retirement written as an update (above) would have been turned down, so the gate row may be slightly pessimistic until the run is repeated.`);
  }
  P(``);
  if (realFix) {
    P(`With candidate selection without the minimum score (\`${rel(realFix.dir)}/\`):`, ``);
    P(realTable(realFix.rows), ``);
  }
}

// Checks
const scAgree = SC.filter((r) => r.agree).length;
const jd = SC.reduce((t, r) => t + (r.judgeDecisions || 0), 0), ja = SC.reduce((t, r) => t + (r.judgeAgree || 0), 0);
const turns = mean(gRuns.map((r) => r.userTurns));
const perE = errors.filter((e) => e > 0).map((e) => n(err(G, "auto", e), "injectedWrongChanges") / e);
P(`## Checks`, ``);
P(`- Value-based scoring (used for Gemini's wording) vs. exact scoring on simulated runs: ${scAgree} of ${SC.length} persona runs identical` + (jd ? `; the two review judges agreed on ${ja} of ${jd} decisions` : ``) + ` (\`${rel(a["scorer-check"])}/\`).`);
P(`- Retrieval re-scoring vs. AURA's real search: ${RQ.filter((r) => r.sanity).length} of ${RQ.length} queries identical.`);
P(`- Consistency: personas average ${f(turns, 1)} user turns, 4 of them distractors. Injected wrong changes per persona (${errors.filter((e) => e > 0).map((e) => f(err(G, "auto", e).injectedWrongChanges)).join(", ")} at e = ${errors.filter((e) => e > 0).join(", ")}) ` +
  `equal e x ${f(Math.min(...perE), 1)}-${f(Math.max(...perE), 1)}, as expected (a wrong change is skipped when no true memory is shown). Every review card was correct at e = 0 (prompt precision ${f(err(G, "gate", 0).promptPrecision)}).`);
P(`- Simulation runs use a simulated clock (1 ms per call), so they are exactly repeatable; a repeated slice of Experiment 1 matched the full run field by field.`);
P(`- \`npm run test:server\` passes with the instrumentation and the option added.`, ``);

  if (i >= 0) P(sm.slice(i).trim().replace(/^## /, "## Experiment 3b: "), ``);

P(`- Gating changes to existing memories prevents almost all destructive errors (${Math.round(100 * Math.min(...red))}-${Math.round(100 * Math.max(...red))}% fewer at e = ${errors.filter((e) => e > 0)[0]}-${errors[errors.length - 1]}) for ${Math.round(Math.min(...gatePrompts))}-${Math.round(Math.max(...gatePrompts))} prompts per 100 turns; gating new facts too costs about ${f(n(err(G, "gateAll", e1), "promptsPer100Turns_mean") / n(err(G, "gate", e1), "promptsPer100Turns_mean"), 1)}x the prompts.`);
P(`- F1 over the user's facts understates the harm of auto-applied wrong changes.`);
P(`- Candidate selection limits what the extractor can change (${pct(Math.min(...missRange))}-${pct(Math.max(...missRange))} of change requests miss their target with 25-${big} other memories), and selecting the 12 best matches without a minimum fixes most of it.`);
P(`- Not re-asking after a rejection makes the gate sensitive to user mistakes.`);
P(``, `Supported by Experiments 5-6 (paired comparisons; see ABLATION.md, ABLATION-REAL.md, ABLATION-REAL-M2.md):`);
P(`- Showing the extractor more candidates (F2) removes most stale facts: in simulation at every error rate, and with real Gemini on two models (12 personas each; paired, sign test). It costs about a third more prompt tokens and a few more review prompts.`);

}

P(`- Anything about real users (burden as felt, trust, time per decision): needs a user study.`);
P(`- A comparison with Mem0 or other published LongMemEval numbers: AURA was run on 30 knowledge-update questions with one model (Experiment 7), a different protocol from published results; do not put the numbers side by side.`);
P(`- Any effect of F1 (re-propose) with real Gemini: Experiment 6 shows none; its effect is small and situational even in simulation.`);
P(`- Effects on LongMemEval: with F1 + F2 the gated system gains questions (see Experiment 7, paired test) but the difference is not significant at 30 questions, and every AURA variant stays below the full-context baseline.`);

P(`- Personas average ${f(turns, 1)} user turns over 5 sessions; long-term effects over months are extrapolated.`);
P(`- Scripted personas written by the evaluator: 12 fact types, short third-person facts, English only; paraphrase coverage is limited (3 per change in Experiment 3, 1 per change elsewhere).`);
P(`- The simulated extractor's errors are independent and uniform; Experiment 4 suggests a real model's errors are concentrated on new facts, not on changes.`);
P(`- The simulated user reviews at the end of each session, with a fixed slip rate.`);
P(`- Labels for Gemini's wording come from rules (eval/lib/loose.mjs); check them by hand with the annotation sheet (\`npm run eval:rescore\`) before publishing.`);
P(`- One embedding model (MiniLM-L6), at the quantised size AURA ships; the largest store tested has ${big} background facts.`);

// Paired comparison of two LongMemEval runs (same questions): baseline vs. +F1+F2, per system.
//
//   npm run eval:compare-lme
//   npm run eval:compare-lme -- --base eval/results/lme/baseline --other eval/results/lme/both --out eval/ABLATION-LME.md
//
// "none" and "context" use no memory, so their difference between the two runs is run-to-run noise of the
// answering and judging model; it tells how much of a difference in the memory systems to believe.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { mdTable } from "./lib/stats.mjs";

const EVAL = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const { values: a } = parseArgs({
  options: {
    base: { type: "string", default: path.join(EVAL, "results", "lme", "baseline") },
    other: { type: "string", default: path.join(EVAL, "results", "lme", "both") },
    out: { type: "string", default: path.join(EVAL, "ABLATION-LME.md") },
  },
});
const rows = (d) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(d, "runs.jsonl"), "utf8").split("\n").filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
const rel = (p) => path.relative(EVAL, p).split(path.sep).join("/");
const A = rows(a.base), B = rows(a.other);
const key = (r) => `${r.policy}|${r.qid}`;
const bm = new Map(B.map((r) => [key(r), r]));

function signP(b, c) {
  const n = b + c;
  if (!n) return 1;
  const lo = Math.min(b, c);
  let p = 0, t = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i <= lo; i++) { p += t; t = (t * (n - i)) / (i + 1); }
  return Math.min(1, (2 * p) / 2 ** n);
}
const f = (x, d = 3) => (Number.isFinite(x) ? x.toFixed(d) : "n/a");
const out = [`# LongMemEval: baseline vs. F1 + F2 (paired by question)`, ``];
out.push(`Baseline: \`${rel(a.base)}\` (candidates default, no re-propose). Other: \`${rel(a.other)}\`. Same ${new Set(A.map((r) => r.qid)).size} questions, same model; "judged" = the judge model's verdict, "strict" = strict string match. b = right only in the baseline run, c = right only in the other run; exact two-sided sign test on the discordant pairs.`, ``);
const table = [];
for (const policy of ["none", "context", "append", "auto", "gate"]) {
  const pairs = A.filter((r) => r.policy === policy && bm.has(key(r))).map((r) => [r, bm.get(key(r))]);
  if (!pairs.length) continue;
  for (const [field, label] of [["judged", "judged"], ["strict", "strict"]]) {
    const n = pairs.length;
    const acc0 = pairs.reduce((t, [x]) => t + x[field], 0) / n, acc1 = pairs.reduce((t, [, y]) => t + y[field], 0) / n;
    const b = pairs.filter(([x, y]) => x[field] && !y[field]).length, c = pairs.filter(([x, y]) => !x[field] && y[field]).length;
    table.push([policy, label, n, f(acc0), f(acc1), `${acc1 - acc0 >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${f(acc1 - acc0)}`, b, c, f(signP(b, c))]);
  }
}
out.push(mdTable(["system", "measure", "questions", "baseline run", "other run", "difference", "b", "c", "p (sign)"], table), ``);
out.push(`The rows for \`none\` and \`context\` use no memory: any difference there is noise between runs (sampling of the answering and judging model). Differences of the memory systems (append, auto, gate) of that size should not be read as an effect.`, ``);
fs.writeFileSync(a.out, out.join("\n"));
console.log(`Wrote ${a.out}`);

FILE: eval/compare-variants.mjs

// Paired comparison of variants (baseline vs. +F1 / +F2 / both) from the run folders, for simulated and real runs.
//
//   npm run eval:compare                                   the simulated ablation in eval/results/ablation
//   npm run eval:compare -- --dir eval/results/real-ablation --out eval/ABLATION-REAL.md
//   npm run eval:compare -- --base eval/results/x/base --variants f1=eval/results/x/f1,both=eval/results/x/both
//
// Rows are matched by (sweep, policy, e, u, seed, persona), so every difference is paired (same persona, same
// seed). Per cell and metric: mean difference (variant - baseline), 95% bootstrap interval, and an exact two-sided
// sign test on the non-tied pairs. No multiple-comparison correction is applied; the tables say how many tests
// were run so the reader can apply one.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { mean, mdTable, toCSV } from "./lib/stats.mjs";

const EVAL = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const { values: a } = parseArgs({
  options: {
    dir: { type: "string", default: path.join(EVAL, "results", "ablation") },
    base: { type: "string" },
    variants: { type: "string" },
    out: { type: "string", default: path.join(EVAL, "ABLATION.md") },
    boot: { type: "string", default: "4000" },
  },
});
const rows = (dir) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, "runs.jsonl"), "utf8").split("\n").filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
const rel = (p) => path.relative(EVAL, p).split(path.sep).join("/");

let baseDir, variants;
if (a.base) {
  baseDir = path.resolve(a.base);
  variants = Object.fromEntries((a.variants || "").split(",").filter(Boolean).map((s) => s.split("=")).map(([k, v]) => [k, path.resolve(v)]));
} else {
  baseDir = path.join(a.dir, "baseline");
  variants = Object.fromEntries(["f1", "f2", "both"].filter((v) => fs.existsSync(path.join(a.dir, v, "runs.jsonl"))).map((v) => [v, path.join(a.dir, v)]));
}
const LABEL = { f1: "+F1 (re-propose)", f2: "+F2 (adaptive candidates)", both: "F1 + F2" };
const METRICS = [
  ["f1", "F1", +1],
  ["stale", "stale facts", -1],
  ["falseMem", "false facts", -1],
  ["destroyed", "true facts destroyed", -1],
  ["wrongChangesApplied", "wrong changes applied", -1],
  ["promptsPer100Turns", "prompts / 100 turns", 0],
  ["exactState", "exact final state", +1],
  ["promptTokens", "prompt tokens", 0],
];
const key = (r) => [r.sweep ?? "", r.policy, r.e ?? "", r.u ?? "", r.seed, r.persona].join("|");
const cellOf = (r) => [r.sweep ?? "", r.policy, r.e ?? "", r.u ?? ""].join("|");

// small deterministic RNG so the intervals are repeatable
function lcg(seed) { let s = seed >>> 0; return () => ((s = (Math.imul(s, 1664525) + 1013904223) >>> 0) / 4294967296); }
function bootCI(d, B) {
  const r = lcg(12345), m = [];
  for (let b = 0; b < B; b++) { let t = 0; for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i++) t += d[Math.floor(r() * d.length)]; m.push(t / d.length); }
  m.sort((x, y) => x - y);
  return [m[Math.floor(0.025 * B)], m[Math.min(B - 1, Math.floor(0.975 * B))]];
}
function signP(d) {
  const nz = d.filter((x) => Math.abs(x) > 1e-12), n = nz.length, k = nz.filter((x) => x > 0).length;
  if (!n) return 1;
  const lo = Math.min(k, n - k);
  let p = 0, c = 1; // C(n,0)
  for (let i = 0; i <= lo; i++) { p += c; c = (c * (n - i)) / (i + 1); }
  return Math.min(1, (2 * p) / 2 ** n);
}

const base = new Map(rows(baseDir).map((r) => [key(r), r]));
const out = [], csvRows = [];
let tests = 0;
const fmt = (x, d = 3) => (Number.isFinite(x) ? x.toFixed(d) : "n/a");
const pfmt = (p) => (p < 0.001 ? "<0.001" : p.toFixed(3));
out.push(`# Variant comparison (paired)`, ``);
out.push(`Baseline: \`${rel(baseDir)}\`. ${Object.entries(variants).map(([k, v]) => `${LABEL[k] || k}: \`${rel(v)}\``).join("; ")}.`, ``);
out.push(`Each row is a paired difference (variant - baseline) over the same persona and seed. Interval = 95% bootstrap (${a.boot} resamples); p = exact two-sided sign test on non-tied pairs. "better" means the direction that helps (higher F1, fewer stale/false/destroyed). No correction for multiple tests is applied.`, ``);

for (const [name, dir] of Object.entries(variants)) {
  const vr = rows(dir), groups = new Map();
  for (const r of vr) {
    const b = base.get(key(r));
    if (!b) continue;
    const c = cellOf(r);
    if (!groups.has(c)) groups.set(c, []);
    groups.get(c).push([b, r]);
  }
  out.push(`## ${LABEL[name] || name} vs. baseline`, ``);
  const table = [];
  for (const [c, pairs] of [...groups].sort()) {
    const [sweep, policy, e, u] = c.split("|");
    for (const [m, label, good] of METRICS) {
      const d = pairs.filter(([b, r]) => Number.isFinite(b[m]) && Number.isFinite(r[m])).map(([b, r]) => r[m] - b[m]);
      if (d.length < 2) continue;
      const md = mean(d), [lo, hi] = bootCI(d, +a.boot), p = signP(d);
      tests++;
      const better = good === 0 ? "" : md * good > 0 ? "better" : md * good < 0 ? "worse" : "same";
      table.push([sweep || "-", policy, e === "" ? "-" : e, u === "" ? "-" : u, label, d.length, `${fmt(mean(pairs.map(([b]) => b[m])))} -> ${fmt(mean(pairs.map(([, r]) => r[m])))}`, `${md >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${fmt(md)} [${fmt(lo)}, ${fmt(hi)}]`, pfmt(p), better]);
      csvRows.push({ variant: name, sweep, policy, e, u, metric: m, pairs: d.length, base: mean(pairs.map(([b]) => b[m])), variantMean: mean(pairs.map(([, r]) => r[m])), diff: md, lo, hi, signP: p });
    }
  }
  // the main table: F1 and stale facts only; the full table follows
  const main = table.filter((r) => r[4] === "F1" || r[4] === "stale facts" || r[4] === "prompts / 100 turns");
  out.push(mdTable(["sweep", "policy", "e", "u", "metric", "pairs", "baseline -> variant", "difference [95% CI]", "p (sign)", ""], main), ``);
  out.push(`<details><summary>All metrics</summary>`, ``, mdTable(["sweep", "policy", "e", "u", "metric", "pairs", "baseline -> variant", "difference [95% CI]", "p (sign)", ""], table), ``, `</details>`, ``);
}
out.push(`${tests} paired tests were run in total.`, ``);
fs.writeFileSync(a.out, out.join("\n"));
fs.writeFileSync(a.out.replace(/\.md$/, ".csv"), toCSV(csvRows));
console.log(`Wrote ${a.out} (${tests} tests)`);
