"""Figures for the paper, drawn from the result folders (needs Python 3 with matplotlib).

    python eval/make_figures.py                      uses the run folders listed below
    python eval/make_figures.py --out eval/results/figures

Every number plotted is read from a summary.csv / threshold.csv written by the experiment scripts.
Series are told apart by colour AND marker AND line style, so the figures also work in grayscale print.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import os

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RES = os.path.join(HERE, "results")
RUNS = {
    "gate": os.path.join(RES, "gate-sim", "v2-20261013"),
    "gate_fix": os.path.join(RES, "gate-sim", "v2-20261013-extract-nomin"),
    "retrieval": os.path.join(RES, "retrieval", "v2-20261013"),
    "reach": os.path.join(RES, "reachability", "v3-20261014"),
}

# reference categorical palette (validated: adjacent CVD dE >= 9.1, normal-vision >= 22.9 on #fcfcfb)
C = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100"]
INK, INK2, GRID, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df", "#fcfcfb"
POLICY = {  # label, colour, marker, line style
    "append": ("append-only", C[0], "s", (0, (1, 1.5))),
    "auto": ("auto-apply", C[1], "o", "-"),
    "gate": ("gate changes (AURA)", C[2], "^", "--"),
    "gateAll": ("gate all", C[3], "D", "-."),
}

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.serif": ["Times New Roman", "Times", "STIXGeneral", "DejaVu Serif"],
    "mathtext.fontset": "stix",
    "font.size": 8,
    "axes.titlesize": 8.5,
    "axes.labelsize": 8,
    "xtick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "ytick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "legend.fontsize": 7,
    "axes.edgecolor": INK2,
    "axes.labelcolor": INK,
    "xtick.color": INK2,
    "ytick.color": INK2,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.6,
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "savefig.dpi": 300,
})


def read(path):
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))


def style(ax):
    ax.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)


def save(fig, out, name):
    for ext in ("pdf", "png"):
        fig.savefig(os.path.join(out, f"{name}.{ext}"), bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    print("wrote", name)


def fig_policies(out):
    """Fig. 1: F1, true facts destroyed, review prompts vs. extractor error rate."""
    rows = [r for r in read(os.path.join(RUNS["gate"], "summary.csv")) if r["sweep"] == "error"]
    es = sorted({float(r["e"]) for r in rows})
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7.16, 2.15))
    panels = [
        ("f1_mean", "f1_ci95", "F1 of the final memory", "(a) Memory accuracy"),
        ("destroyed", None, "true facts destroyed / persona", "(b) Wrong changes that got through"),
        ("promptsPer100Turns_mean", "promptsPer100Turns_ci95", "review prompts / 100 turns", "(c) User burden"),
    ]
    for ax, (key, ci, ylabel, title) in zip(axes, panels):
        for p, (label, col, mk, ls) in POLICY.items():
            sel = sorted((r for r in rows if r["policy"] == p), key=lambda r: float(r["e"]))
            if key == "destroyed":
                ys = [float(r["destroyed_mean"]) + float(r["fillerLost_mean"]) for r in sel]
            else:
                ys = [float(r[key]) for r in sel]
            ax.plot(es, ys, color=col, marker=mk, markersize=4, linestyle=ls, linewidth=1.4, label=label,
                    markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.6)
            if ci:
                lo = [y - float(r[ci]) for y, r in zip(ys, sel)]
                hi = [y + float(r[ci]) for y, r in zip(ys, sel)]
                ax.fill_between(es, lo, hi, color=col, alpha=0.12, linewidth=0)
        ax.set_xlabel("extractor error rate $e$")
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=INK)
        ax.set_xticks(es)
        style(ax)
    axes[0].set_ylim(0.45, 1.0)
    axes[1].set_ylim(bottom=0)
    axes[2].set_ylim(bottom=0)
    handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="upper center", ncol=4, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.08), labelcolor=INK)
    fig.tight_layout(w_pad=1.2)
    save(fig, out, "fig1_policies")


def fig_fix(out):
    """Fig. 2: stale facts left active, AURA as shipped vs. candidate selection without the minimum score."""
    base = [r for r in read(os.path.join(RUNS["gate"], "summary.csv")) if r["sweep"] == "error"]
    fix = [r for r in read(os.path.join(RUNS["gate_fix"], "summary.csv")) if r["sweep"] == "error"]
    es = sorted({float(r["e"]) for r in base})
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.3))
    for p, col, mk in (("auto", C[1], "o"), ("gate", C[2], "^")):
        for rows, ls, tag in ((base, "--", "as shipped"), (fix, "-", "no min. score")):
            sel = sorted((r for r in rows if r["policy"] == p), key=lambda r: float(r["e"]))
            ys = [float(r["stale_mean"]) for r in sel]
            ci = [float(r["stale_ci95"]) for r in sel]
            ax.errorbar(es, ys, yerr=ci, color=col, marker=mk, markersize=4, linestyle=ls, linewidth=1.3, capsize=2,
                        elinewidth=0.7, markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.6, label=f"{POLICY[p][0]}, {tag}")
            ax.annotate(f"{POLICY[p][0].split(' (')[0]}, {tag}", (es[-1], ys[-1]), xytext=(4, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                        va="center", fontsize=6.5, color=INK2)
    ax.set_xlabel("extractor error rate $e$")
    ax.set_ylabel("stale facts still active / persona")
    ax.set_xticks(es)
    ax.set_xlim(es[0] - 0.01, es[-1] + 0.16)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    style(ax)
    # every line carries a direct label at its end; colour = policy, dashed = as shipped, solid = no minimum score
    fig.tight_layout()
    save(fig, out, "fig2_candidate_fix")


def fig_reach(out):
    """Fig. 3: share of change requests whose target memory is shown to the extractor."""
    rows = [r for r in read(os.path.join(RUNS["reach"], "summary.csv")) if r["kind"] == "all"]
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: float(r["size"]))
    ns = [float(r["size"]) for r in rows]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.2))
    series = (
        ("reachable", "lo", "hi", "AURA (search min. score 0.25)", C[1], "o", "--"),
        ("reachableNoMin", "lo2", "hi2", "12 best matches, no minimum", C[0], "s", "-"),
    )
    for key, lo, hi, label, col, mk, ls in series:
        ys = [float(r[key]) for r in rows]
        ax.plot(ns, ys, color=col, marker=mk, markersize=4, linestyle=ls, linewidth=1.4, label=label,
                markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.6)
        ax.fill_between(ns, [float(r[lo]) for r in rows], [float(r[hi]) for r in rows], color=col, alpha=0.15, linewidth=0)
        ax.annotate(f"{ys[-1]:.2f}", (ns[-1], ys[-1]), xytext=(4, 0), textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=7, color=INK)
    ax.set_xlabel("unrelated memories in the store $N$")
    ax.set_ylabel("change target shown to extractor")
    ax.set_ylim(0.5, 1.02)
    ax.set_xlim(-10, max(ns) + 40)
    style(ax)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="lower left", labelcolor=INK)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save(fig, out, "fig3_reachability")


def fig_threshold(out):
    """Fig. 4: retrieval trade-off of the minimum score: found (stored facts) vs. noise (never-stated questions)."""
    rows = read(os.path.join(RUNS["retrieval"], "threshold.csv"))
    sizes = sorted({float(r["size"]) for r in rows})
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.4))
    marks = ["o", "s", "^"]
    styles = ["-", "--", "-."]
    for i, n in enumerate(sizes):
        sel = sorted((r for r in rows if float(r["size"]) == n), key=lambda r: float(r["threshold"]))
        xs = [float(r["noise"]) for r in sel]
        ys = [float(r["found"]) for r in sel]
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=C[i], marker=marks[i], markersize=4, linestyle=styles[i], linewidth=1.3,
                label=f"$N$ = {int(n)}", markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.6)
        for r, x, y in zip(sel, xs, ys):
            t = float(r["threshold"])
            if t == 0.25:
                ax.scatter([x], [y], s=55, facecolors="none", edgecolors=INK, linewidths=0.8, zorder=5)
            if i == len(sizes) - 1:
                # the points for 0 and 0.1 are close together: put the 0 label to the right of its point
                ax.annotate(f"{t:g}", (x, y), xytext=(5, -2) if t == 0 else (3, -8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=6, color=INK2)
    ax.set_xlabel("noise: never-stated questions that return memories")
    ax.set_ylabel("found: right fact in top 6")
    ax.set_xlim(-0.02, 1.07)
    ax.set_ylim(0.45, 1.02)
    style(ax)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0), ncol=3, labelcolor=INK)
    ax.text(0.99, 0.03, "numbers: minimum score ($N$ = 350); circled: AURA's 0.25", transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=6.3, color=INK2)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save(fig, out, "fig4_threshold_tradeoff")


def fig_ablation(out):
    """Gate policy, error sweep: stale facts and prompts per 100 turns for baseline, +F1, +F2, both (paired runs in results/ablation)."""
    base = os.path.join(RES, "ablation")
    names = [("baseline", "baseline"), ("f1", "+F1"), ("f2", "+F2"), ("both", "F1 + F2")]
    if not all(os.path.exists(os.path.join(base, d, "summary.csv")) for d, _ in names):
        return
    data = {}
    for d, _ in names:
        for r in read(os.path.join(base, d, "summary.csv")):
            if r["sweep"] == "error" and r["policy"] == "gate":
                data[(d, float(r["e"]))] = r
    es = sorted({e for (_, e) in data})
    marks, styles = ["o", "s", "^", "D"], ["-", "--", "-.", ":"]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.6, 2.6))
    for ax, key, lab in ((axes[0], "stale", "stale facts per persona"), (axes[1], "promptsPer100Turns", "review prompts per 100 turns")):
        for i, (d, nm) in enumerate(names):
            ys = [float(data[(d, e)][key + "_mean"]) for e in es]
            cs = [float(data[(d, e)][key + "_ci95"]) for e in es]
            ax.errorbar(es, ys, yerr=cs, color=C[i], marker=marks[i], linestyle=styles[i], linewidth=1.2, markersize=4, capsize=2, label=nm)
        ax.set_xlabel("extractor error rate $e$")
        ax.set_ylabel(lab)
        ax.set_xticks(es)
        style(ax)
    axes[1].legend(frameon=False, loc="lower right", labelcolor=INK)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save(fig, out, "fig5_ablation")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(RES, "figures"))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    fig_policies(args.out)
    fig_fix(args.out)
    fig_reach(args.out)
    fig_threshold(args.out)
    fig_ablation(args.out)

"""Builds every table (LaTeX fragments), in-text number macros and the two real-run figures of the paper
from the experiment result folders. Nothing in the paper's results is typed by hand.

    python eval/make_paper_assets.py --root eval --out paper

--root is the eval folder (contains results/, ABLATION*.csv, ABLATION-LME.md).  Needs Python 3 + matplotlib.
"""
import argparse, csv, json, math, os, re
from collections import defaultdict

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--root", default="eval")
ap.add_argument("--out", default="paper")
ap.add_argument("--gate", default="gate-sim/v2-20261013")
ap.add_argument("--reach", default="reachability/v3-20261014")
args = ap.parse_args()
R = os.path.join(args.root, "results")
OUT = args.out
os.makedirs(os.path.join(OUT, "tables"), exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(OUT, "figures"), exist_ok=True)


def read_csv(p):
    with open(p, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))


def read_jsonl(p):
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return [json.loads(l) for l in f if l.strip()]


def mean(x):
    x = list(x)
    return sum(x) / len(x) if x else float("nan")


def sign_p(b, c):
    n = b + c
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    lo = min(b, c)
    s, t = 0.0, 1.0
    for i in range(lo + 1):
        s += t
        t = t * (n - i) / (i + 1)
    return min(1.0, 2 * s / 2 ** n)


def pf(p):
    return "\\ensuremath{<}0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p + 1e-9:.3f}"


def f3(x, d=3):
    return f"{x:.{d}f}"


def sd(x, d=3):  # signed difference
    return f"{x:+.{d}f}".replace("-", "$-$")


def tex(name, body):
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "tables", name + ".tex"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(body)


MACROS = {}


def macro(name, val):
    MACROS[name] = val

gs = read_csv(os.path.join(R, args.gate, "summary.csv"))
POL = [("append", "append-only"), ("auto", "auto-apply"), ("gate", "gate changes"), ("gateAll", "gate all")]
rows = []
for e in ("0", "0.1", "0.3"):
    for i, (p, lab) in enumerate(POL):
        r = next(x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == p and x["e"] == e)
        destroyed = float(r["destroyed_mean"]) + float(r["fillerLost_mean"])
        rows.append(
            (f"{e}" if i == 0 else "", lab, f"{float(r['f1_mean']):.3f} $\\pm$ {float(r['f1_ci95']):.3f}",
             f3(float(r["stale_mean"]), 2), f3(float(r["falseMem_mean"]), 2), f3(destroyed, 2),
             f3(float(r["promptsPer100Turns_mean"]), 1))
        )
        macro(f"sim{p}E{e.replace('.', '')}Destroyed", f3(destroyed, 2))
    rows.append(None)
body = "\\begin{tabular}{llccccc}\n\\toprule\n$e$ & policy & F1 & stale & false & destroyed & prompts/100 \\\\\n\\midrule\n"

    body += "\\addlinespace[2pt]\n" if r is None else " & ".join(r) + " \\\\\n"

n_personas = next(x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error")["n"]

# destroyed reduction, gate vs auto, over the error sweep
red = []
for e in ("0.05", "0.1", "0.2", "0.3"):
    a = next(x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == "auto" and x["e"] == e)
    g = next(x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == "gate" and x["e"] == e)
    da = float(a["destroyed_mean"]) + float(a["fillerLost_mean"])
    dg = float(g["destroyed_mean"]) + float(g["fillerLost_mean"])
    red.append(1 - dg / da)
    macro(f"autoDestroyedE{e.replace('.', '')}", f3(da, 2))
    macro(f"gateDestroyedE{e.replace('.', '')}", f3(dg, 2))
macro("destroyRedMin", f"{100 * min(red):.0f}")
macro("destroyRedMax", f"{100 * max(red):.0f}")
g0 = [float(x["promptsPer100Turns_mean"]) for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == "gate"]
macro("gatePromptsMin", f"{min(g0):.0f}")
macro("gatePromptsMax", f"{max(g0):.0f}")
ga = [float(x["promptsPer100Turns_mean"]) for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == "gateAll"]
macro("gateAllRatio", f"{mean(ga) / mean(g0):.1f}")
macro("appendStaleEZero", f3(float(next(x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == "append" and x["e"] == "0")["stale_mean"]), 2))

rows = []
for r in sorted((x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "user" and x["policy"] == "gate"), key=lambda x: float(x["u"])):

                 f3(float(r["wrongChangesApplied_mean"]), 2), f3(float(r["promptsPer100Turns_mean"]), 1)))

    return next(x for x in ab if x["variant"] == variant and x["policy"] == "gate" and x["sweep"] == sweep
                and x["e"] == e and x["metric"] == metric and (u is None or float(x["u"]) == u))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Real Gemini runs
def real_runs(folder, variants):
    d = {}
    for v in variants:
        d[v] = read_jsonl(os.path.join(R, folder, v, "runs.jsonl"))
    return d


def real_csv(path):
    return read_csv(path)


def table_real(folder, csvname, variants, labels, name, model):
    runs = real_runs(folder, variants)
    cs = real_csv(os.path.join(args.root, csvname))
    body = "\\begin{tabular}{llccccc}\n\\toprule\npolicy & variant & F1 & stale & false & prompts/100 & prompt tokens ($\\times10^3$) \\\\\n\\midrule\n"
    for pol in ("auto", "gate"):
        for v, lab in zip(variants, labels):
            rr = [r for r in runs[v] if r["policy"] == pol]
            cell = lambda m, d=3: mean(r[m] for r in rr)

            def pv(metric, fmt, dd):
                if v == "baseline":
                    return fmt(cell(metric))
                row = next(x for x in cs if x["variant"] == v and x["policy"] == pol and x["metric"] == metric)
                return f"{fmt(cell(metric))} ({sd(float(row['diff']), dd)}, {pf(float(row['signP']))})"
            body += (f"{pol if v == variants[0] else ''} & {lab} & {pv('f1', lambda x: f3(x), 3)} & {pv('stale', lambda x: f3(x, 2), 2)} & "
                     f"{pv('falseMem', lambda x: f3(x, 2), 2)} & {f3(cell('promptsPer100Turns'), 1)} & {cell('promptTokens') / 1000:.1f} \\\\\n")
        body += "\\addlinespace[2pt]\n"
    body = body.removesuffix("\\addlinespace[2pt]\n") + "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n"
    tex(name, body)
    return runs, cs


V4 = ["baseline", "f1", "f2", "both"]
L4 = ["baseline", "+F1", "+F2", "F1+F2"]
runs1, cs1 = table_real("real-ablation", "ABLATION-REAL.csv", V4, L4, "real1", "m1")
runs2, cs2 = table_real("real-ablation-m2", "ABLATION-REAL-M2.csv", ["baseline", "both"], ["baseline", "F1+F2"], "real2", "m2")


def rget(cs, v, pol, metric):
    return next(x for x in cs if x["variant"] == v and x["policy"] == pol and x["metric"] == metric)


for tag, cs, runs in (("A", cs1, runs1), ("B", cs2, runs2)):
    for pol in ("gate", "auto"):
        for m in ("f1", "stale", "promptsPer100Turns", "promptTokens"):
            r = rget(cs, "both", pol, m)
            macro(f"real{tag}{pol}{m}Base", f3(float(r["base"]), 3 if m == "f1" else 2 if m == "stale" else 1 if m == "promptsPer100Turns" else 0))
            macro(f"real{tag}{pol}{m}Both", f3(float(r["variantMean"]), 3 if m == "f1" else 2 if m == "stale" else 1 if m == "promptsPer100Turns" else 0))
            macro(f"real{tag}{pol}{m}Diff", sd(float(r["diff"]), 3 if m == "f1" else 2 if m == "stale" else 1 if m == "promptsPer100Turns" else 0))
            macro(f"real{tag}{pol}{m}P", pf(float(r["signP"])))
            if m != "promptTokens":
                macro(f"real{tag}{pol}{m}Lo", f3(float(r["lo"]), 3 if m == "f1" else 2))
                macro(f"real{tag}{pol}{m}Hi", f3(float(r["hi"]), 3 if m == "f1" else 2))

    for v in ("f1", "f2"):
        r = rget(cs1, v, "gate", m)
        macro(f"realAgate{m}{v}Val", f3(float(r["variantMean"]), 3 if m == "f1" else 2))
        macro(f"realAgate{m}{v}P", pf(float(r["signP"])))

macro("realTests", str(len(cs1) + len(cs2)))
macro("realPairs", rget(cs1, "both", "gate", "f1")["pairs"])
errs = sum(r["extractionErrors"] for rs_ in list(runs1.values()) + list(runs2.values()) for r in rs_)
macro("realExtractionErrors", str(errs))
macro("realExtractions", str(sum(r["extractions"] for rs_ in list(runs1.values()) + list(runs2.values()) for r in rs_)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Agreement
def agreement(path):
    t = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    m = re.search(r"(\d+) labelled rows; agreement (\d+) \(([\d.]+)\); Cohen's kappa (\d\.\d+)", t)
    return m.groups()

    body += f"{lab} & {a[0]} & {a[1]} & {a[2]} & {a[3]} \\\\\n"
body += "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n"

def style(ax):
    ax.grid(True, axis="y", color=GRID, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)


def save(fig, name):
    for ext in ("pdf", "png"):
        fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, "figures", f"{name}.{ext}"), bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)


def boot_ci(vals, B=4000, seed=7):
    import random
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    n = len(vals)
    ms = sorted(sum(vals[rnd.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(B))
    return ms[int(0.025 * B)], ms[int(0.975 * B) - 1]


# Fig. 6: real Gemini, gate policy: F1 and stale facts per variant, two models (per-persona dots + mean)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.16, 2.4))
marks = ["o", "s", "^", "D"]
for ax, (metric, ylab, title) in zip(axes, (("f1", "F1 of the final memory", "(a) Accuracy"), ("stale", "stale facts / persona", "(b) Updates that were missed"))):
    for mi, (runs, vs, col, shift, lab) in enumerate(((runs1, V4, C[0], -0.12, "gemini-3.5-flash-lite"),
                                                      (runs2, ["baseline", "both"], C[1], 0.12, "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"))):
        xs, ms, los, his = [], [], [], []
        for v in vs:
            vals = [r[metric] for r in runs[v] if r["policy"] == "gate"]
            lo_, hi_ = boot_ci(vals)
            xs.append(V4.index(v) + shift); ms.append(mean(vals)); los.append(mean(vals) - lo_); his.append(hi_ - mean(vals))
        ax.errorbar(xs, ms, yerr=[los, his], color=col, marker=marks[mi], markersize=5, linestyle="--" if mi else "-",
                    linewidth=1.3, capsize=2, elinewidth=0.8, markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.6, label=lab)
    ax.set_xticks(range(4)); ax.set_xticklabels(L4)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylab); ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=INK)
    if metric == "stale":
        ax.set_ylim(bottom=-0.05)
    style(ax)
axes[0].legend(frameon=False, loc="lower right", labelcolor=INK)
fig.tight_layout(w_pad=1.5)
save(fig, "fig6_real")

# Fig. 7: LongMemEval accuracy per system, baseline vs F1+F2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.3))
w = 0.38
for k, (runs, col, lab, hatch) in enumerate(((lb, C[0], "baseline", ""), (lo, C[1], "F1+F2", "//"))):
    ys, cil, cih = [], [], []
    for p, _ in SYS:
        vals = [r["judged"] for r in runs if r["policy"] == p]
        m = mean(vals)
        se = 1.96 * math.sqrt(m * (1 - m) / len(vals))
        ys.append(m); cil.append(min(se, m)); cih.append(min(se, 1 - m))
    ax.bar([i + (k - 0.5) * w for i in range(len(SYS))], ys, w, yerr=[cil, cih], color=col, hatch=hatch, edgecolor="white",
           label=lab, capsize=1.5, error_kw={"elinewidth": 0.7})
ax.set_xticks(range(len(SYS)))
ax.set_xticklabels(["no\nmemory", "full\ncontext", "append", "auto", "gate"])
ax.set_ylabel("answers judged correct")
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
style(ax)
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", labelcolor=INK, ncol=2)
fig.tight_layout()
save(fig, "fig7_lme")

# ---- worked example: persona 1, gate, baseline vs. F1+F2
def load_mem(v, pol, persona):
    for l in open(os.path.join(R, "real-ablation", v, "memories.jsonl"), encoding="utf-8"):
        r = json.loads(l)
        if r["policy"] == pol and r["persona"] == persona:
            return r["memories"]
def load_dec(v, pol, persona):
    return [json.loads(l) for l in open(os.path.join(R, "real-ablation", v, "decisions.jsonl"), encoding="utf-8") if json.loads(l)["policy"] == pol and json.loads(l)["persona"] == persona]
def esc(t):
    return t.replace("\\", "").replace("&", "\\&").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_").replace("#", "\\#")
guide = open(os.path.join(R, "real-ablation", "baseline", "annotation-guide.md"), encoding="utf-8").read()
blk = guide.split("## Persona 1-1")[1].split("## Persona")[0].strip().split("\n")
sess = [l for l in blk if l.startswith("Session")]
truth = [l for l in blk if l.startswith("Truth")][0]
ex = "{\\small\n\\begin{itemize}\\setlength\\itemsep{0pt}\n"
for l in sess:
    ex += "\\item " + esc(l.replace('"', "'")) + "\n"
ex += "\\item " + esc(truth.replace('"', "'")) + "\n\\end{itemize}}\n"
tex("example_persona", ex)
def memtable(v):
    out = ""
    for m in load_mem(v, "gate", 1):
        if m["id"] and not m["content"].startswith("The user's friend") and m["judged"] != "filler":
            out += f"{m['status']} & {m['judged']} & {esc(m['content'])} \\\\\n"
    return out
for v, nm in (("baseline", "example_base"), ("both", "example_both")):
    body = "\\begin{tabular}{llp{0.62\\linewidth}}\n\\toprule\nstatus & scored as & memory text \\\\\n\\midrule\n" + memtable(v) + "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n"
    tex(nm, body)
def dectable(v):
    out = ""
    for d in load_dec(v, "gate", 1):
        out += f"{d['session']} & {d['action']} & {esc(d['current'] or '')} $\\rightarrow$ {esc(d['content'] or '(removed)')} & {'yes' if d['accepted'] else 'no'} \\\\\n"
    return out
for v, nm in (("baseline", "dec_base"), ("both", "dec_both")):
    body = "\\begin{tabular}{llp{0.55\\linewidth}l}\n\\toprule\nsession & action & proposal & accepted \\\\\n\\midrule\n" + dectable(v) + "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n"
    tex(nm, body)

# ---- appendix: full policy table (all error rates) and full simulated ablation
body = "\\begin{tabular}{llccccccc}\n\\toprule\n$e$ & policy & F1 & precision & recall & stale & false & destroyed & wrong applied & prompts/100 \\\\\n\\midrule\n".replace("ccccccc}", "cccccccc}")
for e in ("0", "0.05", "0.1", "0.2", "0.3"):
    for i, (p, lab) in enumerate(POL):
        r = next(x for x in gs if x["sweep"] == "error" and x["policy"] == p and x["e"] == e)
        d = float(r["destroyed_mean"]) + float(r["fillerLost_mean"])
        body += (f"{e if i == 0 else ''} & {lab} & {float(r['f1_mean']):.3f} & {float(r['precision_mean']):.3f} & {float(r['recall_mean']):.3f} & {float(r['stale_mean']):.2f} & "
                 f"{float(r['falseMem_mean']):.2f} & {d:.2f} & {float(r['wrongChangesApplied_mean']):.2f} & {float(r['promptsPer100Turns_mean']):.1f} \\\\\n")
    body += "\\addlinespace[2pt]\n"
body = body.removesuffix("\\addlinespace[2pt]\n") + "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n"
tex("app_policies", body)

def abl_rows(policy):
    out = ""
    cells = [("error", "0", "0.05"), ("error", "0.1", "0.05"), ("error", "0.2", "0.05"), ("user", "0.1", "0"), ("user", "0.1", "0.1"), ("user", "0.1", "0.2"), ("user", "0.1", "0.3")]
    if policy == "auto":
        cells = cells[:3]
    def get(v, sw, e, u, m):
        return next(x for x in ab if x["variant"] == v and x["policy"] == policy and x["sweep"] == sw and x["e"] == e and float(x["u"]) == float(u) and x["metric"] == m)
    for sw, e, u in cells:
        base = {m: float(get("f1", sw, e, u, m)["base"]) for m in ("f1", "stale", "falseMem", "promptsPer100Turns", "exactState")}
        out += f"{e} & {u} & baseline & {base['f1']:.3f} & {base['stale']:.2f} & {base['falseMem']:.2f} & {base['exactState']:.3f} & {base['promptsPer100Turns']:.1f} \\\\\n"
        for v, lab in VAR[1:]:
            vals = {m: get(v, sw, e, u, m) for m in base}
            def cell(m, d, tag=False):
                x = vals[m]
                return f"{float(x['variantMean']):.{d}f}" + (f"\\textsuperscript{{*}}" if float(x["signP"]) < 0.05 and tag else "")
            out += (f" & & {lab} & {cell('f1', 3, True)} & {cell('stale', 2, True)} & {cell('falseMem', 2, True)} & {cell('exactState', 3, True)} & {cell('promptsPer100Turns', 1, True)} \\\\\n")
        out += "\\addlinespace[2pt]\n"
    return out.removesuffix("\\addlinespace[2pt]\n")
for pol in ("gate", "auto"):
    body = "\\begin{tabular}{cclccccc}\n\\toprule\n$e$ & $u$ & variant & F1 & stale & false & exact state & prompts/100 \\\\\n\\midrule\n" + abl_rows(pol) + "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n"
    tex(f"app_abl_{pol}", body)

# ---- figure 8: reachability by fact type (N = 350, single sentence)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.16, 2.3))
keys = [k for k, _ in SLOTS if k in slotrows]
labs = dict(SLOTS)
w = 0.2
for i, (m, mlab, col) in enumerate(zip(MODES, ("default", "no minimum", "sentence", "adaptive (F2)"), (C[1], C[0], C[3], C[2]))):

// Re-scores a finished real-Gemini run from its saved memories, with the current eval/lib/loose.mjs,
// and prepares (or reads back) a sheet for checking the automatic labels by hand.
// No database and no Gemini requests.
//
//   npm run eval:rescore -- <run folder>
//
// Writes into the run folder:
//   rescored.md / rescored.csv   the summary with the current scoring rules
//   annotation.csv               one row per memory the assistant still believes (status active);
//                                fill in human_label (created once; never overwritten)
//   annotation-guide.md          what each user said, the truth at the end, and the label definitions
// Once human_label is filled in for some rows, it also reports agreement (Cohen's kappa).
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { makePersona, isFiller, SLOT } from "./lib/scenarios.mjs";
import { classify, mentions } from "./lib/loose.mjs";
import { mean, ci95, fmt, toCSV, mdTable, parseCSV } from "./lib/stats.mjs";

const dir = process.argv[2];
if (!dir || !fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, "memories.jsonl"))) {
  console.log("Usage: npm run eval:rescore -- <folder of a real-gemini run, containing memories.jsonl>");
  process.exit(1);
}
const read = (f) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), "utf8").split("\n").filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
const cfg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, "config.json"), "utf8"));
const runs = read("runs.jsonl");
const mems = read("memories.jsonl");
const LABELS = ["true", "ended", "stale", "false", "hypothetical", "third-party", "other"];

// ---- re-score ----
const rows = [];
const annot = [];
for (const m of mems) {
  const persona = makePersona(m.seed, m.persona);
  const gold = persona.finalGold;
  const run = runs.find((r) => r.policy === m.policy && r.seed === m.seed && r.persona === m.persona) || {};
  const active = m.memories.filter((x) => x.status === "active" && !isFiller(x.content));
  const cls = active.map((x) => classify(x.content, gold));
  const n = (c) => cls.filter((x) => x === c).length;
  const goldPairs = [...gold.state].filter(([, v]) => v != null);
  const correct = goldPairs.filter(([k, v]) => active.some((x) => mentions(x.content).some((mm) => mm.slot === k && mm.value === v))).length;
  const scored = n("true") + n("ended") + n("stale") + n("false") + n("hypothetical");
  const precision = scored ? (n("true") + n("ended")) / scored : 1;
  const recall = goldPairs.length ? correct / goldPairs.length : 1;
  const destroyed = m.memories.filter((x) => x.status !== "active" && ["true"].includes(classify(x.content, gold))).length;
  rows.push({
    policy: m.policy, seed: m.seed, persona: m.persona,
    goldFacts: goldPairs.length, correct, precision, recall, f1: precision + recall ? (2 * precision * recall) / (precision + recall) : 0,
    true: n("true"), ended: n("ended"), stale: n("stale"), false: n("false"), hypothetical: n("hypothetical"), thirdParty: n("third-party"), other: n("other"),
    destroyed,
    prompts: run.prompts ?? null, userTurns: run.userTurns ?? null,
    proposalsJudgedRightDuringRun: run.correctAccepted + run.correctRejected, proposalsJudgedWrongDuringRun: run.wrongAccepted + run.wrongRejected,
    requests: run.requests ?? null, promptTokens: run.promptTokens ?? null, outputTokens: run.outputTokens ?? null, meanLatencyMs: run.meanLatencyMs ?? null,
  });
  active.forEach((x, i) => annot.push({ run: `${m.policy}-${m.seed}-${m.persona}`, policy: m.policy, seed: m.seed, persona: m.persona, memory_id: x.id, content: x.content, auto_label: cls[i], human_label: "", notes: "" }));
}
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "rescored.csv"), toCSV(rows));
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "rescored.jsonl"), rows.map((r) => JSON.stringify(r)).join("\n") + "\n");
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "labels.jsonl"), annot.map((r) => JSON.stringify({ run: r.run, policy: r.policy, memory_id: r.memory_id, content: r.content, auto_label: r.auto_label })).join("\n") + "\n");

const policies = [...new Set(rows.map((r) => r.policy))];
const md = [];
md.push(`# Re-scored: ${cfg.extractor}, ${cfg.personas} personas x ${cfg.seeds} seed(s), candidate selection ${cfg.extractMinScore}`);
md.push(``);
md.push(`Scoring rules of ${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)} (eval/lib/loose.mjs): precision = (true + ended) / (true + ended + stale + false + hypothetical); ` +
  `third-party and other are not counted. Destroyed = a memory that is still true but no longer active.`);
md.push(``);
md.push(mdTable(
  ["policy", "n", "F1", "precision", "recall", "ended", "stale", "false", "hypothetical", "third-party", "destroyed", "prompts / 100 turns", "cards judged right / wrong during the run"],
  policies.map((p) => {
    const sel = rows.filter((r) => r.policy === p);
    const s = (k) => sel.reduce((t, r) => t + (r[k] || 0), 0);
    return [p, sel.length, `${fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.f1)))} Â± ${fmt(ci95(sel.map((r) => r.f1)))}`, fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.precision))), fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.recall))),
      fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.ended)), 2), fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.stale)), 2), fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.false)), 2), fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.hypothetical)), 2), fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => r.thirdParty)), 2),
      s("destroyed"), fmt(mean(sel.map((r) => (100 * r.prompts) / r.userTurns)), 1), `${s("proposalsJudgedRightDuringRun")} / ${s("proposalsJudgedWrongDuringRun")}`];
  })
));
md.push(``);
const wrongCards = rows.reduce((t, r) => t + r.proposalsJudgedWrongDuringRun, 0);
if (wrongCards) {
  md.push(`Note: the simulated user decided the review cards during the run with the scoring rules in place at that time. ` +
    `${wrongCards} card(s) were judged wrong then; if the current rules would accept them, the gate result is pessimistic until the run is repeated.`);
  md.push(``);
}
md.push(`Active memories that are not plainly true:`);
md.push(``);
for (const a of annot.filter((x) => x.auto_label !== "true")) md.push(`- ${a.run}: [${a.auto_label}] ${a.content}`);
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "rescored.md"), md.join("\n") + "\n");

// ---- annotation sheet (created once, never overwritten) ----
const sheet = path.join(dir, "annotation.csv");
if (!fs.existsSync(sheet)) {
  fs.writeFileSync(sheet, toCSV(annot));
  const guide = [];
  guide.push(`# Checking the automatic labels by hand`);
  guide.push(``);
  guide.push(`Open annotation.csv. For each row, read the memory, look up that persona below, and write one label in human_label ` +
    `(without looking at auto_label first if you can). Ideally a second person labels a copy independently.`);
  guide.push(``);
  guide.push(`| label | use when the memory... |`);
  guide.push(`|---|---|`);
  guide.push(`| true | states something that is true about the user at the end |`);
  guide.push(`| ended | correctly says that a fact the user retired is over ("finished the Lotus project") |`);
  guide.push(`| stale | states something the user said earlier that is no longer true, or something the user asked to forget |`);
  guide.push(`| false | states something the user never said about themselves (misread, invented) |`);
  guide.push(`| hypothetical | keeps a hypothetical or a maybe as a memory ("if the user had a cat...") |`);
  guide.push(`| third-party | is a fact about someone else the user mentioned (allowed) |`);
  guide.push(`| other | none of the above (write why in notes) |`);
  guide.push(``);
  for (const key of [...new Set(mems.map((m) => `${m.seed}-${m.persona}`))]) {
    const [seed, idx] = key.split("-").map(Number);
    const p = makePersona(seed, idx);
    guide.push(`## Persona ${key}`);
    guide.push(``);
    p.sessions.forEach((turns, s) => {
      guide.push(`Session ${s + 1}: ` + turns.map((t) => (t.assistantFirst ? `(AURA: "${t.assistantFirst}") ` : "") + `"${t.user}"`).join(" "));
    });
    guide.push(``);
    const truth = [...p.finalGold.state].map(([k, v]) => (v == null ? `${k}: no longer true` : `${k}: ${v}`));
    guide.push(`Truth at the end: ${truth.join("; ")}.` + (p.finalGold.forgotten.length ? ` Asked to forget: ${p.finalGold.forgotten.map((f) => `${f.slot} (${f.value})`).join(", ")}.` : ""));
    guide.push(``);
  }
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "annotation-guide.md"), guide.join("\n") + "\n");
}

// ---- agreement, once labels are filled in ----
// Excel turns the word "true" into TRUE when a CSV is saved, so both columns are compared in lower case
const labelled = parseCSV(fs.readFileSync(sheet, "utf8")).map((r) => ({ ...r, auto_label: String(r.auto_label ?? "").trim().toLowerCase() })).filter((r) => r.human_label.trim());
if (labelled.length) {
  const norm = (s) => s.trim().toLowerCase();
  const agree = labelled.filter((r) => norm(r.human_label) === r.auto_label).length;
  const po = agree / labelled.length;
  const pe = LABELS.reduce((t, l) => t + (labelled.filter((r) => norm(r.human_label) === l).length / labelled.length) * (labelled.filter((r) => r.auto_label === l).length / labelled.length), 0);
  const kappa = pe < 1 ? (po - pe) / (1 - pe) : 1;
  const lines = [`# Human vs. automatic labels`, ``, `${labelled.length} labelled rows; agreement ${agree} (${fmt(po)}); Cohen's kappa ${fmt(kappa)}.`, ``, `Disagreements:`, ``];
  for (const r of labelled.filter((x) => norm(x.human_label) !== x.auto_label)) lines.push(`- ${r.run} #${r.memory_id}: auto ${r.auto_label}, human ${norm(r.human_label)} | ${r.content}${r.notes ? ` (${r.notes})` : ""}`);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "agreement.md"), lines.join("\n") + "\n");
  console.log(`Agreement: ${agree} of ${labelled.length}, kappa ${fmt(kappa)} -> agreement.md`);
}
console.log(`Re-scored ${rows.length} persona runs -> ${path.join(dir, "rescored.md")}`);
console.log(fs.existsSync(sheet) ? `Annotation sheet: ${sheet} (${annot.length} rows)` : "");

# Results: user-controlled memory in AURA (Direction A)

Generated by `npm run eval:results` (eval/build-results.mjs) on 2026-10-15; every number below is computed from the run folders named in each section. Do not edit numbers by hand: re-run the experiment, then this script. How the experiments work: [README.md](README.md).

**Status of the evidence.** Experiments 1-3 use AURA's real memory code, database and local embedding model (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) with a **simulated** extractor and a simulated user: they measure the system's mechanics, not Gemini's judgement. Experiment 4 uses the **real** Gemini extractor (Gemini gemini-3.5-flash-lite) on 4 personas per policy: enough to see which errors a real model makes, too few for firm rates.

## Finding 1: the review gate stops almost all destructive changes, at a cost of 20-33 prompts per 100 turns

`results/gate-sim/v2-20261013/` (n = 60 personas per cell, user slip rate u = 0.05; mean, Â± = 95% CI)

| e | policy | F1 | stale | false | true facts destroyed | prompts / 100 turns | prompt precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | append | 0.597 Â± 0.025 | 5.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.0 | - |
| 0 | auto | 0.881 Â± 0.018 | 1.57 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.0 | - |
| 0 | gate (AURA) | 0.854 Â± 0.022 | 1.80 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 19.5 | 1.00 |
| 0 | gateAll | 0.861 Â± 0.023 | 1.62 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 65.8 | 1.00 |
| 0.05 | append | 0.584 Â± 0.029 | 4.90 | 0.12 | 0.00 | 0.0 | - |
| 0.05 | auto | 0.840 Â± 0.023 | 1.65 | 0.17 | 0.78 | 0.0 | - |
| 0.05 | gate (AURA) | 0.820 Â± 0.023 | 1.90 | 0.12 | 0.05 | 22.2 | 0.82 |
| 0.05 | gateAll | 0.818 Â± 0.028 | 1.82 | 0.00 | 0.03 | 67.3 | 0.93 |
| 0.1 | append | 0.581 Â± 0.023 | 4.58 | 0.33 | 0.00 | 0.0 | - |
| 0.1 | auto | 0.798 Â± 0.026 | 1.68 | 0.43 | 1.60 | 0.0 | - |
| 0.1 | gate (AURA) | 0.797 Â± 0.026 | 1.85 | 0.33 | 0.03 | 24.4 | 0.66 |
| 0.1 | gateAll | 0.795 Â± 0.029 | 1.83 | 0.02 | 0.05 | 69.0 | 0.86 |

| 0.3 | gateAll | 0.707 Â± 0.030 | 1.98 | 0.07 | 0.40 | 77.6 | 0.62 |

- With auto-apply, true facts destroyed grow with the error rate (0.78, 1.60, 2.83, 4.60 per persona at e = 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3). The gate cuts this to 0.05, 0.03, 0.18, 0.25: **94-98% fewer**.
- **F1 hides most of this damage.** F1 counts only the user's own facts; at e = 0.2, auto-apply destroyed 0.10 of the user's facts and 2.73 background facts per persona, because a wrong change hits whatever true memory the extractor was shown, and most shown memories are background ones. Report destroyed facts as the safety metric and F1 next to it.
- The gate does not stop false *new* facts (0.33 vs 0.43 at e = 0.1). Confirming new facts too (gateAll) removes them (0.02) but costs 2.8x the prompts (69.0 vs 24.4 per 100 turns).
- Append-only never destroys anything but leaves every changed fact stale (5.00 per persona at e = 0).

## Finding 2: the gate depends on a careful user, and a mistaken "keep" is never asked again

`results/gate-sim/v2-20261013/`, user sweep at e = 0.1

| u | gate F1 | gate stale | gate wrong changes applied | gateAll F1 | gateAll wrong changes applied |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.808 | 1.75 | 0.02 | 0.828 | 0.02 |
| 0.1 | 0.783 | 2.00 | 0.28 | 0.763 | 0.17 |
| 0.2 | 0.757 | 2.33 | 0.42 | 0.730 | 0.27 |
| 0.3 | 0.732 | 2.52 | 0.62 | 0.669 | 0.57 |

AURA does not propose a change again after the user turns it down (`propose()` in `server/memory.mjs`). That avoids nagging, but one mistaken rejection of a correct update keeps the old fact for good: stale facts rise from 1.75 to 2.52 as u goes from 0 to 0.3. Prompt precision also falls as the extractor gets worse (1.00 at e = 0 to 0.30 at e = 0.3), so users see more wrong cards exactly when the gate matters most.

## Finding 3: 25%-31% of change requests cannot be carried out, because the memory to change is not shown to the extractor

`results/reachability/v3-20261014/` (30 stores per size, 12 fact types, 3 phrasings per change; 95% Wilson intervals)

| unrelated memories N | reachable (AURA) | reachable without the 0.25 minimum |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.898 [0.886, 0.909] | 1.000 [0.999, 1.000] |
| 25 | 0.752 [0.736, 0.769] | 0.990 [0.986, 0.994] |
| 50 | 0.749 [0.732, 0.765] | 0.975 [0.968, 0.980] |
| 100 | 0.727 [0.710, 0.744] | 0.952 [0.944, 0.960] |
| 200 | 0.704 [0.686, 0.721] | 0.934 [0.924, 0.943] |
| 350 | 0.690 [0.672, 0.707] | 0.911 [0.900, 0.922] |

AURA lets the extractor change only memories shown in its prompt: `searchMemories(text, 12)` plus the 8 most recent, and `searchMemories` drops everything scoring below 0.25. Even in a store of only 12 memories, search never retrieved the car fact for "I sold my old car and bought a <new car>." (0 of 60 stores); it was reachable only when it happened to be among the 8 most recent (40 of 60). When the target is missed, the old fact stays active next to the new one. Forget requests are hit hardest (0.649 at N = 350). In Experiment 1 this is the main source of stale facts: 27% of change turns missed their target under the gate at e = 0.

## Finding 4: showing the extractor its 12 best matches without a minimum score removes most stale facts

`results/gate-sim/v2-20261013-extract-nomin/` vs. `results/gate-sim/v2-20261013/` (`--extract-min-score 0`)

| e | policy | F1 as shipped -> fix | stale -> fix | candidate miss rate -> fix | prompts / 100 -> fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | auto | 0.881 -> 0.978 | 1.57 -> 0.22 | 0.272 -> 0.030 | 0.0 -> 0.0 |
| 0 | gate | 0.854 -> 0.941 | 1.80 -> 0.52 | 0.272 -> 0.030 | 19.5 -> 26.1 |
| 0.1 | auto | 0.798 -> 0.854 | 1.68 -> 0.67 | 0.231 -> 0.024 | 0.0 -> 0.0 |
| 0.1 | gate | 0.797 -> 0.857 | 1.85 -> 0.85 | 0.240 -> 0.027 | 24.4 -> 29.6 |
| 0.2 | auto | 0.735 -> 0.774 | 1.73 -> 1.07 | 0.201 -> 0.030 | 0.0 -> 0.0 |
| 0.2 | gate | 0.733 -> 0.771 | 1.98 -> 1.30 | 0.210 -> 0.030 | 28.8 -> 32.0 |

Forget requests whose value is still in a memory row fell from 0.45 to 0.13 per persona (gate, e = 0; 1.67 forget requests per persona). The forgotten value stays in the stored conversation text in every case (1.67 of 1.67): "forget" deletes the memory, not the transcript it came from. The fix costs more review prompts because changes that used to be impossible now reach the user. It is a one-line change (pass `{ minScore: 0 }` from the extractor to `searchMemories`) and is **not** on by default.

## Finding 5: the fixed minimum score in memory search trades recall for noise, and no single cut-off is good

`results/retrieval/v2-20261013/` (726 questions about stored facts and 714 about never-stated ones per store size)

| N | min 0 | min 0.15 | min 0.2 | min 0.25 (AURA) | min 0.3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 0.994 / 1.000 | 0.933 / 0.664 | 0.854 / 0.367 | 0.707 / 0.200 | 0.636 / 0.090 |
| 100 | 0.968 / 1.000 | 0.915 / 0.807 | 0.853 / 0.508 | 0.705 / 0.353 | 0.636 / 0.230 |
| 350 | 0.891 / 1.000 | 0.883 / 0.854 | 0.832 / 0.619 | 0.700 / 0.490 | 0.636 / 0.339 |

Cells: found (right fact in the top 6) / noise (never-stated questions that still return memories). With AURA's 0.25, 28%-29% of questions about a stored fact return **no results at all**, and 29.3% of right answers score below the cut-off; yet at N = 350, 49% of questions about things never stated still return unrelated memories. Keyword-only fallback search: hit@6 0.606. The re-scoring used for the variants reproduced AURA's real `searchMemories()` results in 2178 of 2178 queries. This matters once a user has more than 30 memories; the 30 most recent are always in the Live prompt.

## Finding 6: what the real Gemini extractor gets wrong

`results/real-gemini/20261013-130739/` (Gemini gemini-3.5-flash-lite; 4 personas x 1 seed(s) per policy; u = 0; candidate selection default (0.25); scored with eval/lib/loose.mjs, see rescored.md)

| policy | n | F1 | precision | recall | ended | stale | false | hypothetical | third-party | true facts destroyed | prompts / 100 turns | cards judged right / wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto | 4 | 0.916 Â± 0.027 | 0.846 | 1.000 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.25 | 0.50 | 0.75 | 0 | 0.0 | 0 / 0 |
| gate | 4 | 0.914 Â± 0.063 | 0.846 | 1.000 | 0.00 | 0.75 | 0.00 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0 | 24.6 | 20 / 1 |

- Gemini destroyed **0** true facts in 8 persona runs (170 extraction requests, about 572 input / 39 output tokens each, mean latency 5.2 s). In these scenarios the destructive errors the gate is built for did not occur; its measured benefit here is therefore nil, and the case for it rests on Finding 1 (it is cheap insurance when they do occur).
- Its errors are of two other kinds. **Stale facts** where the old memory was not shown to it (Finding 3), e.g. "The user drives a Seltos.", "The user lives in Bhubaneswar.". **New facts that should not have been stored**, which the gate does not review: hypotheticals ("The user would spend every evening on the beach if they moved to Goa."; "If the user had a cat, they would name her Luna."; "The user would name a hypothetical cat Luna.") and misreadings ("The user wants to move to Goa someday.").
- It also wrote correct memories in forms a strict checker would miss: facts about people in the user's life ("The user's friend Rohan bought a Thar."; "The user's cousin works at Google in Zurich.") and retirements written as updates ("The user finished leading project Lotus last week and is currently between projects as of October 2026."; "The user finished leading the Nimbus project and is currently between projects as of October 2026."). The scoring rules were extended for these after the run (eval/lib/loose.mjs) and re-checked against exact scoring.
- During the run the simulated user turned down 1 review card(s) it judged wrong with the rules in place at the time. Cards were not logged in this run, so which one is not known; a retirement written as an update (above) would have been turned down, so the gate row may be slightly pessimistic until the run is repeated.

## Checks

- Value-based scoring (used for Gemini's wording) vs. exact scoring on simulated runs: 30 of 30 persona runs identical; the two review judges agreed on 208 of 208 decisions (`results/real-scorer-check/v2-20261013/`).
- Retrieval re-scoring vs. AURA's real search: 2178 of 2178 queries identical.
- Consistency: personas average 20.5 user turns, 4 of them distractors. Injected wrong changes per persona (0.82, 1.75, 3.10, 4.97 at e = 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) equal e x 15.5-17.5, as expected (a wrong change is skipped when no true memory is shown). Every review card was correct at e = 0 (prompt precision 1.00).
- Simulation runs use a simulated clock (1 ms per call), so they are exactly repeatable; a repeated slice of Experiment 1 matched the full run field by field.
- `npm run test:server` passes with the instrumentation and the option added.

4. `fig4_threshold_tradeoff`: found vs. noise for each minimum score (Finding 5).

## What the paper can claim, and what it cannot yet

Supported (Experiments 1-3, simulation with AURA's real code):
- Gating changes to existing memories prevents almost all destructive errors (94-98% fewer at e = 0.05-0.3) for 20-33 prompts per 100 turns; gating new facts too costs about 2.8x the prompts.
- F1 over the user's facts understates the harm of auto-applied wrong changes.
- Candidate selection limits what the extractor can change (25%-31% of change requests miss their target with 25-350 other memories), and selecting the 12 best matches without a minimum fixes most of it.
- Not re-asking after a rejection makes the gate sensitive to user mistakes.

Supported by Experiments 5-6 (paired comparisons; see ABLATION.md, ABLATION-REAL.md, ABLATION-REAL-M2.md):
- Showing the extractor more candidates (F2) removes most stale facts: in simulation at every error rate, and with real Gemini on two models (12 personas each; paired, sign test). It costs about a third more prompt tokens and a few more review prompts.
- Hand labels agree with the automatic scoring rules (Cohen's kappa about 0.98 on the two main runs; three disagreements, all retirements written as current facts).

Supported by Experiment 4 (small sample, real Gemini):
- The real extractor's errors are mostly stale facts (unreachable targets) and new facts that should not be stored (hypotheticals, misreadings); it made no destructive changes here.

Not supported yet:
- Rates for Gemini's errors with confidence intervals: needs more personas (Experiment 4 had 4 per policy).
- Anything about real users (burden as felt, trust, time per decision): needs a user study.
- A comparison with Mem0 or other published LongMemEval numbers: AURA was run on 30 knowledge-update questions with one model (Experiment 7), a different protocol from published results; do not put the numbers side by side.
- Any effect of F1 (re-propose) with real Gemini: Experiment 6 shows none; its effect is small and situational even in simulation.
- Effects on LongMemEval: with F1 + F2 the gated system gains questions (see Experiment 7, paired test) but the difference is not significant at 30 questions, and every AURA variant stays below the full-context baseline.
- Novelty of the approval gate: the literature search so far was not exhaustive.

## Limitations

- Personas average 20.5 user turns over 5 sessions; long-term effects over months are extrapolated.
- Scripted personas written by the evaluator: 12 fact types, short third-person facts, English only; paraphrase coverage is limited (3 per change in Experiment 3, 1 per change elsewhere).
- The simulated extractor's errors are independent and uniform; Experiment 4 suggests a real model's errors are concentrated on new facts, not on changes.
- The simulated user reviews at the end of each session, with a fixed slip rate.
- Labels for Gemini's wording come from rules (eval/lib/loose.mjs); check them by hand with the annotation sheet (`npm run eval:rescore`) before publishing.
- One embedding model (MiniLM-L6), at the quantised size AURA ships; the largest store tested has 350 background facts.



================================================
FILE: eval/run-gate-sim.mjs
================================================
// Experiment 1: how the review policy affects memory accuracy and user burden, as the extractor's error
// rate grows. Uses AURA's real memory code, database and local embedding model; only the Gemini extractor
// is simulated, with known error rates, so the effect of the policy can be isolated.
//
//   npm run eval:gate                                   full run (defaults below)
//   npm run eval:gate -- --personas 5 --seeds 1         quick check
//   npm run eval:gate -- --out <folder> --budget 150    resume an unfinished run, stop starting new work after 150 s
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { openIsolated, EVAL_DIR } from "./lib/env.mjs";
import { makePersona, withRestates } from "./lib/scenarios.mjs";
import { runPersona, POLICIES } from "./lib/harness.mjs";
import { mean, ci95, fmt, toCSV, mdTable, writeJSON, outDir, appendRows, readRows, budget } from "./lib/stats.mjs";

const { values: a } = parseArgs({
  options: {
    personas: { type: "string", default: "20" },
    seeds: { type: "string", default: "3" },
    errors: { type: "string", default: "0,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.3" },
    u: { type: "string", default: "0.05" },
    "u-sweep": { type: "string", default: "0,0.1,0.2,0.3" },
    "u-sweep-error": { type: "string", default: "0.1" },
    policies: { type: "string", default: POLICIES.join(",") },
    "filler-initial": { type: "string", default: "30" },
    "filler-gap": { type: "string", default: "10" },
    out: { type: "string" },
    "extract-min-score": { type: "string" },
    // the two memory features under test (see server/memory.mjs); defaults = AURA as shipped
    candidates: { type: "string", default: "default" },
    repropose: { type: "string", default: "0" },
    restate: { type: "string", default: "0" },
    budget: { type: "string", default: "0" },
  },
});
if (a["extract-min-score"] != null) process.env.AURA_EXTRACT_MIN_SCORE = a["extract-min-score"];
const out = outDir(EVAL_DIR, "gate-sim", a.out);
const cfgFile = path.join(out, "config.json");
// a resumed run keeps the configuration it was started with
const cfg = fs.existsSync(cfgFile)
  ? JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(cfgFile, "utf8"))
  : {
      experiment: "gate-sim",
      personas: Number(a.personas),
      seeds: Number(a.seeds),
      errors: a.errors.split(",").map(Number),
      u: Number(a.u),
      uSweep: a["u-sweep"] ? a["u-sweep"].split(",").map(Number) : [],
      uSweepError: Number(a["u-sweep-error"]),
      policies: a.policies.split(","),
      fillerInitial: Number(a["filler-initial"]),
      fillerPerGap: Number(a["filler-gap"]),
      extractor: "simulated (eval/lib/harness.mjs makeSimExtractor)",
      // candidate selection for the extractor: AURA default (search minimum 0.25) or the tested change
      extractMinScore: process.env.AURA_EXTRACT_MIN_SCORE ?? "default (0.25)",
      candidates: a.candidates,
      repropose: Number(a.repropose),
      restate: Number(a.restate),
    };
// a resumed run keeps the features it was started with
process.env.AURA_CANDIDATES = cfg.candidates ?? "default";
process.env.AURA_REPROPOSE = String(cfg.repropose ?? 0);
if (!fs.existsSync(cfgFile)) writeJSON(cfgFile, { ...cfg, startedAt: new Date().toISOString() });

const cells = [];
for (const e of cfg.errors) for (const p of cfg.policies) cells.push({ sweep: "error", policy: p, e, u: cfg.u });
for (const u of cfg.uSweep) for (const p of ["gate", "gateAll"].filter((x) => cfg.policies.includes(x))) cells.push({ sweep: "user", policy: p, e: cfg.uSweepError, u });
const key = (c) => `${c.sweep}|${c.policy}|${c.e}|${c.u}`;

const env = await openIsolated();
const outOfTime = budget(Number(a.budget));
const done = new Set(readRows(out, "runs.jsonl").map((r) => `${key(r)}|${r.seed}|${r.persona}`));
const t0 = performance.now();

for (const c of cells) {
  const pending = [];
  for (let seed = 1; seed <= cfg.seeds; seed++) for (let i = 0; i < cfg.personas; i++) if (!done.has(`${key(c)}|${seed}|${i}`)) pending.push([seed, i]);
  if (!pending.length) continue;
  if (outOfTime()) break;
  const rows = [];
  for (const [seed, i] of pending) {
    const persona = withRestates(makePersona(seed, i), cfg.restate ?? 0, `${seed}`);
    const m = await runPersona(env, persona, { policy: c.policy, e: c.e, u: c.u, fillerInitial: cfg.fillerInitial, fillerPerGap: cfg.fillerPerGap, extractor: "sim", restateUpdates: (cfg.restate ?? 0) > 0 });
    rows.push({ ...c, seed, persona: i, ...m, restates: persona.restates || 0, promptsPer100Turns: (100 * m.prompts) / m.userTurns });
  }
  appendRows(out, "runs.jsonl", rows);
  console.log(`${key(c).padEnd(24)} F1 ${fmt(mean(rows.map((r) => r.f1)))}  stale ${fmt(mean(rows.map((r) => r.stale)), 2)}  false ${fmt(mean(rows.map((r) => r.falseMem)), 2)}  prompts/100 ${fmt(mean(rows.map((r) => r.promptsPer100Turns)), 1)}`);
}
const embedStats = { ...env.models.embedStats };
env.cleanup();

const all = readRows(out, "runs.jsonl");
const expected = cells.length * cfg.personas * cfg.seeds;
if (all.length < expected) {
  console.log(`\nNot finished: ${all.length} of ${expected} persona runs. Continue with:  npm run eval:gate -- --out "${out}"`);
  process.exit(0);
}
summarize(all);
console.log(`\nResults: ${out}`);

function summarize(rows) {
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, "runs.csv"), toCSV(rows));
  const metrics = ["precision", "recall", "f1", "exactState", "stale", "falseMem", "destroyed", "fillerLost", "wrongChangesApplied", "promptsPer100Turns", "candidateMissesOnChange", "forgetMemResidual", "forgetTextResidual"];
  const summary = [];
  for (const c of cells) {
    const sel = rows.filter((r) => key(r) === key(c));
    const s = { ...c, n: sel.length };
    for (const m of metrics) {
      const xs = sel.map((r) => r[m]);
      s[`${m}_mean`] = mean(xs);
      s[`${m}_ci95`] = ci95(xs);
    }
    const sum = (f) => sel.reduce((t, r) => t + f(r), 0);
    s.candidateMissRate = sum((r) => r.changeTurns) ? sum((r) => r.candidateMissesOnChange) / sum((r) => r.changeTurns) : 0;
    const decided = sum((r) => r.correctAccepted + r.correctRejected + r.wrongAccepted + r.wrongRejected);
    s.promptPrecision = decided ? sum((r) => r.correctAccepted + r.correctRejected) / decided : NaN;
    s.injectedWrongChanges = sum((r) => r.injectedWrongChanges) / sel.length;
    summary.push(s);
  }
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, "summary.csv"), toCSV(summary));

  const md = [];
  md.push(`# Experiment 1: review policy vs. extractor error rate (simulated extractor)`);
  md.push(``);
  md.push(`Features under test: candidate selection \`${cfg.candidates ?? "default"}\`, re-proposal limit ${cfg.repropose ?? 0}, restate probability ${cfg.restate ?? 0} (restated facts add turns to every persona and let a correct extractor update a stale memory it is shown).`);
  md.push(``);
  md.push(`Candidate selection for the extractor: ${cfg.extractMinScore === "default (0.25)" || cfg.extractMinScore == null ? "AURA as shipped (search minimum score 0.25)" : `minimum score ${cfg.extractMinScore} (AURA_EXTRACT_MIN_SCORE)`}.`);
  md.push(``);
  md.push(`${cfg.personas} personas x ${cfg.seeds} seeds per cell (n = ${cfg.personas * cfg.seeds}); each persona has 5 sessions (~21 user turns). ` +
    `The memory store starts with ${cfg.fillerInitial} unrelated facts and gains ${cfg.fillerPerGap} between sessions. ` +
    `Means with 95% CI half-widths. Extractor = simulated with error rate e (not Gemini); database, memory logic, candidate selection and embeddings are AURA's real code and local model.`);
  md.push(``);
  md.push(`## Error-rate sweep (user slip rate u = ${cfg.u})`);
  md.push(``);
  md.push(mdTable(
    ["policy", "e", "F1", "exact final state", "stale facts", "false facts", "true facts destroyed", "wrong changes applied", "prompts / 100 turns", "prompt precision"],
    summary.filter((s) => s.sweep === "error").map((s) => [s.policy, s.e, `${fmt(s.f1_mean)} Â± ${fmt(s.f1_ci95)}`, fmt(s.exactState_mean, 2), fmt(s.stale_mean, 2), fmt(s.falseMem_mean, 2), fmt(s.destroyed_mean + s.fillerLost_mean, 2), fmt(s.wrongChangesApplied_mean, 2), fmt(s.promptsPer100Turns_mean, 1), fmt(s.promptPrecision, 2)])
  ));
  if (summary.some((s) => s.sweep === "user")) {
    md.push(``);
    md.push(`## User-reliability sweep (extractor error rate e = ${cfg.uSweepError})`);
    md.push(``);
    md.push(mdTable(
      ["policy", "u", "F1", "stale facts", "false facts", "wrong changes applied", "prompts / 100 turns"],
      summary.filter((s) => s.sweep === "user").map((s) => [s.policy, s.u, `${fmt(s.f1_mean)} Â± ${fmt(s.f1_ci95)}`, fmt(s.stale_mean, 2), fmt(s.falseMem_mean, 2), fmt(s.wrongChangesApplied_mean, 2), fmt(s.promptsPer100Turns_mean, 1)])
    ));
  }
  md.push(``);
  md.push(`## Other measurements`);
  md.push(``);
  const e0 = summary.filter((s) => s.sweep === "error" && s.e === 0);
  md.push(`- Change turns whose target memory was not among the candidates shown to the extractor (e = 0): ` + e0.map((s) => `${s.policy} ${fmt(s.candidateMissRate, 3)}`).join(", ") + `.`);
  md.push(`- Forget requests (per persona) whose value is still in a memory row / still in the stored conversation text (e = 0): ` + e0.map((s) => `${s.policy} ${fmt(s.forgetMemResidual_mean, 2)} / ${fmt(s.forgetTextResidual_mean, 2)}`).join("; ") + ` (forget requests per persona: ${fmt(mean(rows.filter((r) => r.e === 0).map((r) => r.forgets)), 2)}).`);
  md.push(``);
  md.push(`Column definitions: eval/README.md. Raw rows: runs.csv. Configuration: config.json.`);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, "summary.md"), md.join("\n") + "\n");
  writeJSON(path.join(out, "run-info.json"), {
    finishedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    embeddingModel: "Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    node: process.version,
    platform: `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`,
    lastSessionEmbedStats: embedStats,
    lastSessionSeconds: (performance.now() - t0) / 1000,
  });
}

// Experiment 5: AURA's memory pipeline on the LongMemEval knowledge-update questions.
//
// LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2024) gives chat histories in which a fact changes ("I live in Pune" ... later
// "I have just moved to Hyderabad") and asks a question whose right answer is the LATEST value. Here each
// question is played through AURA's real extractor (Gemini), real memory store and real search, under the
// same policies as Experiment 1, and then answered from the memories AURA retrieves.
//
// Setup (once):
//   1. Download a LongMemEval file and put it in eval/data/ (the folder is created for you):
//        longmemeval_s_cleaned.json   (the "S" setting, ~115k-token histories; recommended)
//      from the benchmark's Hugging Face dataset `xiaowu0162/longmemeval-cleaned`
//      (project page: github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval). Check the license before you redistribute it.
//   2. GEMINI_API_KEY in .env, as for Experiment 4.
//
//   npm run eval:lme                          shows the plan and the number of requests, sends nothing
//   npm run eval:lme -- --yes                 runs it (30 questions x policies; see the plan for the count)
//   npm run eval:lme -- --out <folder> --yes  continues an interrupted run
//   npm run eval:lme -- --check-with-sim      no Gemini, no dataset: tests the plumbing on a made-up fixture
//
// What is real and what is a choice made for the evaluation:
//   real     : extractor (Gemini), memory store, operations, review proposals, embeddings, memory search.
//   a choice : a LongMemEval history has ~50 sessions. To keep the request count manageable, each question
//              is played with ALL of its evidence sessions plus --distractors randomly chosen other
//              sessions (same sessions for every policy, in date order). One extraction call per session,
//              as the app extracts a conversation's new messages in one batch. Assistant messages are cut
//              to --assistant-chars characters.
//   answer   : the LLM answers from the top --k memories found by AURA's own search (no dates, in relevance
//              order, as the app does). Correctness is judged by a Gemini judge written after LongMemEval's
//              knowledge-update grading rule (the exact LongMemEval prompt is not reproduced here) and by a
//              strict string match. Both are saved so they can be compared. Use --no-judge to skip the judge.
//   append   : a changed fact is added as one more fact; the old one stays active (an update becomes an add).
//   auto     : every operation is applied.
//   gate     : LongMemEval has no labels saying which memory changes are right, so the reviewer is an oracle
//              approximation: --reviewer evidence accepts every proposal made while reading an evidence
//              session and rejects the rest; accept = accepts all (so gate == auto in the end state, with the
//              prompts counted); reject = rejects all. Treat gate results as a bracket, not as a measurement
//              of real users.
//   baselines: none = answer without memory; context = answer from the raw text of the same sessions.

import { mean, wilson, fmt, toCSV, mdTable, writeJSON, outDir, appendRows, readRows, budget } from "./lib/stats.mjs";

    types: { type: "string", default: "knowledge-update" },
    questions: { type: "string", default: "30" },
    distractors: { type: "string", default: "3" },
    policies: { type: "string", default: "append,auto,gate" },
    baselines: { type: "string", default: "none,context" },
    reviewer: { type: "string", default: "evidence" },

  },
});
if (a["extract-min-score"] != null) process.env.AURA_EXTRACT_MIN_SCORE = a["extract-min-score"];

const list = (s) => (s ? s.split(",").map((x) => x.trim()).filter(Boolean) : []);

function loadData() {
  if (check) return makeFixture(6, 1);

    console.log(`LongMemEval file not found: ${a.data}\nDownload longmemeval_s_cleaned.json (see the header of this script) and put it in eval/data/, or pass --data <file>.`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(a.data, "utf8"));
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) throw new Error("Expected a JSON array of LongMemEval instances.");
  return raw;
}
const REQUIRED = ["question_id", "question_type", "question", "answer", "haystack_sessions", "haystack_session_ids"];
function validate(q) {
  const miss = REQUIRED.filter((k) => !(k in q));
  if (miss.length) throw new Error(`Unexpected file format: instance ${q.question_id ?? "?"} lacks ${miss.join(", ")}. This script expects the LongMemEval format (see lib/lme-fixture.mjs).`);
}
function parseDate(s, fallback) {
  const m = /(\d{4})\/(\d{1,2})\/(\d{1,2})(?:[^\d]+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?/.exec(String(s || ""));
  return m ? Date.UTC(+m[1], +m[2] - 1, +m[3], +(m[4] || 0), +(m[5] || 0)) : fallback;
}

const data = loadData();
const types = new Set(list(a.types));
let pool = data.filter((q) => (types.has("all") || types.has(q.question_type)) && !String(q.question_id).endsWith("_abs"));
pool.forEach(validate);
pool = pool.sort((x, y) => hash(`${x.question_id}|${a.seed}`) - hash(`${y.question_id}|${a.seed}`)).slice(0, Number(a.questions));

function sessionsFor(q) {
  const ids = q.haystack_session_ids;
  const ans = new Set(q.answer_session_ids || []);
  const isEv = (i) => ans.has(ids[i]) || (q.haystack_sessions[i] || []).some((t) => t.has_answer);
  const idx = ids.map((_, i) => i);
  const ev = idx.filter(isEv);
  const r = rng(hash(`${q.question_id}|${a.seed}|distractors`));
  const others = shuffle(idx.filter((i) => !isEv(i)), r).slice(0, Number(a.distractors));
  return [...ev, ...others]
    .map((i) => ({ id: ids[i], date: parseDate(q.haystack_dates?.[i], Date.UTC(2023, 0, 1) + i * 86400000), turns: q.haystack_sessions[i], evidence: isEv(i) }))
    .sort((x, y) => x.date - y.date);
}

// ---------- config and plan ----------
const out = outDir(EVAL_DIR, check ? "lme-check" : "longmemeval", a.out);

      rpm: Number(a.rpm),
      extractMinScore: process.env.AURA_EXTRACT_MIN_SCORE ?? "default (0.25)",
      candidates: a.candidates,
      repropose: Number(a.repropose),
      model: check ? "simulated rule-based extractor" : `Gemini ${env.config.TEXT_MODEL}`,
    };
// a resumed run keeps the features it was started with

process.env.AURA_REPROPOSE = String(cfg.repropose ?? 0);

  (t, { sessions }) => t + cfg.policies.reduce((s) => s + sessions.length + perQ(0), 0) + cfg.baselines.reduce((s) => s + perQ(0), 0),
  0

      `(about ${Math.ceil(requests / cfg.rpm)} min).`
  );
  if (!a.yes) {
    console.log("Nothing was sent. Add --yes to run it.");
    env.cleanup();

  }
