\end{table*}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig6_real.pdf}
\caption{Gate policy with real Gemini extractors: (a) F1, (b) stale facts per persona; mean and 95\% bootstrap interval over 12 personas.}
\label{fig:real}
\end{figure*}

\textbf{Reachability on real conversations.} With the baseline selection, the target memory was missing from the prompt on \candMissABase\ of \changeTurnsA\ change turns (first model; both policies together) and \candMissBBase\ of \changeTurnsB\ (second model). With F1+F2 it was missing on \candMissABoth\ and \candMissBBoth. This is the mechanism of Sec.~\ref{sec:reach} observed with real conversations.

\textbf{Stale facts and F1.} Under the gate, stale facts per persona fell from \realAgatestaleBase\ to \realAgatestaleBoth\ (first model; $p=\realAgatestaleP$) and from \realBgatestaleBase\ to \realBgatestaleBoth\ (second; $p=\realBgatestaleP$), and F1 rose from \realAgatefOneBase\ to \realAgatefOneBoth\ (\realAgatefOneDiff, $p=\realAgatefOneP$) and from \realBgatefOneBase\ to \realBgatefOneBoth\ (\realBgatefOneDiff, $p=\realBgatefOneP$). F2 alone reached \realAgatestalefTwoVal\ stale facts ($p=\realAgatestalefTwoP$) and F1 of \realAgatefOnefTwoVal\ ($p=\realAgatefOnefTwoP$, not significant); the benefit of adding F1 to F2 was not tested separately and is within what 12 personas can resolve. F1 alone changed nothing measurable (stale \realAgatestalefOneVal, $p=\realAgatestalefOneP$): on real models F1 is not supported. Under auto-apply the picture is the same (stale \realAautostaleBase\ to \realAautostaleBoth, $p=\realAautostaleP$).

\textbf{Safety on real models.} No injected errors exist in real runs, so we count what the models did. Across all auto-apply persona runs (\realAutoRuns), \realAutoLostAll\ true background facts were destroyed by the model's own operations (\realAutoLostBase\ of them in the two baseline runs); across the \realGateRuns\ gate runs the count was \realGateLostAll. With the oracle user, no correct change was rejected, no wrong change was accepted and \realWrongApplied\ wrong changes were applied. Because the user is perfect and the counts are small, this is a consistency check on the simulation, not a measurement of real users.

\textbf{Cost.} Prompt tokens per persona rose from about 13.4k to 18.1k (+\tokInc\%, $p<0.001$), and the number of prompts per 100 turns from \realAgatepromptsPerOneZeroZeroTurnsBase\ to \realAgatepromptsPerOneZeroZeroTurnsBoth\ (first model, $p=\realAgatepromptsPerOneZeroZeroTurnsP$) and from \realBgatepromptsPerOneZeroZeroTurnsBase\ to \realBgatepromptsPerOneZeroZeroTurnsBoth\ (second, $p=\realBgatepromptsPerOneZeroZeroTurnsP$), not significant. Of the change prompts, \gateAcceptedABoth\ of \gatePromptsABoth\ (first model) and \gateAcceptedBBoth\ of \gatePromptsBBoth\ (second) in the F1+F2 runs were correct changes that the user accepted, against \gateAcceptedABase\ of \gatePromptsABase\ and \gateAcceptedBBase\ of \gatePromptsBBase\ for the baselines; this is consistent with the added prompts being updates that the baseline missed.\label{sec:cost}

\textbf{Other effects.} Under auto-apply the F2-only variant stored \falseAutoTwoA\ false facts across 12 personas where the baseline stored none, and F1+F2 stored none again; with these counts we cannot say whether this is an effect of F2 or noise.

\subsection{Per-persona results}
Table~\ref{tab:perpersona} lists every persona of the first model under the gate. With the baseline selection, \personasStaleBase\ of 12 personas ended with at least one stale fact and \personasMissBase\ had at least one change target missing from the prompt; with F1+F2 none did. Persona 9 has the same F1 under both settings. Persona 3 has a lower F1 under F1+F2 because the model stored one more hypothetical sentence (``would like to live in Goa someday''), which lowers precision; none of its updates is wrong, so this is not a regression in updating.

\subsection{A worked example}
\label{sec:example}
Persona 1 (Table~\ref{tab:persona}) is a typical case. Table~\ref{tab:decbase} shows the proposals made under the baseline, Table~\ref{tab:membase} the final memories, and Tables~\ref{tab:decboth} and~\ref{tab:memboth} the same under F1+F2. Under the baseline the extractor updated the gym time, the city (twice) and forgot the birthday, but it never proposed to replace ``drives a Seltos''; the user's ``I sold my old car and bought a Swift'' became a separate fact (``bought a Swift car'') and the Seltos memory remained active and stale. The one change target missing from the baseline prompt on this persona is consistent with this. A further proposal, replacing the project memory by ``currently between projects'', was rejected by the oracle reviewer. Under F1+F2 the same persona produced the car update, and the project memory was replaced by an ``ended'' record that was accepted.

The rejected proposal shows a limitation of our reviewer. The oracle judges proposals with the same value-based rules as the scorer, and a correct paraphrase can be rejected when the rules do not recognise its wording. In the baseline run this happened once for this persona; the final memory then still holds the old project memory, which the scorer rightly counts as stale. We therefore treat the oracle as an approximation of a careful user, not as one.

\section{External Check: LongMemEval}
\label{sec:lme}
LongMemEval's knowledge-update questions ask for the latest value of a fact that changed during the history \cite{wu2024longmemeval}. We took \lmeQ\ such questions of the ``S'' setting and played each with all evidence sessions plus three random distractor sessions (the same for every system) through \aura's extractor, store and search; answers come from the ten memories that \aura's search returns, and are graded by a Gemini judge written after the benchmark's rule (the official prompt is not reproduced) and by string match. All runs use \texttt{gemini-3.1-flash-lite}. There is no label for which memory changes are right, so the gate's reviewer is an oracle approximation: it accepts proposals made while reading an evidence session and rejects the rest. This gate figure is therefore an upper-bracket, not a measurement of real users. Baselines are answering with no memory and with the raw sessions as context.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\small
\caption{LongMemEval knowledge-update questions (judge-graded accuracy, $n=\lmeQ$). $b/c$: questions correct only in the baseline / only in the F1+F2 run.}
\label{tab:lme}
\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\input{tables/lme.tex}}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig7_lme.pdf}
\caption{LongMemEval accuracy by system for baseline and F1+F2 selection (95\% normal-approximation bars).}
\label{fig:lme}
\end{figure}

Table~\ref{tab:lme} and Fig.~\ref{fig:lme} show that the gate system improves from \lmegateBase\ to \lmegateBoth\ (\lmeGateB\ questions worse, \lmeGateC\ better, $p=\lmegateP$), which is in the expected direction but not significant at this sample size; the systems without memory or with full context, which cannot be affected, differ by \lmecontextDiff\ between the two runs, which indicates run-to-run noise of that size. Auto-apply and append are not distinguishable between the runs. Full-context answering (\lmecontextBoth\ in the second run) remains clearly above the gate system (\lmegateBoth; \lmeCtxGateB\ vs.\ \lmeCtxGateC\ discordant questions, $p=\lmeCtxGateP$): a memory system trades accuracy for the properties it provides, such as small prompts, forgetting and user control. A run on all 78 knowledge-update questions would be needed for a firm statement.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\textbf{Where the guarantee ends.} The gate provides a guarantee about what is \emph{written}: nothing changes without approval. It provides none about what is \emph{proposed}. In our experiments the second quantity depends on a component that looks like plumbing, the choice of candidate memories, and with default settings it is the main reason that stale facts remain. Evaluating a user-controlled memory by its write accuracy or by the number of approvals alone would miss this.

\textbf{Design implications.} (i) Report reachability alongside accuracy for any extractor-based memory. (ii) Search per sentence rather than per message when messages are mixed. (iii) Treat the minimum score as a trade-off: the unfiltered selection raises reachability (\reachLastNoMin\ at $N=350$) but admits unrelated memories, so the price of F2 is a larger prompt. (iv) Budget for more prompt tokens (about \tokInc\%) and slightly more review cards.

\textbf{What the gate is for.} The gate is a user-control mechanism as much as a safety mechanism. Every change to what the assistant believes about a person passes a visible decision, old values remain as history, and forgetting is an explicit operation that removes the memory. Our results show what this buys (protection against wrong writes) and what it costs (20--33 prompts per 100 turns in simulation, a little more with F2). They also show a limit: the gate's protection is only as good as the user's attention (Table~\ref{tab:slip}), and adding prompts can lower that attention. Whether F2's additional prompts, which are mostly correct updates, are better tolerated than the baseline's is an empirical question for a user study.

\textbf{Why the missed-update problem is easy to overlook.} A missed update does not produce an error message, a wrong answer on the turn it occurs, or a prompt. It surfaces later, when the assistant states an outdated fact. Evaluations that look at single-turn extraction, or at accuracy of what is written, will not see it; measuring the final memory state against the true state, as we do, does.

\textbf{Choosing between larger prompts and better search.} F2 enlarges the prompt by about a third. Alternatives are a better retriever (for example a cross-encoder or a learned relevance gate over candidates, as in \cite{zhang2026memgate} for retrieval), a second extraction pass over the \emph{whole} store for messages with a change cue, or a structured memory with typed slots in which an update names its slot. We did not evaluate these; the point of F2 is that a small, inexpensive change already removes most misses in our setting, and that reachability is a quantity worth tracking whichever remedy is chosen.

\textbf{On F1.} Letting a rejected change return only after new user input is cheap and conceptually neat, but we found no benefit with real models (the oracle user rejected no correct change in these runs), and only small, uncorrected-significance effects in simulation. Its value would have to be shown with real users who slip.

\section{Threats to Validity}
\label{sec:threats}
\textbf{Synthetic and English personas.} Personas, distractors and the wording of changes were written by the system's author. The change cues of F2 were designed after the reachability failures were seen on the same generator, so F2 may be tuned to it; the LongMemEval check is the only independent text and is small. \textbf{Small real samples.} 12 personas, one seed per cell and two models of the same family; exact sign tests with 12 pairs cannot resolve small effects, and several F1 results are inconclusive rather than null. \textbf{Simulated user.} The real runs use a perfect reviewer, the simulations a random slip. Real users may ignore, batch or rubber-stamp prompts; whether additional prompts are tolerated is open. No user study was done. \textbf{Single annotator and scorer.} Labels come from the author. \textbf{One embedding model.} Reachability depends on MiniLM and the 0.25 threshold. \textbf{LongMemEval.} Thirty questions, a judge that is not the official prompt, an oracle reviewer, and a single seed. \textbf{Multiple tests.} Reported as counts; only the large effects are robust to correction. \textbf{Related work.} Sources were read at abstract level.

\section{Future Work}
\label{sec:future}
\textbf{User study.} The most important missing piece is a study with real users that measures how often they approve, reject or ignore proposals, whether they slip, and whether the extra prompts from F2 are tolerated. \textbf{Better candidate selection.} The city case (Table~\ref{tab:reachslot}) shows that sentence search with a larger candidate set is not enough when a statement contains no word that points to the old value; slot-typed memories or a second pass are candidates. \textbf{Other languages and models.} All personas are English and both extractors are Gemini models. \textbf{Bigger real samples.} More personas, more seeds, and all 78 LongMemEval knowledge-update questions would turn several inconclusive results into findings. \textbf{Proactive use of memory.} \aura\ also contains an optional layer that asks the user whether a stored fact is still true, sends reminders and prepares briefings; its checks use the same proposal path as the gate. We did not evaluate it and make no claim about it here.

\section{Conclusion}
A review gate on memory changes is effective against the errors it can see: in our experiments it removes almost all of the true facts that automatic application destroys. It does not address updates the extractor never proposes, and in a retrieval-based design these are governed by which memories the extractor is shown. Showing candidates by sentence, without a minimum score and with a larger set on a change cue, removed all observed misses for two real Gemini models and removed the stale facts, at roughly a third more prompt tokens and no significant increase in review prompts, while an external check on LongMemEval pointed in the same direction without reaching significance. The practical lesson for user-controlled memories is to measure and report what the extractor can reach. Evaluating with real users, in other languages and with larger real samples is the necessary next step; the evaluation code and every raw result file are provided so that others can repeat and extend it.

\appendices
\section{Scoring Rules and Labels}
\label{app:scoring}
\textbf{Value matching.} Each persona slot has a set of possible values (for example the gym slot has ``6 am'', ``7 am'', ``6 pm'', ``8 pm''), each with alternative spellings (``6am'', ``6:00 am'', ``18:00''); birthdays accept ``12 March'', ``March 12'', ``12th March'' and so on; coffee values accept ``black coffee'' or ``oat milk''. A value is matched as a whole word, case-insensitively. Distractor values (a hypothetical city, a friend's car) have their own matchers.

\textbf{Wording of third parties, hypotheticals and ended facts.} A memory that mentions only a distractor value is \emph{third-party} if it contains a word for a relative, friend, colleague or neighbour, \emph{hypothetical} if it contains ``if'', ``would'' or ``hypothetical'', and \emph{false} otherwise. A memory about a retired fact is \emph{ended} if it contains a phrase such as ``no longer'', ``finished'', ``wrapped up'', ``between projects'', ``stopped'', ``sold'', ``unemployed'' or ``not working'' and the fact was retired but not asked to be forgotten. A fact that the user asked to forget and that is still stored counts as \emph{stale}.

\textbf{Annotation protocol.} For every memory in the baseline and F1+F2 real runs the annotator saw the persona's sessions, the true final state and the memory text, and wrote one of seven labels (true, ended, stale, false, hypothetical, third-party, other), looking at the automatic label only afterwards where possible. The automatic and the hand label were then compared (Table~\ref{tab:agree}).

\section{Reproducing the Results}
All commands are run from the repository root. Simulated experiments need no API key; real-model experiments need \texttt{GEMINI\_API\_KEY} and internet access.
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0pt}
\item \texttt{npm run eval:gate}, \texttt{eval:retrieval}, \texttt{eval:reach}: policies, retrieval, reachability;
\item \texttt{npm run eval:gate -- --errors 0,0.1,0.2 --policies auto,gate --restate 1 --candidates adaptive --repropose 2 --out eval/results/ablation/both} (and the three other variants), then \texttt{npm run eval:compare} for the paired statistics;
\item \texttt{npm run eval:real -- --yes}: real-model runs (twelve personas, four variants, one folder each); \texttt{npm run eval:rescore}: scoring and annotation sheet;
\item \texttt{npm run eval:lme -- --yes}: LongMemEval subset; \texttt{npm run eval:compare-lme};
\item \texttt{python eval/make\_paper\_assets.py --root eval --out paper}: every table, number macro and the real-run and LongMemEval figures of this paper.
\end{itemize}

{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0pt}
\item Session 1: 'I go to the gym at 7 am every day.' 'My birthday is on 21 September.' 'I take my coffee as a cappuccino.' 'My dog is called Mithu.'
\item Session 2: 'Like I said, my dog is called Mithu.' 'My friend Rohan just bought a Thar, it looks great.' 'I live in Kolkata.' 'I drive a Seltos.' 'I work at Swiggy.' 'I'm leading a project called Lotus at work.'
\item Session 3: 'Like I said, i go to the gym at 7 am every day.' 'What's the weather like in Shimla today?' 'I moved my gym time to 6 pm.' 'My project wrapped up last week, I'm between projects.'
\item Session 4: 'Like I said, i work at Swiggy.' 'Please forget what I told you about my birthday.' 'Can you set a timer for ten minutes?' 'I've just moved to Pune.'
\item Session 5: 'Is it true that octopuses have three hearts?' 'Like I said, i work at Swiggy.' 'I've just moved to Chennai.' 'I sold my old car and bought a Swift.'
\item Truth at the end: gym: 6 pm; birthday: no longer true; coffee: as a cappuccino; pet: Mithu; city: Chennai; car: Swift; employer: Swiggy; project: no longer true. Asked to forget: birthday (21 September).
\end{itemize}}

// Small helpers for 16 kHz mono PCM16 audio.
export const SAMPLE_RATE = 16000;

export function pcmToWav(pcm, sampleRate = SAMPLE_RATE) {
  const header = Buffer.alloc(44);
  header.write("RIFF", 0);
  header.writeUInt32LE(36 + pcm.length, 4);
  header.write("WAVE", 8);
  header.write("fmt ", 12);
  header.writeUInt32LE(16, 16);
  header.writeUInt16LE(1, 20); // PCM
  header.writeUInt16LE(1, 22); // mono
  header.writeUInt32LE(sampleRate, 24);
  header.writeUInt32LE(sampleRate * 2, 28);
  header.writeUInt16LE(2, 32);
  header.writeUInt16LE(16, 34);
  header.write("data", 36);
  header.writeUInt32LE(pcm.length, 40);
  return Buffer.concat([header, pcm]);
}

/** PCM16 little-endian buffer -> Float32Array in [-1, 1]. */
export function pcmToFloat32(pcm) {
  const n = Math.floor(pcm.length / 2);
  const out = new Float32Array(n);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out[i] = pcm.readInt16LE(i * 2) / 32768;
  return out;
}

export const pcmSeconds = (pcm) => pcm.length / 2 / SAMPLE_RATE;

import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import fs from "node:fs";

export const ROOT_DIR = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");

// load .env.local then .env (values already in the environment win)
for (const f of [".env.local", ".env"]) {
  const p = path.join(ROOT_DIR, f);
  if (fs.existsSync(p)) process.loadEnvFile(p);
}

export const DATA_DIR = process.env.AURA_DATA_DIR
  ? path.resolve(process.env.AURA_DATA_DIR)
  : path.join(ROOT_DIR, "data");

export const PORT = Number(process.env.AURA_PORT || 3001);

// The key stays on the server. The browser only ever receives short-lived
// ephemeral tokens for Gemini Live.
export const GEMINI_API_KEY = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY || "";

// Gemini models used by the server (text + audio understanding).
export const TEXT_MODEL = process.env.GEMINI_TEXT_MODEL || "gemini-3.5-flash-lite";
export const TRANSCRIBE_MODEL =
  process.env.GEMINI_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL || "gemini-3.5-flash-lite";

  process.env.AURA_TEXT_EMBED_MODEL || "Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2";

// Conversation history (assistant chats) stored in SQLite.
import { db, now } from "./db.mjs";

export function createConversation() {
  const t = now();
  const id = db.prepare("INSERT INTO conversations(started_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?)").run(t, t).lastInsertRowid;
  return getConversation(id);
}

export function listConversations() {
  return db
    .prepare(
      `SELECT c.id, c.title, c.started_at, c.updated_at, c.pinned,
              (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages m WHERE m.conversation_id = c.id) AS n,
              (SELECT text FROM messages m WHERE m.conversation_id = c.id AND role = 'user' AND modality != 'document' ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) AS first_user,
              (SELECT name FROM documents d WHERE d.conversation_id = c.id ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) AS first_doc
       FROM conversations c ORDER BY c.pinned DESC, c.updated_at DESC`
    )
    .all()
    .filter((c) => c.n > 0)
    .map((c) => ({
      id: c.id,
      title: c.title || (c.first_user || c.first_doc || "Conversation").slice(0, 60),
      startedAt: c.started_at,
      updatedAt: c.updated_at,
      messageCount: c.n,
      pinned: !!c.pinned,
      renamed: !!c.title,
    }));
}

export function getConversation(id) {
  const c = db.prepare("SELECT * FROM conversations WHERE id = ?").get(id);
  if (!c) return null;
  const messages = db
    .prepare("SELECT id, role, modality, text, meta, created_at FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY id")
    .all(id)
    .map((m) => ({ id: m.id, role: m.role, modality: m.modality, text: m.text, createdAt: m.created_at, ...parseMeta(m.meta) }));
  const firstUser = messages.find((m) => m.role === "user" && m.modality !== "document")?.text;
  const firstDoc = messages.find((m) => m.modality === "document")?.document?.name;
  return {
    id: c.id,
    title: c.title || (firstUser || firstDoc || "Conversation").slice(0, 60),
    renamed: !!c.title,
    pinned: !!c.pinned,
    startedAt: c.started_at,
    updatedAt: c.updated_at,
    messages,
  };
}

function parseMeta(meta) {
  if (!meta) return {};
  try {
    return JSON.parse(meta);
  } catch {
    return {};
  }
}

/** Keep only the web-search details we show: source links and the queries used. */
export function cleanSearchMeta(input) {
  if (!input || typeof input !== "object") return null;
  const sources = Array.isArray(input.sources)
    ? input.sources
        .filter((s) => s && /^https?:\/\//.test(String(s.uri || "")))
        .slice(0, 12)
        .map((s) => ({ title: String(s.title || s.uri).slice(0, 200), uri: String(s.uri).slice(0, 2000) }))
    : [];
  const searchQueries = Array.isArray(input.searchQueries) ? input.searchQueries.slice(0, 8).map((q) => String(q).slice(0, 300)) : [];
  if (!sources.length && !searchQueries.length) return null;
  return { sources, searchQueries };
}

export function addMessage(conversationId, { role, text, modality = "text", meta = null }) {
  const t = now();
  const id = db
    .prepare("INSERT INTO messages(conversation_id, role, modality, text, meta, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")
    .run(conversationId, role, modality, String(text), meta ? JSON.stringify(meta) : null, t).lastInsertRowid;
  db.prepare("UPDATE conversations SET updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?").run(t, conversationId);
  return { id: Number(id), role, modality, text, createdAt: t, ...(meta || {}) };
}

export function recentMessages(conversationId, limit = 20) {
  return db
    .prepare("SELECT role, text FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?")
    .all(conversationId, limit)
    .reverse();
}

export function deleteConversation(id) {
  return db.prepare("DELETE FROM conversations WHERE id = ?").run(id).changes > 0;
}

export function deleteAllConversations() {
  return db.prepare("DELETE FROM conversations").run().changes;
}

export function updateConversation(id, { title, pinned }) {
  if (title !== undefined) {
    const t = String(title ?? "").trim().slice(0, 120);
    db.prepare("UPDATE conversations SET title = ? WHERE id = ?").run(t || null, id); // empty = automatic title
  }
  if (pinned !== undefined) db.prepare("UPDATE conversations SET pinned = ? WHERE id = ?").run(pinned ? 1 : 0, id);
  return getConversation(id);
}

/** Earlier messages, formatted for the assistant when a conversation is continued. */
export function historyForPrompt(id, maxChars = 8000) {
  const rows = db.prepare("SELECT role, text FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 60").all(id);
  const lines = [];
  let used = 0;
  for (const r of rows) {
    const line = `${r.role === "user" ? "User" : "AURA"}: ${r.text}`;
    if (used + line.length > maxChars) break;
    lines.unshift(line);
    used += line.length;
  }
  return lines.join("\n");
}

export function exportConversation(id, format) {
  const c = getConversation(id);
  if (!c) return null;
  const who = (m) => (m.role === "user" ? "You" : "AURA");
  const when = (t) => new Date(t).toLocaleString();
  if (format === "json") {
    return {
      mime: "application/json",
      ext: "json",
      title: c.title,
      body: JSON.stringify(
        {
          title: c.title,
          startedAt: new Date(c.startedAt).toISOString(),
          messages: c.messages.map((m) => ({
            role: m.role,
            modality: m.modality,
            text: m.text,
            at: new Date(m.createdAt).toISOString(),
            ...(m.sources ? { sources: m.sources } : {}),
          })),
        },
        null,
        2
      ),
    };
  }
  if (format === "md") {
    const body = [
      `# ${c.title}`,
      "",
      `_${when(c.startedAt)}_`,
      "",
      ...c.messages.map((m) => {
        const src = m.sources?.length ? "\n\n" + m.sources.map((s, i) => `${i + 1}. [${s.title}](${s.uri})`).join("\n") : "";
        return `**${who(m)}**: ${m.text}${src}\n`;
      }),
    ].join("\n");
    return { mime: "text/markdown", ext: "md", title: c.title, body };
  }
  const body = [c.title, when(c.startedAt), "", ...c.messages.map((m) => `[${new Date(m.createdAt).toLocaleTimeString()}] ${who(m)}: ${m.text}`)].join("\n");
  return { mime: "text/plain", ext: "txt", title: c.title, body };
}

// SQLite storage for AURA. One local file: data/aura.db
// Uses Node's built-in SQLite module, so there is nothing native to compile.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";
import { DATA_DIR } from "./config.mjs";

fs.mkdirSync(DATA_DIR, { recursive: true });
export const DB_PATH = process.env.AURA_DB_PATH || path.join(DATA_DIR, "aura.db");
export const db = new DatabaseSync(DB_PATH);
db.exec("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;");

/** better-sqlite3-style helper: db.transaction(fn)(...args) runs fn atomically. */
db.transaction = (fn) => (...args) => {
  db.exec("BEGIN");
  try {
    const out = fn(...args);
    db.exec("COMMIT");
    return out;
  } catch (e) {
    db.exec("ROLLBACK");
    throw e;
  }
};

db.exec(`
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS settings (
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversations (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  title TEXT,
  started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  extracted_upto INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0  -- last message id processed by memory extraction
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  conversation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('user','assistant')),
  modality TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text',
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- status: active | superseded (replaced by a newer fact) | outdated (no longer true, no replacement)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS memories (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  content TEXT NOT NULL,
  category TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fact',
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  superseded_by INTEGER REFERENCES memories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'conversation',
  conversation_id INTEGER REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  embedding BLOB,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- changes to existing memories that wait for the user's OK
-- action: update | retire | forget; status: pending | accepted | rejected
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS memory_proposals (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  action TEXT NOT NULL,
  memory_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES memories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  content TEXT,
  category TEXT,
  conversation_id INTEGER REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  decided_at INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS speaker_profiles (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  embedding BLOB NOT NULL,
  sample_seconds REAL NOT NULL,
  consent_note TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meetings (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  ended_at INTEGER,
  speaker_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0  -- last N used for an automatic "Speaker N" label
);

-- one row per distinct voice detected in a meeting (a diarization cluster)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meeting_speakers (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  meeting_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES meetings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,              -- name shown in the transcript
  profile_id INTEGER REFERENCES speaker_profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  match_score REAL,                 -- similarity to the registered profile, when matched
  renamed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  merged_into INTEGER,              -- set when the user merged this voice into another speaker
  centroid BLOB,
  n INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS segments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  meeting_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES meetings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  speaker_id INTEGER REFERENCES meeting_speakers(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
  end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
  text TEXT,
  speaker_score REAL,               -- similarity used for the speaker decision
  speaker_uncertain INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending | done | error | empty
  error TEXT,
  audio BLOB                        -- raw 16 kHz PCM, cleared after processing
);
`);

// columns added after the first release
function addColumn(table, column, def) {
  const cols = db.prepare(`PRAGMA table_info(${table})`).all().map((c) => c.name);
  if (!cols.includes(column)) db.exec(`ALTER TABLE ${table} ADD COLUMN ${column} ${def}`);
}
addColumn("messages", "meta", "TEXT"); // JSON: web sources used for an answer
addColumn("conversations", "pinned", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0");
addColumn("speaker_profiles", "model", "TEXT"); // speaker model that produced the voiceprint
addColumn("segments", "embedding", "BLOB"); // voice embedding, used to refine speakers after a meeting
addColumn("segments", "manual", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"); // speaker set by the user, never changed automatically
addColumn("meetings", "refined", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"); // speakers re-checked after the meeting ended
addColumn("meetings", "minutes", "TEXT"); // JSON: minutes of meeting written by Gemini
addColumn("meetings", "minutes_at", "INTEGER");
// memory extraction from the transcript: NULL (not run) | running | done | error | off
addColumn("meetings", "memory_status", "TEXT");
addColumn("meetings", "memory_count", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0");
addColumn("meetings", "memory_error", "TEXT");
addColumn("memories", "meeting_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES meetings(id) ON DELETE SET NULL"); // learned from this meeting
addColumn("memory_proposals", "meeting_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES meetings(id) ON DELETE SET NULL");

// documents added to an assistant conversation (files live in data/documents/)
db.exec(`
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  conversation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,            -- pdf | image | office | text
  label TEXT NOT NULL,           -- "PDF", "Word document", ...
  mime TEXT NOT NULL,
  size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  file TEXT NOT NULL,            -- file name inside data/documents
  text TEXT,                     -- extracted text (Office and text files)
  truncated INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,          -- analysing | ready | error
  error TEXT,
  analysis TEXT,                 -- JSON overview written by Gemini
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS documents_conv ON documents(conversation_id);
`);

// proactive nudges (server/proactive.mjs). Only written when an AURA_PROACTIVE_* switch is on.
db.exec(`
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nudges (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,              -- memory_check | reminder | briefing
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  due_at INTEGER NOT NULL,         -- not shown before this time
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending | shown | accepted | dismissed | snoozed
  source_memory_id INTEGER REFERENCES memories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  source_conversation_id INTEGER REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  decided_at INTEGER,
  source_meeting_id INTEGER REFERENCES meetings(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  kind TEXT,                       -- reminder: confirm (asks to set it) | due (the reminder itself)
  payload TEXT,                    -- JSON details for the UI
  outcome TEXT,                    -- what the user chose: yes | changed | forget | scheduled | done | ...
  shown_at INTEGER,
  snoozes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS nudges_due ON nudges(status, due_at);
-- a deleted memory must not live on in the text of a memory check
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS nudges_memory_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON memories BEGIN
  DELETE FROM nudges WHERE source_memory_id = OLD.id AND type = 'memory_check' AND status IN ('pending','shown','snoozed');
  UPDATE nudges SET text = '(memory deleted)', payload = NULL WHERE source_memory_id = OLD.id AND type = 'memory_check';
END;
`);

export const now = () => Date.now();

export function f32ToBlob(arr) {
  if (!arr) return null;
  const f = arr instanceof Float32Array ? arr : Float32Array.from(arr);
  return Buffer.from(f.buffer, f.byteOffset, f.byteLength);
}

export function blobToF32(buf) {
  if (!buf) return null;
  const copy = new Uint8Array(buf); // fresh, aligned copy
  return new Float32Array(copy.buffer, 0, copy.byteLength / 4);
}

/** BLOB column (Uint8Array) -> Buffer without copying. */
export const asBuffer = (u8) => (u8 ? Buffer.from(u8.buffer, u8.byteOffset, u8.byteLength) : null);

// ---- settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS = {
  liveModel: "gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview",
  voice: "Kore",
  userName: "",
  autoMemory: true,
  // let the assistant use Google Search for current information
  webSearch: true,
  // ask before an existing memory is changed, marked outdated or deleted
  confirmMemoryChanges: true,
  // cosine similarity (WeSpeaker embeddings) needed to attach a registered name to a voice
  voiceMatchThreshold: 0.58,
  // cosine similarity needed to treat a piece of speech as an already-heard voice
  voiceClusterThreshold: 0.55,
  // language of the user's speech in voice chat, used to transcribe it: "auto", "en", "hi" or "en-hi"
  assistantLanguage: "auto",
  // optional hint for meeting transcription, e.g. "English and Hindi"
  meetingLanguage: "",
  // "live": Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Live (streaming, no daily request cap on the free tier)
  // "standard": batched requests to GEMINI_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL
  meetingTranscriber: "live",
  // after a meeting, store durable facts from its transcript in long-term memory (needs autoMemory too)
  meetingMemory: true,
};

export function getSettings() {
  const rows = db.prepare("SELECT key, value FROM settings").all();
  const s = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS };
  for (const r of rows) {
    if (!(r.key in DEFAULT_SETTINGS)) continue; // keys from older versions
    try {
      s[r.key] = JSON.parse(r.value);
    } catch {}
  }
  return s;
}

export function saveSettings(patch) {
  const stmt = db.prepare(
    "INSERT INTO settings(key, value) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value"
  );
  const tx = db.transaction((p) => {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(p)) {
      if (k in DEFAULT_SETTINGS) stmt.run(k, JSON.stringify(v));
    }
  });
  tx(patch);
  return getSettings();
}

FILE: server/doc-text.mjs

// Turns uploaded files into something Gemini can read.
//   PDF and images are sent to Gemini as they are (it reads them, including scans).
//   Word, PowerPoint and Excel files are ZIP archives of XML: their text is pulled out here,
//   without extra dependencies. Plain-text formats are decoded.
import { inflateRawSync } from "node:zlib";

const ext = (name) => (String(name).toLowerCase().match(/\.([a-z0-9]+)$/) || [])[1] || "";

const IMAGE = { png: "image/png", jpg: "image/jpeg", jpeg: "image/jpeg", webp: "image/webp", heic: "image/heic", heif: "image/heif" };
const OFFICE = { docx: "Word document", pptx: "PowerPoint presentation", xlsx: "Excel workbook" };
const TEXT = new Set([
  "txt", "md", "markdown", "csv", "tsv", "json", "xml", "html", "htm", "log", "yaml", "yml", "ini", "toml", "srt", "vtt",
  "js", "jsx", "ts", "tsx", "py", "java", "c", "h", "cpp", "cs", "go", "rs", "rb", "php", "sql", "sh", "css", "scss",
]);
const OLD_OFFICE = { doc: "docx", ppt: "pptx", xls: "xlsx" };

/** What kind of file this is: { kind: "pdf" | "image" | "office" | "text", mime, label } or { error }. */
export function classify(name) {
  const e = ext(name);
  if (e === "pdf") return { kind: "pdf", mime: "application/pdf", label: "PDF" };
  if (IMAGE[e]) return { kind: "image", mime: IMAGE[e], label: "Image" };
  if (OFFICE[e]) return { kind: "office", mime: "text/plain", label: OFFICE[e] };
  if (TEXT.has(e)) return { kind: "text", mime: "text/plain", label: e === "csv" || e === "tsv" ? "Spreadsheet (CSV)" : "Text" };
  if (OLD_OFFICE[e]) return { error: `Old .${e} files can't be read. Save it as .${OLD_OFFICE[e]} or PDF and add it again.` };
  return { error: `.${e || "?"} files aren't supported. Add a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, text, CSV or image file.` };
}

/** Accepted file types, for the browser's file picker. */
export const ACCEPT = [".pdf", ...Object.keys(IMAGE), ...Object.keys(OFFICE), ...TEXT].map((e) => (e.startsWith(".") ? e : "." + e));

// ---- text ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function decodeText(buf) {
  if (buf[0] === 0xff && buf[1] === 0xfe) return buf.subarray(2).toString("utf16le");
  if (buf[0] === 0xfe && buf[1] === 0xff) {
    const b = Buffer.from(buf.subarray(2));
    b.swap16();
    return b.toString("utf16le");
  }
  return buf.toString("utf8").replace(/^ï»¿/, "");
}

const ENT = { lt: "<", gt: ">", amp: "&", quot: '"', apos: "'", nbsp: " " };
const decodeXml = (s) =>
  s.replace(/&(#x[0-9a-f]+|#\d+|\w+);/gi, (m, e) =>
    e[0] === "#" ? String.fromCodePoint(e[1].toLowerCase() === "x" ? parseInt(e.slice(2), 16) : Number(e.slice(1))) : ENT[e] ?? m
  );
const stripTags = (s) => decodeXml(s.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ""));
const tidy = (s) => s.replace(/[ \t]+\n/g, "\n").replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n").trim();

// ---- zip ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const MAX_UNZIPPED = 60 * 1024 * 1024; // per entry, guards against zip bombs

/** Minimal ZIP reader: Map of entry name -> () => Buffer. */
export function unzip(buf) {
  let eocd = -1;
  for (let i = buf.length - 22; i >= Math.max(0, buf.length - 65557); i--) {
    if (buf.readUInt32LE(i) === 0x06054b50) {
      eocd = i;
      break;
    }
  }
  if (eocd < 0) throw new Error("not a valid Office file (damaged or password-protected?)");
  const count = buf.readUInt16LE(eocd + 10);
  let p = buf.readUInt32LE(eocd + 16);
  const entries = new Map();
  for (let n = 0; n < count && p + 46 <= buf.length; n++) {
    if (buf.readUInt32LE(p) !== 0x02014b50) break;
    const method = buf.readUInt16LE(p + 10);
    const compSize = buf.readUInt32LE(p + 20);
    const nameLen = buf.readUInt16LE(p + 28);
    const extraLen = buf.readUInt16LE(p + 30);
    const commentLen = buf.readUInt16LE(p + 32);
    const local = buf.readUInt32LE(p + 42);
    const name = buf.toString("utf8", p + 46, p + 46 + nameLen);
    entries.set(name, () => {
      const start = local + 30 + buf.readUInt16LE(local + 26) + buf.readUInt16LE(local + 28);
      const data = buf.subarray(start, start + compSize);
      if (method === 0) return data;
      if (method === 8) return inflateRawSync(data, { maxOutputLength: MAX_UNZIPPED });
      throw new Error(`unsupported compression in ${name}`);
    });
    p += 46 + nameLen + extraLen + commentLen;
  }
  return entries;
}

const read = (zip, name) => (zip.has(name) ? zip.get(name)().toString("utf8") : null);
const byNumber = (re) => (a, b) => Number(a.match(re)[1]) - Number(b.match(re)[1]);

function docxText(zip) {
  const xml = read(zip, "word/document.xml");
  if (xml == null) throw new Error("this .docx has no document body");
  return tidy(
    stripTags(
      xml
        .replace(/<w:tab\/>/g, "\t")
        .replace(/<w:br[^>]*\/>/g, "\n")
        .replace(/<\/w:tc>/g, "\t")
        .replace(/<\/w:tr>/g, "\n")
        .replace(/<\/w:p>/g, "\n")
    )
  );
}

function pptxText(zip) {
  const re = /^ppt\/slides\/slide(\d+)\.xml$/;
  const slides = [...zip.keys()].filter((k) => re.test(k)).sort(byNumber(re));
  if (!slides.length) throw new Error("this .pptx has no slides");
  return slides
    .map((s, i) => {
      const body = tidy(stripTags(read(zip, s).replace(/<a:br[^>]*\/>/g, "\n").replace(/<\/a:p>/g, "\n")));
      return `--- Slide ${i + 1} ---\n${body}`;
    })
    .join("\n\n");
}

const colIndex = (ref) => {
  const letters = (ref.match(/^[A-Z]+/) || ["A"])[0];
  let n = 0;
  for (const ch of letters) n = n * 26 + (ch.charCodeAt(0) - 64);
  return n - 1;
};

function xlsxText(zip, { maxRows = 3000, maxCols = 100 } = {}) {
  const shared = [];
  const ss = read(zip, "xl/sharedStrings.xml");
  if (ss) for (const si of ss.match(/<si>[\s\S]*?<\/si>/g) || []) shared.push(decodeXml((si.match(/<t[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/t>/g) || []).map((t) => t.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "")).join("")));
  // sheet names in workbook order, mapped to their files through the relationships
  const wb = read(zip, "xl/workbook.xml") || "";
  const rels = read(zip, "xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels") || "";
  const target = {};
  for (const m of rels.matchAll(/<Relationship\b[^>]*>/g)) {
    const id = /Id="([^"]+)"/.exec(m[0])?.[1];
    const t = /Target="([^"]+)"/.exec(m[0])?.[1];
    if (id && t) target[id] = t.startsWith("/") ? t.slice(1) : "xl/" + t.replace(/^\.\//, "");
  }
  let sheets = [...wb.matchAll(/<sheet\b[^>]*>/g)].map((m) => ({
    name: decodeXml(/name="([^"]*)"/.exec(m[0])?.[1] || "Sheet"),
    file: target[/r:id="([^"]+)"/.exec(m[0])?.[1]],
  }));
  if (!sheets.some((s) => s.file && zip.has(s.file))) {
    const re = /^xl\/worksheets\/sheet(\d+)\.xml$/;
    sheets = [...zip.keys()].filter((k) => re.test(k)).sort(byNumber(re)).map((f, i) => ({ name: `Sheet ${i + 1}`, file: f }));
  }
  const out = [];
  for (const s of sheets) {
    const xml = s.file && read(zip, s.file);
    if (!xml) continue;
    const rows = [];
    let cut = false;
    for (const row of xml.match(/<row\b[\s\S]*?<\/row>/g) || []) {
      if (rows.length >= maxRows) {
        cut = true;
        break;
      }
      const cells = [];
      for (const c of row.matchAll(/<c\b([^>]*?)(?:\/>|>([\s\S]*?)<\/c>)/g)) {
        const attrs = c[1];
        const inner = c[2] || "";
        const ref = /r="([A-Z]+)\d+"/.exec(attrs)?.[1];
        const i = ref ? colIndex(ref) : cells.length;
        if (i >= maxCols) continue;
        const type = /t="([^"]+)"/.exec(attrs)?.[1];
        const v = /<v>([\s\S]*?)<\/v>/.exec(inner)?.[1];
        let val = "";
        if (type === "s") val = shared[Number(v)] ?? "";
        else if (type === "inlineStr") val = stripTags((/<is>([\s\S]*?)<\/is>/.exec(inner) || [, ""])[1]);
        else if (v != null) val = decodeXml(v);
        cells[i] = val.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
      }
      if (cells.some((x) => x)) rows.push(Array.from(cells, (x) => x ?? "").join("\t"));
    }
    if (rows.length) out.push(`--- Sheet: ${s.name} ---\n${rows.join("\n")}${cut ? `\n[... more rows not included ...]` : ""}`);
  }
  if (!out.length) throw new Error("this workbook has no cells with values");
  return out.join("\n\n") + "\n\n(Dates may appear as Excel serial numbers.)";
}

/** Text of an Office file or a plain-text file. */
export function extractText(name, buf) {
  const e = ext(name);
  if (e === "docx") return docxText(unzip(buf));
  if (e === "pptx") return pptxText(unzip(buf));
  if (e === "xlsx") return xlsxText(unzip(buf));
  return tidy(decodeText(buf));
}



================================================
FILE: server/documents.mjs
================================================
// Documents added to an assistant conversation: stored locally, read by Gemini, asked about by the assistant.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { DATA_DIR } from "./config.mjs";
import { db, now } from "./db.mjs";
import { generateJSON, hasKey } from "./gemini.mjs";
import { classify, extractText } from "./doc-text.mjs";

export const DOCS_DIR = path.join(DATA_DIR, "documents");
fs.mkdirSync(DOCS_DIR, { recursive: true });

// Gemini takes at most ~20 MB per request including base64 overhead.
export const MAX_INLINE_BYTES = 14 * 1024 * 1024; // PDFs and images
export const MAX_FILE_BYTES = 30 * 1024 * 1024; // Office and text files (only their text is sent)
const MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 300_000; // ~75k tokens: keeps each question well inside the free-tier token limits

const httpError = (status, message) => Object.assign(new Error(message), { status });
const fileOf = (d) => path.join(DOCS_DIR, d.file);
const parse = (s) => {
  try {
    return s ? JSON.parse(s) : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
};

function toDoc(r) {
  if (!r) return null;
  return {
    id: r.id,
    conversationId: r.conversation_id,
    name: r.name,
    kind: r.kind,
    label: r.label,
    size: r.size,
    status: r.status, // analysing | ready | error
    error: r.error || null,
    truncated: !!r.truncated,
    analysis: parse(r.analysis),
    createdAt: r.created_at,
  };
}

export const getDocument = (id) => toDoc(db.prepare("SELECT * FROM documents WHERE id = ?").get(id));
export const listDocuments = (conversationId) =>
  db.prepare("SELECT * FROM documents WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY id").all(conversationId).map(toDoc);

/** Save an uploaded file, add a message for it to the conversation and start reading it. */
export function addDocument(conversationId, { name, body }) {
  const clean = String(name || "").replace(/[\\/]/g, "_").replace(/[\x00-\x1f]/g, "").trim().slice(0, 200);
  if (!clean) throw httpError(400, "The file needs a name.");
  if (!body?.length) throw httpError(400, "The file is empty.");
  const type = classify(clean);
  if (type.error) throw httpError(415, type.error);
  const inline = type.kind === "pdf" || type.kind === "image";
  const max = inline ? MAX_INLINE_BYTES : MAX_FILE_BYTES;
  if (body.length > max) throw httpError(413, `${clean} is ${(body.length / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB. The limit for this type is ${max / 1048576} MB.`);

  let text = null;
  let truncated = 0;
  if (!inline) {
    try {
      text = extractText(clean, body);
    } catch (e) {
      throw httpError(422, `Couldn't read ${clean}: ${e.message}.`);
    }
    if (!text.trim()) throw httpError(422, `${clean} has no text in it.`);
    if (text.length > MAX_TEXT_CHARS) {
      text = text.slice(0, MAX_TEXT_CHARS);
      truncated = 1;
    }
  }

  const t = now();
  const id = Number(
    db
      .prepare(
        `INSERT INTO documents(conversation_id, name, kind, label, mime, size, file, text, truncated, status, created_at)
         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, '', ?, ?, 'analysing', ?)`
      )
      .run(conversationId, clean, type.kind, type.label, type.mime, body.length, text, truncated, t).lastInsertRowid
  );
  const file = `${id}${path.extname(clean).toLowerCase() || ".bin"}`;
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(DOCS_DIR, file), body);
  db.prepare("UPDATE documents SET file = ? WHERE id = ?").run(file, id);

  // the attachment shows up in the conversation like a message
  const meta = { document: { id, name: clean } };
  const msgId = db
    .prepare("INSERT INTO messages(conversation_id, role, modality, text, meta, created_at) VALUES (?, 'user', 'document', ?, ?, ?)")
    .run(conversationId, `Added a document: ${clean}`, JSON.stringify(meta), t).lastInsertRowid;
  db.prepare("UPDATE conversations SET updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?").run(t, conversationId);

  queue(id);
  return {
    document: getDocument(id),
    message: { id: Number(msgId), role: "user", modality: "document", text: `Added a document: ${clean}`, createdAt: t, ...meta },
  };
}

/** What Gemini gets for a document: the file itself (PDF, image) or its text. */
function partsFor(row) {
  const header = { text: `Document ${row.id}: "${row.name}" (${row.label})${row.truncated ? " â€” only the first part of it, it was too long" : ""}` };
  if (row.kind === "pdf" || row.kind === "image") {
    return [header, { inlineData: { mimeType: row.mime, data: fs.readFileSync(fileOf(row)).toString("base64") } }];
  }
  return [header, { text: `<document id="${row.id}">\n${row.text}\n</document>` }];
}

// ---- first read: overview -----------------------------------------------------------------------

const ANALYSE_SYSTEM = `You read documents for a personal assistant and describe them briefly and accurately.
Use only what is in the document. Write in clear English (quote names and terms as written).
For an image, describe what it shows and transcribe any important text.`;

const ANALYSE_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    title: { type: "string", description: "The document's own title, or a short descriptive one" },
    doc_type: { type: "string", description: "What kind of document it is, e.g. 'rental agreement', 'invoice', 'lecture slides'" },
    overview: { type: "string", description: "2 to 4 sentences: what it is, who it is from or for, what it is about" },
    key_points: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, description: "Up to 6 of the most important facts, figures, dates or conclusions" },
    suggested_questions: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, description: "3 short questions the user might ask about this document" },
    pages: { type: "integer", description: "Number of pages or slides, if known" },
  },
  required: ["title", "doc_type", "overview", "key_points", "suggested_questions"],
};

const list = (a, n) => (Array.isArray(a) ? a.map((x) => String(x || "").trim()).filter(Boolean).slice(0, n) : []);

let chain = Promise.resolve();
function queue(id) {
  chain = chain.then(() => analyse(id)).catch(() => {});
  return chain;
}

async function analyse(id) {
  const row = db.prepare("SELECT * FROM documents WHERE id = ?").get(id);
  if (!row) return;
  try {
    if (!hasKey()) throw new Error("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set");
    const out = await generateJSON({
      system: ANALYSE_SYSTEM,
      parts: [...partsFor(row), { text: "Describe this document." }],
      schema: ANALYSE_SCHEMA,
    });
    const analysis = {
      title: String(out.title || "").trim() || row.name,
      docType: String(out.doc_type || "").trim() || null,
      overview: String(out.overview || "").trim(),
      keyPoints: list(out.key_points, 6),
      suggestedQuestions: list(out.suggested_questions, 3),
      pages: Number.isFinite(out.pages) && out.pages > 0 ? out.pages : null,
    };
    db.prepare("UPDATE documents SET status = 'ready', analysis = ?, error = NULL WHERE id = ?").run(JSON.stringify(analysis), id);
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`[documents] reading ${row.name} failed:`, e.message);
    db.prepare("UPDATE documents SET status = 'error', error = ? WHERE id = ?").run(String(e.message).slice(0, 300), id);
  }
}

/** The stored original, for downloading. */
export function documentFile(id) {
  const row = db.prepare("SELECT name, file FROM documents WHERE id = ?").get(id);
  if (!row?.file || !fs.existsSync(fileOf(row))) return null;
  return { name: row.name, path: fileOf(row) };
}

export function retryDocument(id) {
  const d = getDocument(id);
  if (!d) throw httpError(404, "Not found");
  db.prepare("UPDATE documents SET status = 'analysing', error = NULL WHERE id = ?").run(id);
  queue(id);
  return getDocument(id);
}

// ---- questions --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const ASK_SYSTEM = `You answer questions about the user's documents for a voice assistant.
Answer only from the documents provided. If the answer is not in them, say so plainly and set found to false; never guess or fill in from general knowledge.
Be concise and specific: give the actual figures, names, dates and wording. Mention the page, slide, sheet or section when you can.
Quote short exact passages in "quotes" to back the answer.`;

const ASK_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    answer: { type: "string" },
    found: { type: "boolean", description: "false when the documents don't contain the answer" },
    quotes: {
      type: "array",
      items: {
        type: "object",
        properties: { text: { type: "string" }, where: { type: "string", description: "page, slide, sheet or section, if known" } },
        required: ["text"],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ["answer", "found"],
};

/**
 * Answer a question about one document, or about all readable documents in the conversation.
 * Returns what the assistant needs to reply.
 */
export async function askDocuments(conversationId, { question, documentId } = {}) {
  const q = String(question || "").trim();
  if (!q) throw httpError(400, "question required");
  let rows = db.prepare("SELECT * FROM documents WHERE conversation_id = ? AND status != 'error' ORDER BY id").all(conversationId);
  if (documentId) rows = rows.filter((r) => r.id === Number(documentId));
  if (!rows.length) {
    return { found: false, answer: documentId ? `There is no readable document ${documentId} in this conversation.` : "No documents have been added to this conversation." };
  }
  const inlineBytes = rows.filter((r) => r.kind === "pdf" || r.kind === "image").reduce((n, r) => n + r.size, 0);
  if (inlineBytes > MAX_INLINE_BYTES) {
    return {
      found: false,
      answer: "These documents are too large to read together. Ask about one of them at a time (pass its document_id).",
      documents: rows.map((r) => ({ id: r.id, name: r.name })),
    };
  }
  const parts = rows.flatMap(partsFor);
  parts.push({ text: `Question: ${q}` });
  const out = await generateJSON({ system: ASK_SYSTEM, parts, schema: ASK_SCHEMA });
  const quotes = Array.isArray(out.quotes)
    ? out.quotes
        .map((x) => ({ text: String(x?.text || "").trim(), where: String(x?.where || "").trim() || undefined }))
        .filter((x) => x.text)
        .slice(0, 4)
    : [];
  return {
    documents: rows.map((r) => ({ id: r.id, name: r.name })),
    found: out.found !== false,
    answer: String(out.answer || "").trim(),
    quotes,
    ...(rows.some((r) => r.truncated) ? { note: "A document was too long and only its first part was read." } : {}),
  };
}

// ---- deleting -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const unlink = (file) => {
  if (!file) return;
  try {
    fs.unlinkSync(path.join(DOCS_DIR, file));
  } catch {}
};

export function deleteDocument(id) {
  const row = db.prepare("SELECT * FROM documents WHERE id = ?").get(id);
  if (!row) return false;
  db.prepare("DELETE FROM documents WHERE id = ?").run(id);
  unlink(row.file);
  return true;
}

/** Remove stored files whose document (or conversation) is gone. */
export function cleanUpFiles() {
  const keep = new Set(db.prepare("SELECT file FROM documents").all().map((r) => r.file));
  let n = 0;
  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(DOCS_DIR)) {
    if (!keep.has(f)) {
      unlink(f);
      n++;
    }
  }
  return n;
}

/** Documents interrupted by a restart are read again. */
export function resumeDocuments() {
  cleanUpFiles();
  for (const r of db.prepare("SELECT id FROM documents WHERE status = 'analysing' ORDER BY id").all()) queue(r.id);
}

/** For the assistant's instructions: the documents in this conversation. */
export function documentsForPrompt(conversationId) {
  return listDocuments(conversationId).map((d) => {
    const a = d.analysis;
    const what = a ? `${a.docType ? a.docType + ", " : ""}${a.overview}` : d.status === "error" ? `could not be read (${d.error})` : "still being read";
    return `- document_id ${d.id}: "${d.name}" (${d.label}) â€” ${what}`;
  });
}

// Server-side Gemini API access: ephemeral Live tokens, JSON generation, transcription.
import { GEMINI_API_KEY, TEXT_MODEL, TRANSCRIBE_MODEL } from "./config.mjs";
import { pcmToWav } from "./audio.mjs";

let sdk = null;
async function genai() {
  if (!sdk) sdk = await import("@google/genai");
  return sdk;
}

let ai = null;
async function client() {
  if (!GEMINI_API_KEY) {
    const err = new Error(
      "GEMINI_API_KEY is not set. Add it to the .env file in the project root and restart."
    );
    err.status = 503;
    throw err;
  }
  if (!ai) {
    const { GoogleGenAI } = await genai();
    ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: GEMINI_API_KEY });
  }
  return ai;
}

export const hasKey = () => Boolean(GEMINI_API_KEY);

// Running totals for generateJSON calls (read by the evaluation harness; the app ignores them).
export const usage = { calls: 0, promptTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, latencyMs: 0 };

/** Short-lived, single-use token the browser uses to open a Gemini Live session. */
export async function createLiveToken() {
  await client(); // throws a helpful error when the key is missing
  const { GoogleGenAI } = await genai();
  const c = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: GEMINI_API_KEY, httpOptions: { apiVersion: "v1alpha" } });
  const t = Date.now();
  const token = await c.authTokens.create({
    config: {
      uses: 1,
      // the session itself may last up to 3 hours, a new one must start within 2 minutes
      expireTime: new Date(t + 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
      newSessionExpireTime: new Date(t + 2 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
      httpOptions: { apiVersion: "v1alpha" },
    },
  });
  return { token: token.name, expiresAt: t + 2 * 60 * 1000 };
}

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

function isRetryable(e) {
  const s = e?.status ?? e?.code;
  return s === 429 || s === 500 || s === 503 || s === 504 || /fetch failed|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT/i.test(String(e?.message));
}

async function withRetry(fn, tries = 4) {
  let delay = 2000;
  for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i >= tries - 1 || !isRetryable(e)) throw e;
      // honour "retry in Xs" hints from 429 responses when present
      const m = /retry in ([\d.]+)s/i.exec(String(e?.message));
      await sleep(m ? Math.min(60000, Number(m[1]) * 1000 + 250) : delay);
      delay *= 2;
    }
  }
}

/** Generate JSON that follows `schema` (a JSON Schema object). */
export async function generateJSON({ system, prompt, schema, model = TEXT_MODEL, parts }) {
  const c = await client();
  const t0 = Date.now();
  const res = await withRetry(() =>
    c.models.generateContent({
      model,
      contents: [{ role: "user", parts: parts || [{ text: prompt }] }],
      config: {
        systemInstruction: system,
        responseMimeType: "application/json",
        responseJsonSchema: schema,
        temperature: 0.1,
      },
    })
  );
  const um = res.usageMetadata || {};
  usage.calls++;
  usage.promptTokens += um.promptTokenCount || 0;
  usage.outputTokens += um.candidatesTokenCount || 0;
  usage.latencyMs += Date.now() - t0;
  const text = res.text || "";
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    const m = text.match(/[[{][\s\S]*[\]}]/);
    if (m) return JSON.parse(m[0]);
    throw new Error("Model did not return valid JSON");
  }
}

/**
 * Transcribe several short PCM16 (16 kHz mono) clips in one request.
 * `context` is the most recent transcript (plain text) to help with names and terms.
 * Returns { texts, raw }: one string per clip, in order ("" when no intelligible speech).
 */
export async function transcribeSegments(pcmBuffers, { context = "", language = "" } = {}) {
  const n = pcmBuffers.length;
  const parts = [];
  if (context) {
    parts.push({ text: `Transcript so far (for context only, do not repeat it):\n${context}` });
  }
  pcmBuffers.forEach((pcm, i) => {
    parts.push({ text: `Clip ${i + 1} of ${n}:` });
    parts.push({ inlineData: { mimeType: "audio/wav", data: pcmToWav(pcm).toString("base64") } });
  });
  parts.push({
    text:
      `Transcribe each of the ${n} audio clips above, word for word. ` +
      `Return "transcripts" as an array of exactly ${n} strings: the first string is clip 1, the second is clip 2, and so on. ` +
      (language
        ? `The speakers mostly use: ${language}. `
        : `Write each clip in the language it is spoken in. `) +
      `If speakers mix languages (for example Hindi and English), keep the words as spoken; do not translate. ` +
      `Use normal punctuation. Leave out filler sounds like "um". ` +
      `Use an empty string only when a clip has no intelligible speech at all. ` +
      `Do not add speaker names, timestamps, descriptions or comments.`,
  });
  const out = await generateJSON({
    model: TRANSCRIBE_MODEL,
    system: "You are an accurate meeting transcriber. You only write down what is said in the audio.",
    parts,
    schema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {
        transcripts: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, minItems: n, maxItems: n },
      },
      required: ["transcripts"],
    },
  });
  const list = Array.isArray(out?.transcripts) ? out.transcripts : Array.isArray(out) ? out : [];
  const texts = new Array(n).fill("");
  for (let i = 0; i < n && i < list.length; i++) {
    const v = list[i];
    texts[i] = String(typeof v === "string" ? v : v?.text ?? "").trim();
  }
  return { texts, raw: out, count: list.length };
}

// ---- tiny router ---------------------------------------------------------------------
const routes = [];
const add = (method) => (pattern, ...handlers) => {
  const keys = [];
  const re = new RegExp("^" + pattern.replace(/:(\w+)/g, (_, k) => (keys.push(k), "([^/]+)")) + "/?$");
  routes.push({ method, re, keys, handler: handlers[handlers.length - 1], raw: handlers.length > 1 });
};
const app = { get: add("GET"), post: add("POST"), put: add("PUT"), patch: add("PATCH"), delete: add("DELETE") };
const raw = "raw"; // marker: handler wants the binary body

const MAX_BODY = 50 * 1024 * 1024;
function readBody(req) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const chunks = [];
    let size = 0;
    req.on("data", (c) => {
      size += c.length;
      if (size > MAX_BODY) {
        reject(Object.assign(new Error("Request too large"), { status: 413 }));
        req.destroy();
      } else chunks.push(c);
    });
    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks)));
    req.on("error", reject);
  });
}

function sendJSON(res, status, data) {
  const body = JSON.stringify(data ?? { ok: true });
  res.writeHead(status, { "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8", "Cache-Control": "no-store" });
  res.end(body);
}

// handler result -> JSON; thrown errors -> {error}
const h = (fn) => fn;
const id = (req, name = "id") => Number(req.params[name]);
const notFound = () => Object.assign(new Error("Not found"), { status: 404 });
const bad = (msg) => Object.assign(new Error(msg), { status: 400 });
function sendDownload(res, { mime, ext, body, title }) {
  const safe = String(title || "export").replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\- ]+/gu, "").trim().replace(/\s+/g, "_").slice(0, 80) || "export";
  res.writeHead(200, {
    "Content-Type": `${mime}; charset=utf-8`,
    "Content-Disposition": `attachment; filename="${safe.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g, "_")}.${ext}"; filename*=UTF-8''${encodeURIComponent(safe)}.${ext}`,
  });
  res.end(body);
}

Then read back the exact day and time it returns and ask the user to confirm. Only after a clear yes, call confirm_reminder with the reminderId; if they say no or want a different time, call cancel_reminder (and set_reminder again for a new time). Never say a reminder is set unless confirm_reminder succeeded. When it is due, AURA shows the reminder in the app and reads it aloud (the AURA tab must be open); it cannot call the user's phone.`
    : `\n\nYou cannot set reminders, alarms or timers in this app. If asked, say so plainly and do not promise to remind the user.`;

// ---- static production build (npm run build && npm run serve) -------------------------------------
const BUILD = path.join(ROOT_DIR, "build");
const MIME = { ".html": "text/html", ".js": "text/javascript", ".css": "text/css", ".json": "application/json", ".ico": "image/x-icon", ".png": "image/png", ".svg": "image/svg+xml", ".txt": "text/plain", ".map": "application/json" };
function serveStatic(req, res, pathname) {
  if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(BUILD, "index.html"))) return false;
  let file = path.normalize(path.join(BUILD, decodeURIComponent(pathname)));
  if (!file.startsWith(BUILD) || !fs.existsSync(file) || fs.statSync(file).isDirectory()) file = path.join(BUILD, "index.html");
  res.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": MIME[path.extname(file)] || "application/octet-stream" });
  fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res);
  return true;
}

// ---- server ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const server = http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
  const url = new URL(req.url, "http://localhost");
  req.query = Object.fromEntries(url.searchParams);
  try {
    if (!url.pathname.startsWith("/api/")) {
      if (req.method === "GET" && serveStatic(req, res, url.pathname)) return;
      throw notFound();
    }
    let route = null;
    for (const r of routes) {
      if (r.method !== req.method) continue;
      const m = r.re.exec(url.pathname);
      if (m) {
        route = r;
        req.params = Object.fromEntries(r.keys.map((k, i) => [k, decodeURIComponent(m[i + 1])]));
        break;
      }
    }
    if (!route) throw Object.assign(new Error("Unknown endpoint"), { status: 404 });
    const body = await readBody(req);
    if (route.raw) req.body = body;
    else if (body.length) {
      try {
        req.body = JSON.parse(body.toString("utf8"));
      } catch {
        throw bad("Invalid JSON body");
      }
    } else req.body = {};
    const out = await route.handler(req, res);
    if (!res.headersSent) sendJSON(res, 200, out);
  } catch (e) {
    if (!e.status || e.status >= 500) console.error(`[api] ${req.method} ${url.pathname}:`, e.message);
    if (!res.headersSent) sendJSON(res, e.status || 500, { error: e.message || "Server error" });
  }
});

export function start(port = PORT) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      console.log(`[aura] server on http://localhost:${port}  (data: ${DATA_DIR})`);
      if (!hasKey()) console.warn("[aura] GEMINI_API_KEY is missing - add it to .env (see README).");
      if (process.env.REACT_APP_GEMINI_API_KEY)
        console.warn("[aura] REACT_APP_GEMINI_API_KEY is set: rename it to GEMINI_API_KEY so the key is never bundled into the web app.");
      meet.resumePending();
      docs.resumeDocuments();
      proactive.startScheduler(); // only when an AURA_PROACTIVE_* switch is on
      if (process.env.AURA_NO_WARMUP !== "1") warmUp();
      resolve(server);
    });
  });
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href) {
  start();
}
export { server };

// What happens with a meeting after the transcript is written:
//   - minutes of meeting (on request)
//   - durable facts go to long-term memory (automatically, when enabled)
//   - lookup by date / topic for the assistant
import { db, now, getSettings } from "./db.mjs";
import { generateJSON, hasKey } from "./gemini.mjs";
import { getMeeting, meetingLines, parseMinutes, hooks } from "./meetings.mjs";
import { extractFromMeeting } from "./memory.mjs";

const clock = (ms) => {
  const s = Math.floor(ms / 1000);
  const h = Math.floor(s / 3600);
  const mm = String(Math.floor((s % 3600) / 60)).padStart(2, "0");
  const ss = String(s % 60).padStart(2, "0");
  return h ? `${h}:${mm}:${ss}` : `${mm}:${ss}`;
};

/** "Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 01:18" in the computer's time zone. */
export const longDate = (t) =>
  new Date(t).toLocaleString("en-GB", { weekday: "long", day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric", hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" });

const httpError = (status, message) => Object.assign(new Error(message), { status });

// ---- minutes ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const MINUTES_SYSTEM = `You write the minutes of a meeting from its transcript.
Write in clear, plain English, even when the transcript is in Hindi or a mix of languages.
Use only what was said. Never invent decisions, owners, numbers or dates.

Speaker names come from voice recognition and can be wrong; "Speaker N" is an unidentified person.
Name an owner for an action item only when it is clear from the transcript who will do it.
When a deadline is relative ("tomorrow", "next Friday"), turn it into a date using the meeting date.

For a short or casual conversation keep everything short, and leave lists empty when there is nothing for them.
summary: 2 to 5 sentences on what the meeting was about and how it ended.
suggested_title: 3 to 8 words naming the main topic, no date.`;

const MINUTES_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    suggested_title: { type: "string" },
    summary: { type: "string" },
    key_points: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
    decisions: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
    action_items: {
      type: "array",
      items: {
        type: "object",
        properties: { task: { type: "string" }, owner: { type: "string" }, due: { type: "string" } },
        required: ["task"],
      },
    },
    open_questions: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
  },
  required: ["summary", "key_points", "decisions", "action_items", "open_questions"],
};

const strList = (a) => (Array.isArray(a) ? a.map((x) => String(x || "").trim()).filter(Boolean) : []);
const DEFAULT_TITLE = /^Meeting \d/; // createMeeting's automatic "Meeting <date>" title

export async function writeMinutes(id) {
  const m = getMeeting(id);
  if (!m) throw httpError(404, "Not found");
  const lines = meetingLines(id);
  if (!lines.length) throw httpError(400, "This meeting has no transcript yet, so there is nothing to summarise.");
  const busy = m.segments.some((s) => ["pending", "queued", "analysing", "live"].includes(s.status));
  const transcript = lines.map((l) => `[${clock(l.startMs)}] ${l.speaker}: ${l.text}`).join("\n").slice(0, 120000);
  const prompt = [
    `Meeting: ${m.title}`,
    `Meeting date: ${longDate(m.startedAt)}`,
    `Participants (from voice recognition): ${m.speakers.filter((s) => s.segments > 0).map((s) => s.label).join(", ") || "unknown"}`,
    busy ? `Note: the last few lines may still be missing from the transcript.` : ``,
    ``,
    `Transcript:`,
    transcript,
  ].join("\n");
  const out = await generateJSON({ system: MINUTES_SYSTEM, prompt, schema: MINUTES_SCHEMA });
  const minutes = {
    summary: String(out.summary || "").trim(),
    keyPoints: strList(out.key_points),
    decisions: strList(out.decisions),
    actionItems: (Array.isArray(out.action_items) ? out.action_items : [])
      .map((a) => ({ task: String(a?.task || "").trim(), owner: String(a?.owner || "").trim() || null, due: String(a?.due || "").trim() || null }))
      .filter((a) => a.task),
    openQuestions: strList(out.open_questions),
    suggestedTitle: String(out.suggested_title || "").trim() || null,
    lines: lines.length, // how much transcript the minutes are based on
  };
  db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET minutes = ?, minutes_at = ? WHERE id = ?").run(JSON.stringify(minutes), now(), id);
  // an automatic title becomes something you can recognise in the list
  if (minutes.suggestedTitle && DEFAULT_TITLE.test(m.title)) {
    db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET title = ? WHERE id = ?").run(minutes.suggestedTitle.slice(0, 120), id);
  }
  return getMeeting(id);
}

export function deleteMinutes(id) {
  db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET minutes = NULL, minutes_at = NULL WHERE id = ?").run(id);
  return getMeeting(id);
}

// ---- memory -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let chain = Promise.resolve();

/** Learn durable facts from a meeting. Runs one meeting at a time. */
export function memorizeMeeting(id) {
  if (!getMeeting(id)) throw httpError(404, "Not found");
  if (!hasKey()) throw httpError(503, "GEMINI_API_KEY is not set.");
  db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET memory_status = 'running', memory_error = NULL WHERE id = ?").run(id);
  const job = chain.then(async () => {
    const m = getMeeting(id);
    if (!m) return;
    try {
      const applied = await extractFromMeeting({ meetingId: id, title: m.title, startedAt: m.startedAt, lines: meetingLines(id) });
      db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET memory_status = 'done', memory_count = ?, memory_error = NULL WHERE id = ?").run(applied.length, id);
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(`[memory] meeting ${id} failed:`, e.message);
      db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET memory_status = 'error', memory_error = ? WHERE id = ?").run(String(e.message).slice(0, 300), id);
    }
  });
  chain = job.catch(() => {});
  return job;
}

// a server restart interrupts a running extraction: let the user start it again
db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET memory_status = NULL WHERE memory_status = 'running'").run();

hooks.finished = (id) => {
  const s = getSettings();
  if (!hasKey()) return;
  if (s.autoMemory && s.meetingMemory) memorizeMeeting(id).catch(() => {});
  else db.prepare("UPDATE meetings SET memory_status = 'off' WHERE id = ? AND memory_status IS NULL").run(id);
};

// ---- lookup for the assistant -------------------------------------------------------------

const participants = (id) =>
  db
    .prepare("SELECT label FROM meeting_speakers WHERE meeting_id = ? AND merged_into IS NULL AND n > 0 ORDER BY n DESC")
    .all(id)
    .map((r) => r.label);

const durationMin = (id) => {
  const r = db.prepare("SELECT MAX(end_ms) AS d FROM segments WHERE meeting_id = ?").get(id);
  const d = r?.d || 0;
  return d > 0 ? Math.max(1, Math.round(d / 60000)) : 0;
};

/**
 * Meetings that started in [from, to] (ms epoch, both optional), optionally matching `q`
 * in the title, minutes or transcript. Newest first.
 */
export function findMeetings({ from, to, q, limit = 10 } = {}) {
  const where = [];
  const args = [];
  if (Number.isFinite(from)) where.push("m.started_at >= ?"), args.push(from);
  if (Number.isFinite(to)) where.push("m.started_at <= ?"), args.push(to);
  const base = `SELECT m.* FROM meetings m ${where.length ? "WHERE " + where.join(" AND ") : ""}`;
  let rows = [];
  let matchedQuery = false;
  const query = String(q || "").trim();
  if (query) {
    const words = query.split(/\s+/).filter((w) => w.length > 2).slice(0, 6);
    if (words.length) {
      const like = words.map(() => `(m.title LIKE ? OR m.minutes LIKE ? OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM segments s WHERE s.meeting_id = m.id AND s.text LIKE ?))`);
      const wargs = words.flatMap((w) => [`%${w}%`, `%${w}%`, `%${w}%`]);
      rows = db
        .prepare(`${base} ${where.length ? "AND" : "WHERE"} (${like.join(" OR ")}) ORDER BY m.started_at DESC LIMIT ?`)
        .all(...args, ...wargs, limit);
      matchedQuery = rows.length > 0;
    }
  }
  // no topic match: fall back to the date range alone (the topic may be phrased differently)
  if (!rows.length && (where.length || !query)) rows = db.prepare(`${base} ORDER BY m.started_at DESC LIMIT ?`).all(...args, limit);
  return {
    matchedQuery,
    meetings: rows.map((m) => {
      const mi = parseMinutes(m.minutes);
      const preview = mi
        ? null
        : (meetingLines(m.id) || [])
            .slice(0, 4)
            .map((l) => `${l.speaker}: ${l.text}`)
            .join("\n") || null;
      return {
        id: m.id,
        title: m.title,
        when: longDate(m.started_at),
        startedAt: new Date(m.started_at).toISOString(),
        durationMinutes: durationMin(m.id),
        participants: participants(m.id),
        summary: mi?.summary || null,
        preview,
      };
    }),
  };
}

/** Everything the assistant needs to answer questions about one meeting. */
export function meetingBrief(id, maxChars = 30000) {
  const m = getMeeting(id);
  if (!m) return null;
  const lines = meetingLines(id).map((l) => `[${clock(l.startMs)}] ${l.speaker}: ${l.text}`);
  let transcript = lines.join("\n");
  let truncated = false;
  if (transcript.length > maxChars) {
    // keep the start and the end; the minutes cover the whole meeting
    transcript = `${transcript.slice(0, maxChars * 0.6)}\n[... part of the transcript left out ...]\n${transcript.slice(-maxChars * 0.4)}`;
    truncated = true;
  }
  const memories = db
    .prepare("SELECT content FROM memories WHERE meeting_id = ? AND status = 'active' ORDER BY id")
    .all(id)
    .map((r) => r.content);
  return {
    id: m.id,
    title: m.title,
    when: longDate(m.startedAt),
    durationMinutes: durationMin(id),
    participants: participants(id),
    speakerNamesNote: "Names come from voice recognition and can be wrong; 'Speaker N' is an unidentified person.",
    minutes: m.minutes,
    memoriesFromThisMeeting: memories,
    transcript: transcript || "(no transcript)",
    transcriptTruncated: truncated,
  };
}



================================================
FILE: server/meetings.mjs
